topic_desc: The 12 gauge shotshell is among the most versatile ammunition types in the Mojave Wasteland, with more documented variants than any other round. The standard Purebore Buckslayer "Shure Shot" buckshot load is the most common, while hand loaders can produce magnum loads with higher powder charges for increased velocity and stopping power at the cost of accelerated weapon wear. Slug variants trade spread for range and accuracy, functioning effectively against armored targets. Several specialized loads reflect the ingenuity—and desperation—of wasteland munitions craft. Coin shotshells, loaded with Legion denarii instead of conventional pellets, draw on old western folklore about filling shotguns with coins; they match magnum buckshot in damage and carry elevated trade value. Beanbag rounds serve a less-than-lethal role historically associated with riot control, inflicting fatigue rather than outright trauma, though their reliability in the field is questionable. The Gun Runners' Arsenal expanded the lineup considerably, introducing 4/0 buckshot loads with fewer but larger projectiles, flechette shells packed with tiny metal darts for superior armor penetration and reduced muzzle flash, pulse slugs with electromagnetic payloads effective against robots and power armor, and dragon's breath shells using zirconium-based pyrotechnic compounds to function as short-range incendiary devices. NCR Heavy Troopers, Centurions, Prime Legionaries, and Great Khans are known to carry 12 gauge rounds, and merchants across the Mojave stock them regularly.
topic_desc_basic: The 12 gauge round is a large bore shotshell widely used throughout the Mojave Wasteland. The standard Purebore Buckslayer "Shure Shot" buckshot load is most common, but numerous variants exist, including magnum loads, slugs, beanbag rounds, and improvised coin shot loaded with Legion denarii. Specialized varieties such as flechette, pulse slugs, and dragon's breath incendiary shells have also appeared. These rounds can be hand-loaded at reloading benches and are carried by NCR troopers, Legionaries, and Great Khans alike.
tags: 12 gauge shotshell,beanbag riot round,coin shot variant,gun runners arsenal,mojave wasteland ammo,shotgun ammunition

topic_desc: The reloading bench is a sturdy work surface fitted with presses, dies, and hand tools used to disassemble, convert, and hand-load metallic cartridges. It works only with conventional firearm ammunition—energy weapon cells require a workbench instead. Cartridges are broken down into recoverable components: lead, powder, primers, and casings or hulls. Because different cartridge families do not share casings, conversions are not one-to-one; a shooter might break down surplus 5mm rounds to supply lead and powder for .308 hand-loads. Lead can also be smelted from scrap metal. Reloading benches are common across the Mojave and surrounding territories, found in settlements such as Goodsprings, Novac, Primm, Jacobstown, the 188 Trading Post, and Freeside's Cerulean Robotics. More secure facilities—Brotherhood and NCR safehouses, the Gun Runners' factory, Ranger Station Foxtrot, Nellis Hangars—house them as well. Scavengers in Zion Canyon and the Sierra Madre Villa also maintained or constructed benches. The practice reflects a deeply rooted wasteland tradition: factory ammunition is scarce, and anyone with components, patience, and skill can keep a firearm fed indefinitely.
topic_desc_basic: A reloading bench is a workbench used to hand-load, convert, and break down conventional firearm ammunition. Shooters disassemble unwanted cartridges to recover lead, powder, primers, and casings, then reassemble them into more useful rounds. Lead can also be extracted from scrap metal. Reloading benches are found across the Mojave in settlements, camps, safehouses, and trading posts. They cannot process energy weapon ammunition; a standard workbench is needed for that.
tags: ammunition crafting station,cartridge breakdown,hand loading equipment,mojave workbench,scrap lead recovery,wasteland reloading tools

topic_desc: The electron charge pack is a specialized high-capacity energy ammunition container designed to feed rapid-fire directed energy weapons, most notably the Gatling laser and Tesla cannon. Its relative scarcity in the Capital Wasteland reflects both the complexity of its manufacture and the limited number of weapons chambered for it. Packs are most commonly recovered from sentry bots equipped with Gatling lasers, as well as from personnel of the Brotherhood of Steel, the Outcasts, and the Enclave who field such weapons. A handful of fixed caches exist across the wasteland, including Evergreen Mills Foundry, the Mechanist's Forge, SatCom Array NN-03d, Rivet City's Flak 'N Shrapnel's, and Old Olney Underground. Merchants such as Chief Gustavo at Tenpenny Tower and Lucky Harith occasionally stock quantities. Super mutant overlords wielding Gatling lasers also serve as an uncommon source. The pack's rarity at lower experience levels underscores the difficulty of maintaining advanced energy weapon systems in the post-war environment.
topic_desc_basic: The electron charge pack is a type of energy ammunition used primarily by heavy directed-energy weapons such as the Gatling laser and Tesla cannon. It is among the rarer ammunition types found in the Capital Wasteland. Packs are occasionally recovered from sentry bots, Enclave and Brotherhood personnel, and select merchants. A few fixed caches are known to exist in locations such as Evergreen Mills, the Mechanist's Forge, and SatCom Array NN-03d.

topic_desc: The .44 Magnum cartridge represents one of the most powerful handgun rounds still circulating in the Capital Wasteland. Pre-war manufacturers designed it for high-pressure performance, giving it substantially more stopping power than common pistol calibers such as 10mm or .32. In the post-war era, the round's scarcity reflects both the limited number of weapons chambered for it and the high demand among those who possess such firearms. Weapons utilizing .44 Magnum ammunition include the Scoped .44 Magnum revolver, the prized Lincoln's Repeater, and the Blackhawk. Traders across the Capital Wasteland occasionally stock the round in quantity, with arms dealers at Tenpenny Tower, Rivet City, and Evergreen Mills being among the more reliable sources. The round's expense makes it impractical for routine use, and most wastelanders reserve it for situations demanding maximum firepower from a sidearm or lever-action rifle.
topic_desc_basic: The .44 Magnum round is a heavy pistol-caliber cartridge found in the Capital Wasteland. It is among the most expensive pistol ammunition available, and relatively few weapons chamber it. Notable firearms using this round include the Scoped .44 Magnum, Lincoln's Repeater, and the Blackhawk. Despite its cost, it is prized for its stopping power.

topic_desc: Ant queen pheromones are a specialized chem extracted from the corpses of giant ant queens found throughout the Capital Wasteland. The substance exhibits pronounced aphrodisiac properties, reportedly enhancing a user's personal charisma and social presence while simultaneously impairing cognitive function and sensory awareness. Three giant ant queens are known to inhabit the region: one within the tunnels of Marigold Station, one near the Shalebridge ant colony, and one in the vicinity of the Corvega Factory. The pheromones can also be obtained commercially from Cindy Cantelli, a chem dealer operating A Quick Fix in the Rivet City Market. The chem has garnered attention among certain Rivet City residents for its intended romantic applications, reflecting the persistent demand for social and interpersonal aids in post-war communities despite the associated mental degradation.
topic_desc_basic: Ant queen pheromones are a chem harvested from giant ant queen corpses in the Capital Wasteland. The substance functions as an aphrodisiac, boosting charisma while dulling intelligence and perception. Specimens have been recovered from queens in Marigold Station, Shalebridge, and near the Corvega Factory. Cindy Cantelli at Rivet City's A Quick Fix is known to stock a supply. Some wastelanders seek the pheromones for their seductive properties.

topic_desc: Fancy Lads Snack Cakes are among the many pre-war food products that survived the nuclear holocaust in edible, if slightly irradiated, condition. Their durable packaging and preservative-heavy formula allowed them to endure for over two centuries, and they remain a staple trade good throughout the Mojave Wasteland. Most food merchants stock them, and they serve as a modest supplement to a wastelander's diet, offering limited nourishment alongside minor radiation exposure. The cakes have permeated post-war culture in small ways. Members of the Kings, the Freeside gang that models itself on pre-war rock-and-roll nostalgia, have been known to voice a humorous fondness for them. Veronica, a scribe of the Brotherhood of Steel, once jokingly named a lifetime supply of Fancy Lad Snack Cakes as her greatest wish—ahead of the destruction of her enemies and world peace. Such remarks suggest the cakes hold a place in the collective memory of the wasteland as a symbol of simpler pre-war life.
topic_desc_basic: Fancy Lads Snack Cakes are a pre-packaged confection surviving from before the Great War. These individually wrapped cakes remain widely available across the Mojave Wasteland, sold by most food vendors. Their long shelf life and familiar packaging make them a recognizable comfort food, though like most preserved pre-war foodstuffs they carry trace radiation.

topic_desc: Pressure cookers were common household appliances in pre-war American kitchens, valued for rapidly cooking tough cuts of meat and preserving nutrients under sealed steam pressure. Following the Great War, surviving units became scattered salvage across the Mojave Wasteland, turning up in settlements like Goodsprings, Novac, and Westside, as well as in abandoned shacks, mine camps, and military installations such as Camp McCarran and Camp Golf. Their durable construction ensured many remained functional over two centuries. While most wasteland residents view them simply as cookware, their sealed, pressurized design has made them valuable components for fabrication projects requiring airtight containers. Notably, the Boomers at Nellis Air Force Base sought pressure cookers as part of efforts to construct underwater breathing apparatus, and the NCR military has shown interest in obtaining them for maintaining field food-processing equipment. Their presence in the Ultra-Luxe kitchen and the Lucky 38 Presidential Suite reflects the enduring association of these devices with civilized domestic life.
topic_desc_basic: A pressure cooker is a pre-war kitchen appliance designed to cook food rapidly under trapped steam pressure. Durable examples survive throughout the Mojave Wasteland, found in homes, general stores, military camps, and abandoned shacks from Goodsprings to the New Vegas Strip. Though originally mundane cookware, the sealed pressurized container has proven useful for wasteland fabrication and repair work beyond simple cooking.

topic_desc: Within the abandoned research installations of the Big MT, a set of thirteen holotapes survives, each containing detailed printing and binding instructions for a specific educational text. These recipes correspond to well-known wasteland skill books ranging from Nikola Tesla and You to the Wasteland Survival Guide. The recipes specify that twenty-five blank books and two tubes of wonderglue, combined at a workbench, yield one finished volume. Because each recipe is consumed in the process, the number of books that can be produced is strictly finite. The existence of these recipes suggests that someone at the Big MT anticipated the need to preserve and reproduce practical knowledge long after institutional collapse, encoding assembly procedures for texts covering barter, medicine, science, repair, and combat disciplines alike.
topic_desc_basic: Skill book recipes are holotapes recovered from the Big MT research facility. Each contains instructions for assembling a specific educational text at a workbench, requiring twenty-five blank books and two tubes of wonderglue. Thirteen recipes exist in total, each corresponding to a different field of practical knowledge. The holotape is consumed during use, making each recipe a one-time resource.

topic_desc: The auto-inject stimpak represents a notable evolution in field medical technology, pairing the restorative compounds of a standard stimpak with an automated vital-signs monitoring system. This integration allows the device to administer treatment without conscious action from the injured party, a critical advantage in combat or other situations where manual application is impractical. These units are encountered primarily in the Divide, the devastated corridor between the Mojave Wasteland and regions farther west, typically cached in lead-lined metal boxes that appear designed to preserve emergency supplies against the Divide's harsh conditions. The existence of a more potent variant, the auto-inject super stimpak, suggests the auto-inject framework is adaptable to stronger formulations. Notably, the monitoring system does not trigger in response to environmental damage such as that caused by the Sierra Madre cloud, indicating it is calibrated to detect physical trauma rather than chemical or atmospheric hazards. Unlike standard stimpaks, these modified versions carry measurable weight, likely owing to the additional monitoring and injection mechanisms housed within the casing.
topic_desc_basic: The auto-inject stimpak is a modified stimpak fitted with a vital-signs monitoring system that automatically administers emergency treatment when the user's condition deteriorates to a critical threshold. These devices are primarily found in the Divide, often stored in lead-lined metal boxes. Unlike standard stimpaks, they carry noticeable weight and do not activate in response to environmental hazards such as the Sierra Madre cloud. A more potent variant, the auto-inject super stimpak, also exists.

topic_desc: Irradiated Sunset Sarsaparilla is simply a standard bottle of the popular Mojave soft drink that has been left in a sufficiently radioactive environment long enough to absorb significant contamination. The beverage itself remains recognizable as Sunset Sarsaparilla, but consuming it introduces a meaningful dose of radiation into the body alongside whatever refreshment it provides. Bottles in this condition tend to turn up in locations with elevated background radiation, such as the Searchlight Fire Station kitchen, where several were left upstairs alongside other contaminated foodstuffs. Additional bottles have been recovered from the refrigerator at Hell's Motel near the Mescale Mountains Crater and from the X-13 Research Facility, suggesting that pre-war and post-war stockpiles in irradiated zones are the primary source. The phenomenon illustrates how common consumer goods can become hazardous simply through prolonged exposure rather than any manufacturing defect.
topic_desc_basic: Irradiated Sunset Sarsaparilla is an ordinary bottle of Sunset Sarsaparilla that has absorbed significant radiation from prolonged exposure to a highly irradiated environment. The drink remains recognizable but carries a harmful dose of radiation. Such bottles are typically found in areas with elevated background radiation, including the Searchlight Fire Station, Hell's Motel at the Mescale Mountains Crater, and the X-13 Research Facility.

topic_desc: Cloud Kiss is a venom derived from the toxic Cloud that permeates the Sierra Madre and its surrounding villa. The Cloud itself is a corrosive, poisonous phenomenon unique to the Sierra Madre region, and its properties can be harnessed by mixing concentrated Cloud residue with common household cleaning products. The result is a synthetic poison that damages health over time, with three tiers of potency: weak, potent, and lethal. The lethal variety is the most virulent, delivering rapid health degradation over an extended duration compared to its weaker counterparts. Like all venoms, a dose of Cloud Kiss can be applied to melee weapons, unarmed implements, or thrown projectiles, coating the striking surface so that a successful hit delivers the toxin into the target's system. Each dose is consumed upon a single successful strike or hit from a thrown weapon. The crafting of Cloud Kiss represents one of the few practical applications of the Sierra Madre Cloud, turning an environmental hazard into a deliberate tool of harm. Knowledge of its preparation is uncommon outside those who have spent time in the Sierra Madre villa.
topic_desc_basic: Cloud Kiss is a deadly venom crafted from the corrosive Cloud of the Sierra Madre combined with common household cleaning products. It comes in weak, potent, and lethal varieties, with the lethal form dealing the most rapid and longest-lasting health damage. Like all venoms, it can be applied to melee, unarmed, or thrown weapons to envenom a target on a successful hit. A single dose lasts for one successful strike.

topic_desc: Lead has been known to humanity for thousands of years, prized for its density, malleability, and resistance to corrosion. Classified as element eighty-two on the periodic table, it was used extensively in pre-war construction, batteries, radiation shielding, and plumbing systems. Ancient alchemists regarded lead as a base metal and sought to transmute it into gold through philosophical and chemical processes, though no such transformation was ever achieved. In the post-war Mojave, lead retains practical value primarily as a component in hand-loaded ammunition. Reloaders and craftsmen collect lead scraps to cast bullets for various calibers, making it a staple trade good among independent gunsmiths, caravaners, and survivalists who cannot rely on factory-produced cartridges. Its availability directly affects the feasibility of sustained firearm use across the wasteland.
topic_desc_basic: Lead is a heavy, soft metal known since antiquity, identified as element number eighty-two on the periodic table. In the Mojave Wasteland, lead is valued as a crafting component for producing conventional ammunition. Wasteland smiths and reloaders seek out scraps of lead to hand-load bullets and cartridges. Ancient alchemists reportedly attempted to transmute lead into gold, a pursuit that never succeeded.

topic_desc: Giant rats inhabit the Mojave Wasteland, displaying behaviors somewhere between defensive and passive depending on location. In Freeside, certain giant rats are entirely non-hostile, and local children have been observed chasing one particular specimen through the streets. When threatened at close range, they attack in groups of three to seven. A unique anatomical feature is their tail, which can be severed; crippling it causes the animal to frenzy, attacking all nearby targets indiscriminately. Giant rat meat has no known culinary or crafting use. The trader Lady Jane has referenced "Rodents of Unusual Size" inhabiting Broc Flower Cave, where her caravan was raided. These creatures are comparable in size to mole rats and are recognized by their light brown coloring, glowing blue eyes, and the white stripe of hair along their backs. Idle giant rats occasionally produce a sound resembling a howl.
topic_desc_basic: Giant rats are creatures found throughout the Mojave Wasteland. They are light brown with distinctive glowing blue eyes and white hair running down their backs. Roughly the size of a mole rat, they are notably fast and tend to attack in groups. Generally defensive rather than aggressive, they stand their ground when threatened and only attack if approached closely. Some populations, such as those in Freeside, are notably docile.

topic_desc: The dart gun schematics provide detailed instructions for fabricating a weapon that delivers radscorpion venom via dart projectiles. The design calls for four key components: a toy car mechanism, surgical tubing, a paint gun, and a radscorpion poison gland. The toy car provides the firing assembly, surgical tubing serves as the propulsion band, the paint gun forms the barrel, and the poison gland supplies the toxic payload. Multiple copies of the schematics circulate across the Capital Wasteland. Hannibal Hamlin is known to possess a copy. Boutique Le Chic in Tenpenny Tower stocks another. A third set rests beside a deceased engineer at the MDPL-05 Power Station. The schematics reflect the ingenuity of wasteland engineers who repurpose pre-war consumer goods and biological materials into functional weaponry. The dart gun's silent operation and venom-based delivery make it particularly effective against living targets, though its construction requires scavenging across multiple locations, as no single site typically contains all necessary components.
topic_desc_basic: The dart gun schematics are hand-drawn plans detailing how to construct a dart gun, a small arms weapon that fires poisoned darts. The schematics specify the necessary components and assembly process using a workbench. Copies of these schematics can be found at various locations throughout the Capital Wasteland, including Tenpenny Tower's Boutique Le Chic and the MDPL-05 Power Station.

topic_desc: Thick Red Paste is a restorative substance developed or stored within the Big MT research complex, specifically recoverable from the X-13 testing facility and from the remains of Patient Zero at the X-22 Botanical Garden. When consumed, it not only mends injuries but also temporarily augments the body's overall vitality beyond its normal limits, suggesting a biochemical formulation more sophisticated than typical wasteland stimulants. The paste can be manufactured with the proper components, implying that the underlying recipe has circulated beyond its original pre-war custodians. Despite its medicinal value, Caesar's Legion classifies Thick Red Paste as a banned substance; Legionaries at The Fort confiscate it from anyone entering their territory, reflecting the Legion's broader suspicion of chemical aids and foreign medical products that might undermine discipline or reliance on natural remedies. Its association with Big MT's experimental facilities raises questions about whether it was originally intended for human use or as part of a broader biomedical testing program.
topic_desc_basic: Thick Red Paste is a medicinal consumable that heals injuries and temporarily increases the body's maximum vitality. It can be crafted from raw components and has been found in Big MT facilities such as the X-13 testing facility and the X-22 Botanical Garden. Caesar's Legion considers it a banned substance and confiscates it from travelers entering The Fort.

topic_desc: Party Time Mentats are a modified variant of standard Mentats, formulated with additional ingredients that produce a more pronounced boost to the user's personality and charisma. Unlike regular Mentats, which offer sustained cognitive enhancement over an extended period, Party Time Mentats deliver a brief but potent surge lasting roughly one minute. This makes them less suited for prolonged analytical work and more appropriate for short, high-stakes social encounters where charm and persuasiveness are paramount. The chem's effects can be stacked with standard Mentats and with other charisma-enhancing substances such as alcohol, allowing users to significantly bolster their bartering and conversational aptitude in a pinch. Despite being addictive, no overt negative physiological symptoms are recorded on standard Pip-Boy medical readouts. Party Time Mentats are known to circulate in limited quantities around the Mojave Wasteland, with production rumored at the Red Rock Drug Lab, where a chemist named Jack may manufacture them if provided the proper recipe. A solitary dose has also been recovered in the Puesta del Sol area, secured behind a hard-locked gate along a service route.
topic_desc_basic: Party Time Mentats are a modified form of Mentats that provide a stronger boost to the user's personality and charisma than the standard version. Their effects are brief, lasting only about one minute. They can be stacked with regular Mentats and other charisma-enhancing substances such as alcohol. Though addictive, no negative status effects appear on standard Pip-Boy medical readouts. They are occasionally sold at the Red Rock Drug Lab and have been found in the Puesta del Sol area.

topic_desc: The Rock-It Launcher schematics represent a practical example of Capital Wasteland ingenuity, documenting how to convert pre-war household appliances into a functional projectile weapon. The design repurposes a leaf blower's motor as a propulsion system, a vacuum cleaner for housing, and a firehose nozzle as a barrel, illustrating how scavengers transform mundane domestic technology into improvised armaments. Multiple copies of the schematics circulate throughout the Capital Wasteland. Moira Brown at Craterside Supply in Megaton is a known seller, and copies have been recovered from Rivet City's secured armory behind the bridge tower's reinforced door. The traveling merchant Crazy Wolfgang has been known to carry a copy as well. A fourth set was reportedly discovered within a framed quote in the Vault 101 clinic. Horace Pinkerton's quarters in the Rivet City bow are noted for containing components useful for multiple crafted weapon designs. The schematics demonstrate the broader wasteland practice of fabricating weapons from salvage, a necessity in a region where functioning pre-war firearms are scarce and ammunition is precious.
topic_desc_basic: The Rock-It Launcher schematics are detailed blueprints enabling construction of a custom-built projectile weapon that fires scavenged debris. Copies circulate in the Capital Wasteland, including at Craterside Supply in Megaton, Rivet City's armory, and among traveling merchants. Assembly requires a workbench and common salvage components including a vacuum cleaner, leaf blower, firehose nozzle, and conductor.

topic_desc: The auto-inject super stimpak represents a convergence of battlefield trauma medicine and automated biometric monitoring technology. Standard super stimpaks already deliver a potent concentrated healing compound far beyond that of an ordinary stimpak, but they traditionally require manual administration—a limitation that can prove fatal when a user is incapacitated or unable to reach their supplies during critical injury. The auto-inject variant incorporates a vital-signs monitoring system that continuously assesses the user's physical condition and triggers injection automatically once health falls below approximately a quarter of maximum tolerance. This makes it especially valuable for individuals operating alone in hostile territory where no companion or medic can intervene. Curiously, the auto-inject variant appears to have resolved one of the super stimpak's most notorious side effects: the temporary reduction in agility and strength commonly called stimpak sickness. Whether this is achieved through reformulated compounds or improved delivery mechanisms is not widely documented. The device does carry measurable weight, unlike standard stimpaks, suggesting additional hardware for the monitoring and injection apparatus. It can be assembled by those with sufficient medical expertise and access to appropriate components, and is considered a variant within the broader auto-inject family of emergency medical supplies.
topic_desc_basic: The auto-inject super stimpak is a modified super stimpak fitted with a vital-signs monitoring system. When the user's condition deteriorates to critical levels, the device automatically administers emergency treatment from their inventory. Unlike a standard super stimpak, it does not cause the agility and strength impairment known as stimpak sickness, though it does carry measurable weight unlike its lighter counterpart.

topic_desc: The Weapon Binding Ritual is a tribal adaptation of the pre-war stimulant known as Psycho, modified by the tribes of Zion Canyon to suit their combat traditions. Performed shortly before battle, the ritual serves both practical and spiritual purposes — numbing pain inflicted on limbs, sharpening the warrior's mind, and steeling their fighting spirit for close-quarters combat. Unlike its pre-war counterpart, the ritual is non-addictive and carries only minor physical drawbacks, making it remarkably efficient for its intended purpose. The preparation restores limb condition similarly to medical supplies such as doctor's bags and hydra, while simultaneously boosting the user's effectiveness in melee and unarmed combat. The White Legs tribe is known to carry and use this ritual preparation, reflecting their aggressive raiding culture. Joshua Graham, the former Malpais Legate turned missionary in Zion, also provides the preparation to those he aids in the canyon. The ritual exemplifies how tribal societies in the post-war world have adapted pre-war pharmacological knowledge into culturally meaningful practices, blending practical combat enhancement with ceremonial significance tied to their warrior traditions.
topic_desc_basic: The Weapon Binding Ritual is a tribal preparation used by certain tribes in Zion Canyon before battle. It numbs pain in the limbs, sharpens the mind, and strengthens fighting spirit, making warriors more deadly in hand-to-hand combat. It restores limb condition and enhances melee and unarmed prowess. The White Legs tribe is known to carry it, and Joshua Graham provides it to those he aids in Zion.

topic_desc: Holy Water is produced by Mother Curie III, leader of the Church of the Apostles of the Eternal Light, a small sect operating in the Capital Wasteland that splintered from the Children of Atom. The Apostles share the Children of Atom's reverence for radiation but diverge in theology: where the Children of Atom seek Division—the splitting of their atoms—the Apostles seek the Glow, believing that gradual irradiation and eventual ghoulification represent humanity's next step toward perfection. To spread this blessing, the Church steals Aqua Pura, the purified water distributed from Project Purity, and deliberately contaminates it with heavy doses of radiation, rebranding it as Holy Water. This act effectively neutralizes any Modified FEV that may have been introduced into the water supply, as radiation destroys the virus. The sect distributes Holy Water to the poor and thirsty of the wasteland, framing irradiation as a sacred gift rather than a danger. Members such as Brother Gerard and Sister Rosa actively hand out bottles to wastelanders and beggars near Megaton and the Brotherhood of Steel's distribution points.
topic_desc_basic: Holy Water is irradiated Aqua Pura produced by Mother Curie III of the Church of the Apostles of the Eternal Light, an offshoot of the Children of Atom. They believe irradiation and ghoulification are humanity's path to perfection and distribute Holy Water to spread Atom's Glow among the unenlightened of the Capital Wasteland.

The crafting of Cloud Kiss suggests practical knowledge of the Sierra Madre's environmental hazards and an understanding of how caustic household chemicals can amplify the Cloud's natural toxicity.
topic_desc_basic: Cloud Kiss is a poisonous venom crafted from the corrosive Cloud of the Sierra Madre combined with common household cleaning products. topic_desc: Ant nectar is a chem naturally secreted by giant ants, the mutated insects that inhabit numerous nests throughout the Capital Wasteland. The substance directly enhances muscular output, granting a measurable increase in physical strength to those who consume it. However, this benefit comes at a cost: the nectar simultaneously dulls both intelligence and social aptitude, suggesting it interacts with the nervous system in ways not fully understood by wasteland scholars. Colonies of giant ants produce the substance within their nests, and it has been recovered from sites including the AntAgonizer's Lair, the Corvega Factory, Marigold Station, and Shalebridge. A distinct variant, fire ant nectar, is produced by fire ants, while ant queens yield pheromones with altogether different properties. Though the risk of addiction from ant nectar is generally low with moderate use, repeated and excessive consumption dramatically increases the likelihood of dependency. Wastelanders who rely on it for its strength-enhancing effects should exercise caution, as the accompanying cognitive and social impairments can prove dangerous in hostile territory.
topic_desc_basic: Ant nectar is a substance naturally produced by giant ants. When consumed, it bolsters physical strength but dulls both mental sharpness and social grace. Excessive consumption carries a risk of addiction, though the likelihood is generally low with moderate use.

topic_desc: Radscorpion poison glands are plump, smooth organs extracted from the tails of slain radscorpions, differing noticeably from the shriveled, desiccated glands found on specimens in the Capital Wasteland. In the Mojave, these glands serve as a key ingredient in several crafted remedies and poisons, including antivenom, Silver Sting, Tremble, and Hydra. Their high value-to-weight ratio makes them prized by scavengers and caravaners alike. Radscorpions can be encountered throughout the Mojave, though they are less common in urban areas; notable populations exist near Goodsprings Cemetery, around the Mojave Outpost, and in the irradiated ruins of Camp Searchlight. A related variant, the bark scorpion poison gland, is harvested from the smaller bark scorpion. Some wasteland cooks, such as Ruby Nash in Primm, are known to use the glands in regional recipes like radscorpion casserole.
topic_desc_basic: A radscorpion poison gland is an organ harvested from the tail of a dead radscorpion. These glands are valued across the Mojave Wasteland for their use in crafting antivenom and other remedies at campfires. They are relatively light and fetch a respectable price from traders, making them a dependable source of caps for hunters willing to risk a scorpion's pincers.

topic_desc: Ultrajet is a specialized stimulant developed by a Ghoul named Murphy operating out of Northwest Seneca Station in the Capital Wasteland. Standard Jet, the widespread chem derived from brahmin dung fumes, has little to no effect on Ghouls due to their altered physiology. Murphy solved this problem by combining Jet with Sugar Bombs—a preserved pre-war breakfast cereal—and two additional ingredients, producing a compound with roughly double the potency of ordinary Jet. The resulting drug sharply increases the user's reflexes and stamina for a limited duration. Ultrajet is chemically distinct enough from regular Jet that the two substances do not share addictive cross-dependencies; one will neither relieve nor trigger addiction to the other. Murphy's operation is small-scale and supply-constrained, requiring steady deliveries of Sugar Bombs to maintain production. This makes Ultrajet a rare commodity in the Capital Wasteland, primarily circulated among Ghoul communities who seek a Jet alternative.
topic_desc_basic: Ultrajet is a potent chem created by a Ghoul named Murphy at Northwest Seneca Station in the Capital Wasteland. Ghouls are barely affected by normal Jet, so Murphy combined Jet with Sugar Bombs and other ingredients to produce a drug with double Jet's potency. Ultrajet sharply boosts reflexes and stamina for several minutes. It is chemically distinct from Jet, and the two drugs do not share addictive cross-effects.

topic_desc: The .44 Magnum is a high-powered pistol cartridge derived from the older .44 Special round, sharing all dimensions except case length. The .44 Special is similar enough to be chambered in weapons designed for the .44 Magnum, though it produces lower pressures. Several variants exist in the wasteland. Hollow Point rounds break on impact, sacrificing penetrating power for expanded wound channels. Semi-wadcutter hand-loaded variants feature a flat-nosed bullet effective against armored targets, superior to standard ball ammunition. Junk rounds fabricated from refuse materials are of shoddy quality, dealing reduced damage and accelerating weapon wear. Standard and semi-wadcutter rounds can be hand-loaded at reloading benches. The .44 Magnum sees service among NCR Rangers and Caesar's Legion legionaries alike, and is chambered in weapons such as the .44 Magnum Revolver, the Trail Carbine, and similar longarms. The Great Khan Armory and Nellis Array generator room are known to stock supplies of this ammunition.
topic_desc_basic: The .44 Magnum round is a high-powered pistol cartridge derived from the .44 Special pistol round. It is used in revolvers and carbines throughout the Mojave Wasteland. NCR Rangers and Caesar's Legion legionaries both carry these rounds. Variants include hollow point, semi-wadcutter hand loads, .44 Special, and junk rounds made from refuse materials. Standard and hand-loaded variants can be crafted at reloading benches.

topic_desc: Mississippi Quantum Pie represents one of the more eccentric culinary achievements of the Capital Wasteland, born from the obsession of Sierra Petrovita, a Nuka-Cola enthusiast residing in the small settlement of Girdershade. The recipe calls for three ingredients: flour, a bottle of Nuka-Cola Quantum, and vodka. Nuka-Cola Quantum itself is a rare pre-war beverage distinguished by its characteristic isotope-induced luminescence, making the pie as visually striking as it is potent. The combination produces a noticeable strengthening effect alongside the intoxicating qualities of vodka, though it reportedly dulls the consumer's mental sharpness slightly. Notably, the pie avoids the addictive risk associated with Nuka-Cola Quantum consumption alone. The economics of the pie are peculiar: the combined value of its ingredients exceeds fifty caps, yet a finished pie fetches only about twenty caps, making it a labor of passion rather than profit. Flour's scarcity in the Capital Wasteland further limits production. Sierra shares the recipe only with those who have assisted her research efforts, keeping the knowledge within a small circle.
topic_desc_basic: Mississippi Quantum Pie is a rare wasteland delicacy created by Sierra Petrovita in Girdershade. It combines Nuka-Cola Quantum, vodka, and flour into a pie. The concoction carries the energizing properties of Nuka-Cola Quantum alongside the intoxicating effects of vodka. Flour is scarce in the Capital Wasteland, making this pie difficult to produce. Each pie is valued at roughly twenty caps, far less than the combined worth of its ingredients.
tags: capital wasteland food,girdershade delicacy,nuka-cola quantum,sierra petrovita recipe,vodka flour pie

topic_desc: Steady is a combat chem prized by snipers and sharpshooters across the Mojave Wasteland for its near-total elimination of weapon sway, granting the user an exceptionally steady aim ideal for lining up long-distance shots. Its manufacture is decidedly improvised: each dose is assembled using an empty Sunset Sarsaparilla bottle as the body, fitted with a tinfoil heating element and a hose mouthpiece, reflecting the resourceful nature of post-war chem production. Despite its effectiveness, Steady is untested and notoriously addictive, carrying perhaps the highest addiction rate of any known chem in circulation. This dangerous profile makes it a double-edged tool—capable of transforming a marginal shot into a near-certain hit, but at considerable risk of chemical dependency. Steady can be obtained through various channels in the Mojave, including Gomorrah's Lower Brimstone bar, Vault 3, the Red Rock Drug Lab operated by the Great Khans, and Crimson Caravan Company trade posts. Bulk quantities are also available through Sierra Madre vending machines, and caches have been reported near Hopeville Missile Base. Its prevalence in Fiend-occupied Vault 3 suggests significant production or stockpiling by raider chem operations.
topic_desc_basic: Steady is a potent combat chem that grants the user an exceptionally steady aim, making it highly valued by snipers and sharpshooters. It is administered through a makeshift inhaler crafted from an empty Sunset Sarsaparilla bottle fitted with a tinfoil heating element and a hose mouthpiece. Due to its untested nature and potency, Steady is extremely addictive, carrying one of the highest addiction rates of any chem in circulation across the Mojave Wasteland.

topic_desc: Microfusion cells exist in several variants tailored to different combat needs. Bulk cells trade reduced damage output for lower cost and reduced weapon wear, making them economical for routine engagements. Over charge and max charge variants increase damage significantly and penetrate armor more effectively, but accelerate weapon degradation considerably. Optimized cells, produced through advanced recycling techniques, offer superior performance across nearly all metrics with minimal drawbacks. Spent cells can often be recovered as drained casings and recycled at workbenches, making them a renewable resource for those with sufficient scientific knowledge. Cells can also be converted between energy ammunition types—electron charge packs and energy cells—providing flexibility in field supply chains. Significant stockpiles have been documented at REPCONN Headquarters, the Magnetohydraulics Complex, and within Vault 22's reactor room. Quartermaster Bardon at Hoover Dam and the Great Khan Armorer maintain large inventories for bulk purchase. The Van Graffs at the Silver Rush are known to sell substantial quantities. Securitrons utilize a specialized robot variant, reflecting their role as New Vegas's automated security force. When carried in large numbers, the cumulative weight becomes a serious logistical concern for travelers and supply caravans alike.
topic_desc_basic: Microfusion cells are a standard type of energy ammunition, more powerful than energy cells but less capable of rapid discharge than electron charge packs. They serve as the power source for a wide variety of energy weapons, including plasma and laser rifles. Spent cells can sometimes be recovered and recycled at workbenches. They are among the most versatile ammunition types in the wasteland, compatible with numerous weapon platforms.
tags: energy weapon ammunition,microfusion cell variants,mojave wasteland supplies,recycled ammunition,securitron power source,workbench recycling

topic_desc: Nuka-Cola Victory is a bright red-orange variant of the classic Nuka-Cola product, distinguished by its vivid coloration and distinctive flavor profile. It was produced as a limited regional release by the Nuka-Cola Corporation prior to the Great War, alongside the similarly scarce Nuka-Cola Quartz, rather than receiving the nationwide distribution enjoyed by standard Nuka-Cola or the promotional Nuka-Cola Quantum. In the Mojave Wasteland, Victory is exceptionally rare — second only to Quantum among known Nuka-Cola variants — and no merchants stock it for regular sale. Only a handful of bottles survive in the world, scattered across specific locations rather than cached in containers. Additional specimens have been recovered in the Big MT research facility. Victory is prized not only as a collectible but also as a key ingredient in the preparation of Atomic Cocktails, a favored beverage in establishments such as the Atomic Wrangler in Freeside. Its scarcity and vibrant appearance make it a sought-after curio among Nuka-Cola enthusiasts and collectors traversing the post-war Mojave.
topic_desc_basic: Nuka-Cola Victory is a bright red-orange variant of the Nuka-Cola soft drink, produced as a limited regional release before the Great War. It is one of the rarest Nuka-Cola variants found in the Mojave Wasteland, with only a small number of bottles known to survive. Victory is not sold by merchants and is prized both as a collectible and as an ingredient in Atomic Cocktails. Its vivid color and scarcity make it a notable curio among wasteland travelers.

topic_desc: Across the Mojave, safe drinking water remains a persistent concern. Most natural water sources retain radioactive contamination from the Great War, making untreated water a common but hazardous staple. Dirty water is distinguishable from purified water by its grimy bottle and the crude label "WATER," contrasted with purified water's "H²O" designation. Despite the radiation risk, dirty water sees wide circulation among raiders, Fiends, Powder Gangers, Jackals, and Vipers, as well as among Legionaries and traveling merchants. It can also be found in first aid boxes and scattered around shelters such as Raul's shack. Those lacking access to clean water or trade goods must either tolerate the radiation sickness that follows consumption or seek treatment from a doctor or use RadAway. With the proper knowledge and a campfire, dirty water can be purified in bulk, reflecting the resourcefulness demanded by desert life.
topic_desc_basic: Dirty water is the most common water found throughout the Mojave Wasteland, drawn directly from tainted lakes and rivers. Unlike purified water, drinking it induces moderate radiation exposure. It is sold by merchants such as Lupe at the Grub n' Gulp rest stop and Blake at the Crimson Caravan Company, and is often carried by wasteland thugs and Legionaries. It can be purified in bulk at a campfire.
tags: common wasteland item,crimson caravan goods,grub n gulp rest stop,mojave wasteland water,radiation contaminated drink,water purification campfire

topic_desc: Fire ant nectar is a substance harvested from the mutated fire ants that infested the Grayditch area following the experiments of a scientist who had been manipulating ant colonies with a modified strain of FEV. The nectar is closely related to ordinary ant nectar but carries distinct properties tied to the fire ants' unique biology, particularly their ability to generate and project flame. The compound appears to interact with the human nervous system in complex ways, sharpening reflexes and motor coordination while simultaneously dulling higher cognitive function, a tradeoff that some wastelanders find acceptable in environments where heat hazards are present. The substance is most reliably recovered from fire ant corpses around Grayditch and from the queen ant's hatchery within Marigold Station, though smaller quantities occasionally turn up in ant refuse piles alongside conventional ant nectar. Repeated use carries a well-documented risk of chemical dependency, with habitual users reporting escalating cravings and withdrawal symptoms. The exact biochemical mechanism by which the nectar confers resistance to thermal injury remains poorly understood, though Followers researchers have speculated that it may temporarily alter cellular heat-shock protein expression in the consumer.
topic_desc_basic: Fire ant nectar is a chem derived from the mutated fire ants found around Grayditch and Marigold Station in the Capital Wasteland. It is related to ordinary ant nectar but carries properties tied to the fire ants' flame-producing biology. Consumption reportedly sharpens reflexes and grants some resistance to heat, while dulling mental faculties. Repeated use can lead to chemical addiction. It is most commonly recovered from fire ant corpses and ant refuse piles.
tags: ant derived chem,capital wasteland medicine,fire ant nectar,fire resistance chem,grayditch ants,marigold station

topic_desc: Potato Crisps are a surviving pre-packaged snack product of the Spring Valley brand, recognizable by their small red and white packaging. A yellow promotional bubble on the box urges purchasers to 'See Moon Map Offer on Back!' though no such offer actually exists—the rear of the box is merely a duplicate of the front, suggesting either a manufacturing error or a cost-cutting measure in the final production runs before the Great War. In the Mojave Wasteland, these snacks are most frequently recovered from Eat'o'tronic 3000 vending units installed in homes and other residential spaces, with scarcer quantities turning up in assorted buildings across the region. They are functionally near-identical to generic junk food in packaging and nutritional value, offering only marginal restorative benefit while introducing trace radiation. Wasteland survival guides note that while such packaged snacks can help stave off starvation, their salt content contributes to dehydration—a meaningful concern for travelers in the arid Mojave climate. Some wastelanders with basic survival training have been known to prepare similar crisps from available ingredients.
topic_desc_basic: Potato Crisps are a pre-packaged Spring Valley-brand snack found throughout the Mojave Wasteland, most commonly inside Eat'o'tronic 3000 vending units in homes and other living spaces. They come in a small red and white box bearing a yellow label promising a 'Moon Map Offer on Back,' though no such offer exists. They provide modest nourishment but carry trace radiation, and their salt content can worsen dehydration in desert conditions.

topic_desc: Yao guai meat is derived from the yao guai, heavily mutated bears whose population is concentrated in regions east and north of the Mojave. In the Zion Canyon region, yao guai are sufficiently numerous that their meat is a practical staple for travelers and tribal groups operating there. By contrast, the Mojave Wasteland proper hosts no native yao guai population, making the meat an exotic and uncommon commodity. Its presence in the Legate's War Tent at the Legate's Camp suggests either trade routes extending into territories where yao guai roam, or provisioning through Caesar's Legion's far-reaching supply lines. The meat's notable restorative properties come paired with an elevated radiation burden, reflecting the heavy environmental contamination typical of the creatures' habitats. Merchants in the Mojave have been known to stock yao guai meat when trade connections to regions such as Zion are active, indicating that commercial networks can bridge the gap between ecologically distinct wasteland zones.
topic_desc_basic: Yao guai meat is food harvested from yao guai, large mutated bears. It is more nourishing than common wasteland meats such as mole rat, brahmin, or dog meat, but carries a proportionally higher burden of residual radiation. Yao guai are not native to the Mojave Wasteland, making the meat rare there, though it is plentiful in regions where the creatures roam, such as Zion Canyon.

topic_desc: Campfires are a common sight across the Mojave Wasteland, typically found at makeshift campsites surrounded by benches, bedding, and scattered cooking utensils such as pots and pans. They serve as essential survival tools, allowing wastelanders to cook raw meats and prepare a wide variety of medicines, chems, and poisons using gathered ingredients. Some recipes require prior knowledge of a specific recipe before they can be prepared. Campfires may be found lit or unlit, but both function identically. They appear at numerous locations throughout the Mojave, including rest stops, caves, and abandoned buildings. Notable concentrations exist at sites such as the Sunstone Tower roof, the Third Street Municipal Building, and the Water Treatment Plant. Additional campfires have been documented at the Junction 7 Rest Stop campsite within a collapsed highway tunnel, the Crow's Nest, and various points around Hopeville and Ashton in the Divide. These fire pits represent one of the most accessible and widely distributed crafting resources available to travelers in the region.
topic_desc_basic: Campfires are scattered throughout the Mojave Wasteland, usually found at makeshift campsites surrounded by benches, bedding, and cooking utensils like pots and pans. They serve as cooking and crafting stations where raw meats can be cooked and a variety of medicines, chems, and poisons can be prepared. Campfires may appear lit or unlit but function the same either way.

topic_desc: Missiles are self-propelled explosive ordnance dating to pre-war military arsenals, designed for use with shoulder-fired launcher systems. In the Capital Wasteland, they are among the rarer forms of heavy ammunition, typically recovered from combatants who themselves carry missile launchers—super mutants, Talon Company mercenaries, raiders, and armed wastelanders. Scavengers have catalogued notable caches at the National Guard Depot armory, Franklin Metro Utility, Farragut West Station, and the Washington Monument grounds. Destroyed sentry bots frequently yield one or two missiles among their internal stores. Merchants such as Flak 'N Shrapnel's in Rivet City and the traveling caravaner Lucky Harith maintain limited inventories, though supply seldom meets demand. Fort Independence and the Mobile Base Crawler at Adams Air Force Base also preserve stocks. The scarcity reflects both the specialized nature of the weapon platform and the attrition of pre-war military supplies over two centuries of post-nuclear conflict.
topic_desc_basic: Missiles are self-propelled explosive projectiles designed for use with missile launchers. These heavy ordnance rounds are scarce in the Capital Wasteland, rarely found outside merchant inventories or recovered from enemies who carry missile launchers themselves. Super mutants, Talon Company mercenaries, raiders, and some wastelanders occasionally possess them. Caches have been documented at locations including the National Guard Depot, Franklin Metro Utility, and the Washington Monument.

topic_desc: Wine production through grape juice fermentation has survived into the post-war era, with bottles circulating throughout the Mojave Wasteland. The casinos of the New Vegas Strip maintain notable stocks, particularly the Ultra-Luxe, whose kitchen holds a very large cache of wine bottles. The Tops Presidential Suite also stocks wine alongside other alcoholic beverages, and the Lucky 38 Cocktail Lounge contains numerous bottles. Wine can additionally be found at the King's School of Impersonation in Freeside, an Abandoned Warehouse, and behind the bar at the Mojave Outpost Barracks. The White Glove Society, operators of the Ultra-Luxe, maintain wine as part of their refined dining atmosphere. Bottles are occasionally found in the possession of Fiends. In earlier supply lines, wine was used in crafting Atomic Cocktails, though this practice appears to have fallen out of favor. Historical labeling sometimes referred to wine as "Banquet Wine."
topic_desc_basic: Wine is an alcoholic beverage produced through the fermentation of grape juice. It remains available in the Mojave Wasteland, particularly around New Vegas. Bottles can be purchased from bartenders at Strip casinos and found in various locations such as the Ultra-Luxe kitchen, the Tops Presidential Suite, and the Mojave Outpost Barracks. Wine is sometimes carried by Fiends.

topic_desc: Mirelurk cakes are prepared from mirelurk meat, though the resulting dish is notably less nutritious than the raw meat itself, providing only a fraction of the restorative benefit while carrying a slightly higher radiation content. Despite this, they remain a recognizable wasteland food, circulating among diner merchants across the Capital Wasteland. Gary Staley, proprietor of Gary's Galley in Rivet City's market, claims the cakes as his personal specialty. A recipe for the cakes exists, hidden among the supplies left at Anchorage Memorial. The memorial, a pre-war monument now overrun by mirelurks, contains a stash belonging to someone named Ted, which includes the recipe alongside other provisions. The stash is secured behind a locked storage room requiring a specific door component to access, with a key and a holotape providing directions to the hidden cache in one of the refrigerators beneath the kitchen area. The large number of mirelurk cakes stored in the memorial's refrigerators suggests the recipe was in active use there at some point before the mirelurk infestation made the location hazardous.
topic_desc_basic: Mirelurk cakes are a food item made from mirelurk meat. They are known as the specialty of Gary Staley, owner of the Rivet City Market diner called Gary's Galley. The cakes can be found among diner merchants throughout the Capital Wasteland. A notable cache of them is stored in the refrigerators at Anchorage Memorial.

topic_desc: Thin red paste is a curious medicinal consumable associated with the Big Empty's experimental remnants. It appears as a reddish, paste-like substance that, when consumed, not only mends injuries but also briefly enhances the body's overall vitality beyond its normal limits. The paste serves as a precursor component in the preparation of the more potent thick red paste, suggesting a deliberate refinement process known to those familiar with Old World biomedical science. Caesar's Legion considers thin red paste a banned substance, and Legionaries at the Fort will confiscate it from travelers crossing the river, likely viewing its stimulant-like properties as contrary to Legion discipline or medicinal doctrine. Several units have been recovered from the X-13 Research Facility, found near prototype stealth-suit boot components, hinting at a connection between the facility's research programs and the paste's development. Its origins may tie to pre-war biomedical experimentation conducted across the Big MT complex, though the exact nature of its ingredients remains poorly documented among wasteland scholars.
topic_desc_basic: Thin red paste is a reddish consumable substance with mild healing properties. When eaten, it restores health and temporarily boosts the body's maximum vitality. It can be refined into the more potent thick red paste. Caesar's Legion treats it as a banned item and confiscates it from anyone entering the Fort. Some quantities have been recovered from the X-13 Research Facility in the Big Empty.

topic_desc: Salient Green represents a breakthrough in agricultural science developed within the Big Mountain research facility. The substance is created through the Biological Research Station located in the Sink, which breaks down plant material into a universal, easily convertible nutrient source. Any variety of common wasteland flora can be processed into Salient Green, after which the substance can be reconstituted into any desired plant type using basic heating equipment. The process effectively allows complete interconversion between plant species, making it an extraordinarily versatile tool for food production and agricultural management. The substance's trade value far exceeds that of raw plant material, reflecting its refined and concentrated nature. Supplies of Salient Green have been found in locations throughout the Big Empty, including the X-13 stealth testing lab, and some units are carried by robotic custodial units. The name itself evokes comparisons to pre-war synthetic food movements, suggesting the scientists of Big Mountain sought to solve nutritional scarcity through universal nutrient processing.
topic_desc_basic: Salient Green is a universal nutrient substance housed in jars, containing plant material broken down into its base components. It is produced at the Biological Research Station in the Sink, which processes plant matter into this versatile green substance. Once created, Salient Green can be reconstituted into various plant types. It serves as an easily convertible nutrient source, making it valuable for trade and sustenance.

topic_desc: The steam gauge assembly is a pre-war industrial instrument designed to measure and monitor steam pressure in mechanical systems. It consists of a roughly two-foot-long metal pipe fitted with several smaller auxiliary pipes and an attached gauge meter, suggesting it was once part of a larger pressure-regulation apparatus. These assemblies can still be found scattered across the Mojave Wasteland in locations that once housed heavy machinery or industrial infrastructure, including Camp McCarran's terminal building, the Cerulean Robotics facility in Freeside, train tunnels, Michael Angelo's workshop, Techatticup Mine, the Ultra-Luxe, Vault 11, and the Securitron De-Construction Plant. At Camp McCarran, NCR personnel have found practical use for the assembly as a replacement component in the terminal building's food processor, which relies on steam-driven mechanisms. The scarcity of intact replacement parts in the post-war Mojave means that functional pressure-measuring instruments retain value among engineers and maintenance personnel attempting to keep aging pre-war machinery operational.
topic_desc_basic: A steam gauge assembly is a pre-war industrial instrument used to measure steam pressure. It appears as a two-foot-long metal pipe fitted with smaller pipes and a gauge meter. These devices can be found in various locations across the Mojave Wasteland, including Camp McCarran, Freeside's Cerulean Robotics, train tunnels, and several other industrial sites. They remain useful to anyone attempting to repair aging steam-driven machinery.

topic_desc: The Deathclaw Gauntlet schematics represent a pinnacle of improvised wasteland engineering, combining pre-war medical hardware with biological components harvested from the Capital Wasteland's most feared predator. The design calls for a Medical Brace to provide structural reinforcement, Wonderglue as a binding agent, a Leather Belt for strap mounting, and a Deathclaw Hand as the primary striking surface. Copies of these schematics have surfaced in several locations across the Capital Wasteland. One set is known to be stored in a trailer at the F. Scott Key Trail & Campground, an area frequented by Deathclaws. Another was offered as compensation for political services rendered in Rivet City's Council Seat dispute, specifically in favor of Bannon. A third copy has reportedly been carried by an unfortunate wastelander killed during a Deathclaw encounter in the open wastes. The gauntlet itself is prized among unarmed combatants for its ability to inflict grievous wounds that ignore conventional armor protection, making it especially effective against heavily defended targets.
topic_desc_basic: Schematics for the Deathclaw Gauntlet detail how to construct a fearsome unarmed weapon from a Deathclaw Hand, Medical Brace, Wonderglue, and Leather Belt at a workbench. Copies of these schematics have been recovered from locations across the Capital Wasteland, including the F. Scott Key Trail & Campground and Rivet City. The resulting gauntlet is prized by wastelanders who favor close-quarters combat.
tags: capital wasteland weapon,deathclaw gauntlet schematics,deathclaw hand component,improvised weapon design,medical brace component,unarmed combat weapon,workbench crafting

topic_desc: In the Capital Wasteland, where nearly all surface water is irradiated, purified water represents a scarce and valuable commodity. Water completely free of radiation can be safely consumed without harming the drinker and provides notably greater restorative benefits than dirty water. Bottles are occasionally found in caches and stockpiles across the region, including the National Guard Depot armory, Enclave camps southwest of Vault 92, the Museum of Technology west wing, and drainage chambers such as Signal Oscar Tango. Certain residences equipped with robotic attendants — such as those in Megaton or Tenpenny Tower — can dispense limited quantities, up to five bottles per week. The scarcity of clean water is a defining hardship of wasteland life. Beggars near Megaton, Rivet City, and Tenpenny Tower are known to plead for water from passersby. Purified water is distinct from other regional variants including dirty water, Aqua Pura, Aqua Cura, and Holy Water. Notably, Aqua Pura — despite appearing clean — can prove fatal to water beggars, underscoring the importance of distinguishing genuine purified water from imitations. Each bottle bears the chemical formula "H2O" handwritten on its label.
topic_desc_basic: Purified water is water completely free of radiation, making it safe to drink without any harmful effects. It is relatively rare in the Capital Wasteland and heals far more effectively than dirty water. Bottles of purified water can occasionally be found as loot in various locations across the wastes. Some residences with robotic attendants can dispense limited supplies on a regular basis.
tags: capital wasteland,clean water,purified water,radiation-free drink,scarce commodity,water beggars

topic_desc: Workbenches are utility stations scattered across the Mojave Wasteland and beyond, serving as the primary surface for fabricating homemade weapons, explosives, health items, and Weapon Repair Kits. They also allow the recycling of expended flame and energy ammunition into fresh rounds, and the conversion of one type of energy ammunition into another. Workbenches are typically found in workshops, garages, military bases, and commercial facilities — including Gun Runners' warehouse, the Hidden Valley Bunker workshop, Nellis Air Force Base, Crimson Caravan Company, and REPCONN Test Site. They are distinct from Reloading Benches, which focus on ammunition assembly, and Campfires, which serve Survival-based crafting. Some items require no schematics, relying instead on the crafter's Repair or Survival skill. Notably, certain companions can function as mobile workbench equivalents.
topic_desc_basic: A workbench is a utility station found throughout the Mojave Wasteland, used for crafting homemade weapons, explosives, health items, and Weapon Repair Kits. It also enables recycling of expended energy and flame ammunition into fresh rounds, and conversion between energy ammunition types. Workbenches are distinct from Reloading Benches and Campfires, each offering different crafting options. They are commonly found in workshops, garages, military bases, and trading posts.
tags: ammunition recycling,crafting station,homemade weapons,mojave wasteland,repair kits,utility object

topic_desc: Rocket is a chem variant derived from Jet, produced by combining processed Jet with common household detergent. The detergent's chemical additives alter the stimulant's interaction with the nervous system, producing a more intense but shorter-lived effect than standard Jet. When inhaled, Rocket floods the user's system with a burst of heightened reflexive capacity, increasing both immediate and peak physical response for roughly one minute. The compound's effects are cumulative with Jet, Ultrajet, and Dixon's Jet, making it popular among those who rely on rapid bursts of exertion. However, the addition of detergent compounds significantly increases the risk of chemical dependency. Rocket can be crafted with basic knowledge of chem preparation and access to detergent boxes commonly found in pre-War settlement kitchens throughout the Mojave Wasteland, including Goodsprings, Nipton, and Nelson. The Great Khans' Red Rock Drug Lab is known to produce and sell Rocket, provided their chemists are taught the recipe. Its short duration and stacking properties make it distinct from other Jet variants, though repeated rapid use dramatically increases addiction risk.
topic_desc_basic: Rocket is a variant of the chem Jet, crafted by combining Jet with household detergent. When used, it provides a powerful but short-lived stimulant effect, enhancing physical reflexes and stamina for about one minute. Its effects stack with Jet and other similar chems. Rocket carries a significant risk of addiction with each use. It can be crafted by those with basic chem-making knowledge and is sometimes sold at the Red Rock Drug Lab.
tags: addiction risk,crafted stimulant,detergent additive,jet variant chem,mojave chem,red rock drug lab

topic_desc: Turpentine is a pre-war solvent distilled from pine resin, valued in the Capital Wasteland for its flammability and chemical properties. Its primary known use among wasteland crafters is as an ingredient in improvised incendiary devices, particularly Nuka-Grenades, where its volatile nature complements other combustible components. Bottles of turpentine can be recovered from a wide range of surviving industrial and commercial sites across the wasteland, including Franklin Metro Utility, L.O.B. Enterprises, Adams Air Force Base, Red Racer Factory, Takoma Industrial, Mama Dolce's, and Vault 106, as well as smaller caches in abandoned grocers, supply closets, and utility tunnels. The concentration of stockpiles in pre-war manufacturing and storage facilities reflects its once-commonplace role in maintenance, painting, and cleaning applications throughout the Washington D.C. metropolitan area. Scavengers and traders familiar with improvised chemistry consider turpentine a useful find, though its flammability demands careful handling during transport.
topic_desc_basic: Turpentine is a flammable liquid distilled from pine resin, historically used as a solvent for paint and cleaning. In the Capital Wasteland, intact bottles are occasionally recovered from abandoned industrial sites, supply closets, and old grocery stores. Its combustible properties make it valued by scavengers and crafters familiar with improvised chemistry, particularly as a component in homemade incendiary devices.
tags: flammable solvent,improvised incendiary ingredient,pine resin distillate,pre-war chemical,scavenged industrial supply

topic_desc: The doctor's bag represents one of the most comprehensive field medical kits available in the Mojave Wasteland, designed to address traumatic injuries beyond the capabilities of standard stimpacks. Its primary function is treating crippled limbs, a critical concern for travelers facing the hazards of raider territory, wildlife, and unexploded ordnance. The bag contains surgical instruments, splints, bandages, and pharmaceutical supplies sufficient for multiple applications. Skilled practitioners can apply its contents to a single limb for concentrated treatment, or distribute them across all limbs for broader but less potent care. The bags are manufactured or assembled by various sources: Legion supply caches contain significant quantities, suggesting systematic production within Caesar's forces. Wasteland doctors such as Doc Mitchell in Goodsprings keep them on hand for patient treatment. The bags can also be crafted by those with sufficient medical knowledge and access to appropriate components. In Hardcore Mode survival conditions, where limb damage persists without intervention, the doctor's bag becomes essential alongside professional medical services, Hydra, or rest in an owned bed. Their presence in Legion dropboxes, trading posts, vault clinics, and even Sierra Madre vending machines indicates widespread recognition of their value across diverse communities.
topic_desc_basic: A doctor's bag is a portable medical kit used to treat crippled limbs. It contains surgical tools, bandages, and supplies sufficient for either treating all limbs partially or one limb extensively. Doctor's bags are carried by physicians like Doc Mitchell and found in clinics, Legion supply caches, and trading posts across the Mojave Wasteland. They can also be crafted by those with proper medical training and materials.
tags: craftable medical supplies,crippled limb treatment,doc mitchell goodsprings,hardcore mode medicine,legion supply caches,portable medical kit

topic_desc: BlamCo Mac & Cheese is a surviving pre-war convenience food produced by the BlamCo corporation, a company whose branding emphasized quick preparation and family-friendly marketing. The distinctive packaging bears both the company logo and an image of the prepared macaroni and cheese dish inside. Like many preserved pre-war foodstuffs scattered across the Mojave Wasteland, the product remains technically edible more than two centuries after the Great War, though it carries residual radiation from prolonged environmental exposure. Its enduring presence in supply chains and kitchen stores across the region speaks to the sheer volume of pre-war food production and the durability of commercial packaging. BlamCo Mac & Cheese retains culinary value beyond simple sustenance; it serves as a recognized ingredient in more elaborate wasteland dishes such as brahmin Wellington and the Wasteland Omelet, prized by cooks who combine scavenged pre-war goods with local ingredients. Merchants such as Michelle at the 188 Trading Post and Corporal William Farber at Camp McCarran's mess hall regularly stock the boxes, indicating steady demand among both travelers and NCR personnel. Its availability at locations ranging from the New Vegas Strip to Westside underscores how pre-war manufactured food remains a backbone of post-war diets.
topic_desc_basic: BlamCo Mac & Cheese is a pre-war fast food product still found across the Mojave Wasteland. The familiar box bears the BlamCo logo and a picture of macaroni and cheese. Though irradiated after centuries of exposure, it remains edible and is valued both as a quick meal and as an ingredient in dishes like brahmin Wellington and the Wasteland Omelet. Merchants and mess halls commonly stock it.
tags: blamco corporation,brahmin wellington ingredient,irradiated foodstuff,mojave wasteland food,pre-war food product,wasteland omelet ingredient

topic_desc: Turbo is a chem manufactured primarily by the Great Khans at their Red Rock Drug Lab, where Jack and Diane produce and distribute it alongside other narcotics. Its construction is crude but effective: a standard Jet inhaler secured to a can of HairStylez hairspray, combining the two products into a single dose. When inhaled, Turbo induces a state in which the user perceives surrounding motion at roughly a third of normal speed while retaining their own reflexes and motor function. Enemy movements, projectiles, and even the chem's own duration all appear stretched. This perceptual distortion has practical combat applications, allowing a user to react to threats with unusual precision. The Great Khans guard the recipe closely; knowledge of its manufacture is shared only with trusted associates. Turbo can be found in Great Khan camps at Red Rock Canyon and is sold by their chemists. It has also spread to other corners of the Mojave, appearing in Nipton, Boulder City, Gomorrah, Black Mountain, and even among Powder Ganger populations at the NCR Correctional Facility. Addiction is a known risk, and the chem's effects do not interact reliably with all weapon types or physical actions. Some wastelanders report that Implant GRX, a medical implant offering a similar effect, serves as a non-addictive alternative, though with shorter duration per activation.
topic_desc_basic: Turbo is a chem produced by the Great Khans at their Red Rock Drug Lab. It consists of a Jet inhaler taped to a can of HairStylez hairspray. When used, it briefly slows the user's perception of surrounding motion to roughly a third of normal speed, while the user's own movement and actions remain unaffected. Turbo is addictive and is sold by Great Khan chemists such as Jack, as well as by various traders and bartenders across the Mojave Wasteland.
tags: great khans chem,inhaler chem,jet derivative,mojave narcotics,red rock drug lab,time perception drug

topic_desc: Strange meat is a kebab-style cut of suspicious, reddish meat skewered in chunks and widely regarded with distrust by those who encounter it. Its appearance resembles iguana bits, but its true origin remains a subject of dark rumor. The largest known concentration is in the settlement of Andale, a seemingly idyllic community whose households — the Smiths and the Wilsons — stock prodigious quantities in kitchen and basement refrigerators, with additional stores in a nearby garden shed. This abundance has led wasteland travelers to question what livestock or game could sustain such a supply in a region as desolate as the Capital Wasteland. Smaller caches have been reported in the Chryslus Building lower offices and the County Sewer Mainline, and isolated hunters occasionally carry portions for trade. In the Pitt, a raider known as O-Dog possesses some, and trappers in the Point Lookout swamplands have been found with stores in their shacks. The meat's unsettling prevalence in Andale, combined with the residents' evasive hospitality, has cemented its reputation as something best avoided by the cautious and the squeamish.
topic_desc_basic: Strange meat is a kebab-style serving of suspicious-looking meat chunks, similar in appearance to iguana bits. Its origin is questionable and widely distrusted. The largest known source is the settlement of Andale, where large quantities fill refrigerators in the Smith and Wilson households and a nearby garden shed. Smaller amounts have been found in the Chryslus Building, the County Sewer Mainline, and carried by wandering hunters or trappers in distant regions.
tags: andale settlement,capital wasteland food,kebab meat,questionable provisions,suspicious meat

topic_desc: Tremble represents a specialized category of synthetic toxins produced by knowledgeable wasteland chemists using simple heat sources such as campfires or electric heating plates. The poison's formulation appears tailored to disrupt higher motor functions rather than simply killing outright, making it particularly valued in close-quarters engagements where a momentarily incapacitated foe can be dispatched at leisure. When applied to a blade, club, or thrown weapon, a single dose remains viable until the next successful contact, at which point the full payload transfers into the victim's system. The toxin's most distinctive property is its selective impairment of weapon-handling skills while leaving unarmed capability intact, implying an effect on cognitive or neuromuscular pathways associated specifically with tool manipulation. The gradual damage it inflicts over roughly twenty seconds suggests a slow-acting metabolic poison rather than a fast-acting neurotoxin. Survivors of tremble exposure report a profound loss of dexterity and coordination with any implement, though the effects are temporary under normal physiological conditions. The poison's preparation requires no sophisticated laboratory equipment, making it accessible to any wastelander with sufficient chemical knowledge and basic supplies, though its precise formula is not widely circulated.
topic_desc_basic: Tremble is a contact poison developed in the Mojave Wasteland, designed for application to melee weapons and thrown projectiles. Upon entering a target's bloodstream through a successful strike, the toxin rapidly degrades fine motor coordination and weapon proficiency while simultaneously dealing gradual internal damage over approximately twenty seconds. Its effects spare only unarmed combat techniques, suggesting it targets neural pathways governing tool use rather than raw muscle function.
tags: contact poison,melee weapon coating,mojave poison,motor coordination impairment,synthetic toxin,wasteland chemistry
