topic_desc: The Old Mormon Fort is the oldest surviving structure in the New Vegas area, originally established as the Old Las Vegas Mormon State Historic Park before the Great War. In the post-War era it became the regional headquarters of the Followers of the Apocalypse, who use the walled compound to provide medical care, food distribution, reconstruction assistance, and education to Freeside's impoverished population. The fort also hosts medical research aimed at recreating pre-War pharmaceuticals under wasteland conditions. The interior courtyard is filled with tents serving as wards and dormitories, while two guardhouses anchor the western and eastern corners. Julie Farkas oversees operations, coordinating the Followers' humanitarian mission in a district largely abandoned by the NCR and Mr. House alike. The fort's continued operation represents one of the few organized charitable institutions in the Mojave.
topic_desc_basic: The Old Mormon Fort, located just inside Freeside's North Gate, is the oldest building in New Vegas. It serves as the regional headquarters of the Followers of the Apocalypse, who provide medical care, food distribution, education, and reconstruction services from within its walls. The fort's courtyard is filled with tents sheltering patients and staff, and it houses ongoing medical research into recreating pre-War medicines.

topic_desc: Red Rock Canyon occupies the northwest corner of the Mojave Wasteland and serves as the principal refuge of the Great Khans. Before the Great War the area was designated the Southwest Commonwealth Conservation Area, and remnants of pre-War campsites and ancient petroglyphs still survive among the sandstone formations. The Great Khans relocated here following the Bitter Springs Massacre, in which NCR forces killed a large number of their non-combatants. Under the leadership of Papa Khan, the tribe has concentrated on rebuilding its numbers and expanding its chem manufacturing and distribution enterprise. The canyon features a central arena used for indoctrination rituals, a longhouse where Papa Khan holds court, and a drug lab operated by Jack and Diane. A steep northwestern pass leads past cazador nests toward the Remnants Bunker. The canyon's defensible geography and distance from NCR patrols make it an effective stronghold, though the tribe's future direction remains a subject of internal debate.
topic_desc_basic: Red Rock Canyon is a location in the northwest Mojave Wasteland that serves as the refuge and stronghold of the Great Khans. The tribe relocated there after the Bitter Springs Massacre, in which NCR forces killed many of their non-combatants. The canyon contains the Great Khans' camps, a central arena for initiation rituals, Papa Khan's longhouse, and a chem manufacturing lab. Ancient petroglyphs and pre-War campsites still dot the area.

topic_desc: The Vikki and Vance Casino is a gambling establishment in Primm, named after the pre-War outlaws Vikki and Vance. It is owned and operated by Johnson and Ruby Nash. The casino floor is dominated by the Death Car, the vehicle in which Vikki and Vance were shot and killed, displayed as a morbid centerpiece. The casino offers blackjack, roulette, and slots. During the period of lawlessness following the murder of Primm's sheriff, townsfolk barricaded themselves inside the casino to escape escaped convicts who had seized the town's exterior. A display case intended to hold Vance's 9mm submachine gun was robbed, though the Protectron Primm Slim remains convinced the weapon is still in place. The casino's fortunes are tied to the restoration of law and order in Primm; until a new sheriff is established, gambling remains suspended. The establishment reflects the broader pattern of Mojave border communities existing in a precarious state between NCR authority and frontier anarchy.
topic_desc_basic: The Vikki and Vance Casino is a casino in Primm, named after the outlaws Vikki and Vance. It is owned and operated by Johnson and Ruby Nash. The casino floor features the Death Car, the vehicle in which Vikki and Vance were killed. During the convict takeover of Primm, townsfolk barricaded themselves inside. The casino offers blackjack, roulette, and slots, though its operation depends on the restoration of local law enforcement.

topic_desc: Standard issue for the Rivet City Security Force, this black combat armor variant is paired with a matching helmet. Despite its combat armor classification, the uniform is among the least protective of such variants in the Capital Wasteland, offering less protection than Talon Combat Armor and comparable only to ordinary leather armor while weighing more, which hinders both movement and stealth. Nevertheless, it surpasses most common wasteland garments including mercenary outfits and raider armors. Its principal advantage is a valuable enhancement to small guns proficiency, making it practical for guards who rely on firearms. Officers Lorin and Davis are known to wear the uniform, and guards accompanying water caravans have been observed wearing it as well. A Rivet City security guard was reportedly found in one of the holding cells aboard Mothership Zeta.
topic_desc_basic: The Rivet City Security Uniform is a black combat armor suit worn as standard protection by members of the Rivet City Security Force. It is scratched and worn, with a faint camouflage pattern more visible on the female version. Though heavier and less protective than standard combat armor, it offers better protection than most wasteland clothing and provides a notable bonus to small arms proficiency.

topic_desc: Outcast Power Armor is the distinctive power armor worn by members of the Brotherhood Outcasts, the faction that broke from the main Brotherhood of Steel contingent in the Capital Wasteland under Elder Lyons. The Outcasts, led by Protector Casdin, rejected Lyons' commitment to charity and local aid, preferring to focus on recovering and preserving advanced technology. The armor can be found on dead Brotherhood Outcasts and at Fort Independence, the Outcasts' fortified headquarters. Protector Casdin is known to confiscate Outcast Power Armor from outsiders carrying or wearing it, unless the individual has earned sufficient trust through proven service. Outcasts encountered during the Anchorage simulation will recognize a wearer of this armor as one of their own, while treating those without it as locals. Wearing power armor requires specialized training that most wastelanders lack.
topic_desc_basic: Outcast Power Armor is a suit of power armor worn by the Brotherhood Outcasts, a splinter faction that separated from the Brotherhood of Steel over ideological differences. The armor and its matching helmet can be recovered from fallen Outcasts or found at Fort Independence, the Outcasts' headquarters in the Capital Wasteland.

topic_desc: The Rivet City Security Helmet is a black combat helmet fitted with an acrylic face shield, serving as standard headgear for the Rivet City Security Force alongside its matching uniform. Visually, it is indistinguishable from the Vault 101 Security Helmet, though it accommodates additional eyewear such as sunglasses. Compared to a regular combat helmet, it offers reduced protective value and roughly half the durability, making it a comparatively fragile piece of equipment. Members of the Rivet City Security Force wear the helmet while patrolling Rivet City. Notably, Dusty of Big Town wears one, making him the only known individual outside Rivet City to don a piece of the settlement's security uniform. Officers Lorin and Davis have been identified wearing the helmet, as have guards escorting water caravans. A Rivet City security guard wearing the helmet was reportedly discovered in a holding cell aboard Mothership Zeta.
topic_desc_basic: The Rivet City Security Helmet is a black combat helmet with an acrylic face shield, worn as standard head protection by members of the Rivet City Security Force. topic_desc: The Mechanist's Costume is a distinctive armor set associated with the Mechanist, a costumed figure who adopted a superhero persona in the Capital Wasteland. The costume, paired with the matching Mechanist's Helmet, provides substantial protection comparable to quality combat armor, while boosting the wearer's endurance at the cost of reduced charisma. The Mechanist's conflict with a rival costumed figure known as the AntAgonizer drew attention from nearby Canterbury Commons. The costume can be obtained from the Mechanist, either by force or by persuading him to abandon his persona. Wearing the costume can trigger encounters with admirers, including a child seeking an autograph. The costume also unlocks unique dialogue with Moira Brown of Craterside Supply in Megaton, who may react to the wearer's appearance during discussions related to the Wasteland Survival Guide project. Unlike most armor, the costume cannot be self-repaired and requires a merchant's services.
topic_desc_basic: The Mechanist's Costume is a unique armor set worn by the self-styled superhero known as the Mechanist, who operates in the Capital Wasteland. topic_desc: The Bridge Tower is an integral part of Rivet City's security infrastructure, housing both personnel and matériel critical to maintaining order aboard the derelict aircraft carrier settlement. The Rivet City Security Force, commanded by Harkness with Commander Danvers as second-in-command, uses the tower as its primary base of operations. The first floor provides sleeping and recreation space for guards, while secured footlockers hold personal effects. The armory represents the most sensitive area within the tower. Access is controlled by keys carried only by Harkness and Danvers, with Private Jones, a Mister Gutsy robot, stationed at the threshold as an additional deterrent. An automated turret inside the armory provides further protection against unauthorized entry. Security terminals on the middle and upper floors maintain logs documenting the force's activities. The armory's contents include weaponry and notable schematics, making it a tempting but dangerous target for theft. Rivet City's leadership treats armory security with utmost seriousness; unauthorized intrusion triggers immediate lethal response from both Jones and the turret system.
topic_desc_basic: The Bridge Tower of Rivet City serves as headquarters for the Rivet City Security Force. It contains guards' sleeping quarters, recreation areas, and a well-stocked armory. A Mister Gutsy designated Private Jones stands guard at the armory door. Commander Danvers can be found here overseeing security operations. The tower is a restricted area, with access to the armory tightly controlled by the security leadership.

topic_desc: Boutique Le Chic reflects the curated luxury that defines Tenpenny Tower's commercial concourse. Proprietor Lydia Montenegro manages inventory ranging from practical survival goods—ammunition and protective wear—to aesthetic commodities such as interior design themes for residential suites. The shop's layout includes tall shelving stocked with consumable goods, a counter with cash register, a wall safe, and a terminal behind the counter. The boutique's fortunes are tied to the political stability of Tenpenny Tower itself. In the event of a ghoul takeover, management changes hands to Michael Masters, a ghoul who expands the inventory to include weapons and dart gun schematics. Lydia's continued operation depends on the tower's security arrangements; theft from her safe has been known to drive her from the premises, citing inadequate protection. She periodically leaves the shop unattended, creating vulnerability. The boutique remains the sole purveyor of suite furnishings for residents who relocated from Megaton, making it an essential commercial node within the tower's self-contained economy.
topic_desc_basic: Boutique Le Chic is a retail establishment on the ground floor of Tenpenny Tower, operated by Lydia Montenegro. The shop sells ammunition, armor, and custom furnishing themes for the Tenpenny Tower Suite. Located opposite Café Beau Monde on the west side of the concourse, it features a service counter, shelved merchandise, and a secured safe. It is the primary vendor for suite furnishings available to Tenpenny Tower residents.

topic_desc: The Republic of Dave Capitol Building embodies the micro-state's peculiar approach to governance, combining executive residence and electoral infrastructure under one roof. The ground floor houses the president's office—Dave's seat of power—alongside a voting booth and ballot box used during the settlement's periodic elections. This arrangement reflects the Republic's nominally democratic structure, where leadership is contested through formal voting rather than hereditary succession or force. Upstairs, Rosie resides in a bedroom, one of several family members positioned throughout the settlement. The president's office contains a secured safe whose contents include Ol' Painless, a unique variant of the hunting rifle. Access to the safe varies depending on electoral outcomes: if Rosie or Bob prevails in an election, the combination becomes available, while Dave's continued leadership yields a key. Notably, even with legitimate access, items removed from the safe may still be regarded as stolen property, underscoring the informal and inconsistent nature of property law in the Republic. The building does not permit waiting within its walls, a minor but notable restriction.
topic_desc_basic: The Republic of Dave Capitol Building is the administrative center of the Republic of Dave, a small settlement in the Capital Wasteland. The two-story structure contains the president's office and a voting booth with ballot box on the first floor, and a bedroom upstairs occupied by Rosie. A safe in the president's office holds the unique hunting rifle Ol' Painless.

topic_desc: Foggy Bottom Station is a component of the pre-War DCTA Metro network that once served the greater Washington, D.C. area. Situated on the White Line, the station retains its original infrastructure: toll-booth entrances from the north and south, a central escalator descending to the platform level, and a second-floor waiting area with benches. The tunnel system is partially collapsed, with caved-in passages limiting transit options, though one serviceable tunnel leads east and another connects westward to Metro Central. The station has attracted raider holdouts who occupy the waiting area and platform, exploiting the confined corridors and limited access points for defensive advantage. Approaches to neighboring stations are hazardous: the Dupont Circle route is littered with bear traps, while the Georgetown approach contains only one. A Protectron charging pad and terminal on the north side of the platform suggest pre-War automated maintenance protocols persisted. The station also contains a unique book belonging to someone named Danielle, and a copy of Nikola Tesla and You rests on an electrical cabinet near the charging station.
topic_desc_basic: Foggy Bottom Station is a pre-War Metro station on the White Line, part of the underground transit system beneath the Washington, D.C. ruins. It features two entrances with toll-booths, a second-floor waiting area, and multiple tunnel connections including routes to Metro Central and DCTA Tunnel 014-B Potomac. Raiders have established holdouts within the station. The approach to Dupont Circle contains several bear traps.

topic_desc: Veronica's Power Fist is a personal unarmed weapon carried by Veronica, a scribe of the Brotherhood of Steel chapter operating from Hidden Valley in the Mojave Wasteland. It is functionally identical to a standard Power Fist, a pneumatic melee weapon that uses hydraulic impact to amplify the force of a punch. The weapon bears thirty-three notches along its surface, presumably a tally of some significance to its owner. It is classified as an improved holdout weapon, meaning it can be concealed in restricted areas under certain conditions. The Power Fist family of weapons includes several variants found across the Mojave and beyond, including models modified by the Gun Runners' Arsenal, the industrial-grade Industrial Hand, and Saturnite-based fists developed at Big MT. Veronica, as a Brotherhood scribe with combat training, favors this weapon as her sidearm, reflecting the order's tradition of pairing technological literacy with practical field skill.
topic_desc_basic: Veronica's Power Fist is an unarmed weapon used by Veronica, a scribe of the Brotherhood of Steel in the Mojave Wasteland. It is functionally identical to a standard Power Fist, a pneumatic device that amplifies the force of a punch through hydraulic impact. The weapon bears thirty-three notches visible upon close inspection, though their significance is known only to Veronica herself. It is classified as an improved holdout weapon.

topic_desc: The Prototype Medic Power Armor, designated MP-47/A, was a pre-war military prototype designed to function as an automated field medic for soldiers in combat. Its core innovation was an integrated Med-X injection system that monitored the wearer's limb condition and automatically administered the drug when health dropped below critical thresholds or when a limb was severely damaged. Production models were planned to support additional injectables such as Stimpaks, but the prototype phase never advanced that far. The armor also featured a verbal feedback system modeled on the Mister Gutsy line of military robots, delivering gruff, motivational announcements when enemies were detected or injections were administered. More sinister features included command-level data reporting and a self-destruct mechanism capable of delivering a lethal injection to deserters, though these remained offline in the prototype. The armor's shoulder guards bear U.S. military roundels rather than Brotherhood insignia, marking it as a genuine pre-war artifact. A dead Brotherhood of Steel Initiate was found wearing the armor in the Olney Sewers, suggesting the Brotherhood had attempted to recover or deploy it. The armor's voice refers to Med-X as "Vitamin M" or "Morphine," reflecting earlier pre-war nomenclature.
topic_desc_basic: The Prototype Medic Power Armor, also called the MP-47/A, is a unique pre-war power armor prototype designed to act as an automated field medic. It monitors its wearer's limb condition and automatically injects Med-X when health or limb condition drops below critical levels. The armor features a verbal feedback system resembling a Mister Gutsy robot, announcing enemy presence and injections. It was found on a dead Brotherhood of Steel Initiate in the Olney Sewers.

topic_desc: Metal Armor in the Capital Wasteland is a improvised protective suit assembled from scavenged scrap metal plates welded onto a black leather base, with spiked shoulder guards for additional intimidation and protection. It represents a middle tier of wasteland protection, offering better defense than leather or raider gear but lacking the sophistication of combat armor or power armor. The armor is typically paired with a Metal Helmet to form a complete set. Several variants exist across the wasteland, including the Gamma Shield Armor, which trades additional weight for radiation resistance, and the Samurai Armor worn by Toshiro Kago, which enhances melee combat capability. Metal armor is commonly worn by slavers, mercenaries, and bandits, reflecting its association with the rougher elements of wasteland society. Notable figures such as Leroy Walker of the slavers, Commander Jabsco at Fort Bannister, and the slaver duo Jotun and Ymir at Paradise Falls are known to wear it. Bandits who attack Aqua Pura caravans also favor this armor, and Split Jack is known to distribute suits to those who join his raids.
topic_desc_basic: Metal Armor is a suit of improvised protective gear crafted from scrap metal plates attached to a black leather base, with spiked shoulder guards. It is commonly worn by slavers, mercenaries, and bandits throughout the Capital Wasteland. The armor is part of a set that includes a matching Metal Helmet. It offers better protection than leather armor but is less sophisticated than combat armor or power armor.

topic_desc: Linden's Outcast Power Armor is a suit of power armor formerly belonging to Branchtender Linden, a member of the Oasis treedwellers who was once an Outcast of the Brotherhood of Steel. The armor is notable for its enhancement of the Big Guns skill, a rare attribute among power armor variants in the Capital Wasteland, making it prized by those who favor heavy weaponry. Unlike standard Brotherhood power armor, the game treats Linden's armor as a faction-less variant, meaning it does not trigger confiscation by Protector Casdin of the Outcasts, nor do Outcast forces from the Anchorage Reclamation Simulation recognize it as their own. This unusual status likely reflects Linden's departure from the Outcasts and his integration into the Oasis community. The armor is offered by Linden as a reward following the resolution of events at Oasis, specifically when Harold's heart is treated with Laurel's Liniment. Only three armors in the Capital Wasteland are known to enhance Big Guns proficiency: Linden's, the Bombshell Armor, and Lag-Bolt's Combat Armor. Like all power armor, wearing it requires specialized Power Armor Training, which can be obtained through the Brotherhood at the Citadel or through the Anchorage simulation.
topic_desc_basic: Linden's Outcast Power Armor is a suit of power armor belonging to Branchtender Linden, a former Brotherhood of Steel Outcast who joined the Oasis treedwellers. Unlike standard power armor, it enhances the wearer's Big Guns skill. The armor is treated as faction-less, meaning Outcasts do not recognize it as their own. Linden offers it as a reward following events at Oasis.
tags: big guns bonus,branchtender linden,brotherhood outcast armor,capital wasteland,faction-less power armor,oasis treedwellers

topic_desc: The Caesar's Legion Safehouse serves as a forward operating base for Legion operatives conducting business in the Mojave Wasteland, west of the Colorado River. The safehouse is maintained by Veteran Atticus, a Legion veteran who appears at the location every few days to offer supplies to those trusted by the Legion. Access is tightly controlled: the key is held by Lucius, a senior Legion officer stationed at the Fort, and cannot be taken from him by force or theft. It is only offered to individuals who have demonstrated strong loyalty to the Legion. The building itself consists of two large rooms connected by stairs, with ample storage in cabinets and footlockers. Outside, a campfire provides a place for crafting. Inside, the safehouse contains three beds, a radio tuned to Radio New Vegas, and a water fountain dispensing clean water. Sets of Legion armor—including Centurion, Vexillarius, and Praetorian variants—are laid out on the beds, along with weapons such as a chainsaw, sniper rifle, and displacer glove. Lucky Shades are also available. Atticus provides periodic supplies including Stealth Boys, Cateye, and skill magazines to those who maintain the Legion's trust.
topic_desc_basic: The Caesar's Legion Safehouse is a small house in the Mojave Wasteland used by Caesar's Legion for operations west of the Colorado River. It is maintained by Veteran Atticus, who visits periodically. The key is held by Lucius at the Fort and can only be obtained through him. Inside are beds, storage, a radio, clean water, and various sets of Legion armor and equipment.
tags: caesar legion safehouse,legion armor storage,legion forward base,lucius fort key,mojave wasteland location,veteran atticus

topic_desc: Dead Wind Cavern is one of the most dangerous natural formations in the Mojave Wasteland, situated at the end of a long, shallow valley northeast of Primm Pass and south of the REPCONN Test Site, past Harper's Shack. The cavern is home to a substantial population of Deathclaws at various stages of maturity, from young deathclaws to a fearsome Legendary Deathclaw that inhabits the deepest chamber. The cave's layout consists of an entrance cavern that funnels into a forking passage. The right fork leads to a dead-end room, while the left fork opens into a longer area containing a deathclaw hatchery, where a Deathclaw Mother guards eggs and young. Beyond the hatchery lies the final chamber, where the Legendary Deathclaw dwells alongside two additional deathclaws. In this deepest room lies the corpse of a Brotherhood of Steel paladin clad in T-45d power armor, carrying dozens of 40mm grenades. Beside the body rests Mercy, a unique 40mm grenade machine gun. A duffle bag with supplies can be found against impassable rubble accessible only from the hatchery side. A hollowed-out rock near the entrance provides a small cache for travelers.
topic_desc_basic: Dead Wind Cavern is a cave system in the Mojave Wasteland, located near Primm Pass and south of the REPCONN Test Site. It is infested with a wide variety of Deathclaws, including a Legendary Deathclaw. The cavern contains a deathclaw hatchery with eggs, and the remains of a Brotherhood of Steel paladin bearing unique weaponry.
tags: brotherhood paladin corpse,dead wind cavern,deathclaw lair,legendary deathclaw,mercy grenade machinegun,mojave cave system

topic_desc: The East Pump Station is a critical infrastructure facility in the Mojave Wasteland, situated between Vault 34 and the NCR Sharecropper Farms, just west of the monorail track system. Its importance to the NCR cannot be overstated: it is responsible for filtering water pumped along a giant water pipe from Lake Las Vegas before redirecting it to the sharecropper farms, making it a linchpin in the NCR's regional agricultural efforts. The station consists of two main rooms—an office area and a reactor room. The office contains a damaged terminal that requires significant scientific expertise to repair and reconnect to the network. Two nearby entrances to the East Central Sewers provide subterranean access. The station is connected via a pipe to the east cistern, a separate single-room structure containing junk, supplies, bottles of Nuka-Cola, and a copy of Fixin' Things on a desk beside a broken terminal. The cistern also features a water valve and trough dispensing clean water. Posters and postcards referencing the Sierra Madre casino and Dean Domino can be found inside, suggesting pre-war or wasteland-era interest in that distant establishment.
topic_desc_basic: The East Pump Station is a facility in the Mojave Wasteland located between Vault 34 and the NCR Sharecropper Farms. It is vital to the NCR, filtering water pumped from Lake Las Vegas to the sharecropper farms. The station contains a damaged terminal and is connected to an east cistern with supplies and clean water.
tags: east central sewers,east pump station,lake las vegas filtration,mojave facility,ncr water infrastructure,sharecropper farms water

topic_desc: The Whittaker Farmstead is a modest agricultural dwelling situated on the northern side of Nevada 159 in the Mojave Wasteland, southwest of the Allied Technologies Offices. In recent times, the farmstead has been commandeered by a group of four to five Powder Gangers who have established it as their hideout. The front door is secured with an easy lock, and a ham radio sits inside. Two graves lie west of the main building. Among the items present are a giant damaged garden gnome outside, a copy of Future Weapons Today in the kitchen, and a Ranger Holodisk Message on a table near the front door. The holodisk message details a group of NCR rangers and soldiers cut off from their platoon by Legion forces. Curiously, this same message also appears in Boulder City, the result of a development error that mixed up two separate notes. The intended message for the farmstead was reportedly about Powder Ganger leader Samuel Cooke taking most of his gang to investigate Vault 19 while leaving a few behind to monitor local NCR and Fiends activity. A large cloud of yellow sulfur smoke may be visible to the west if nearby caves are destroyed.
topic_desc_basic: The Whittaker Farmstead is a small farm in the Mojave Wasteland on the northern side of Nevada 159, southwest of the Allied Technologies Offices. It has recently been taken over by a group of Powder Gangers who use it as a hideout. The farmstead contains a ham radio and two graves to the west.
tags: mojave farmstead,nevada 159 location,powder ganger hideout,ranger holodisk message,samuel cooke vault 19,whittaker farmstead

topic_desc: Tenleytown Station is part of the pre-War Red Line Metro network, connecting to Friendship Station and providing access to Chevy Chase North via its southern exit. The tunnel system has become a hazardous transit corridor frequented by feral ghouls, radroaches, and at least one super mutant that occupies the northern tunnel entrance. The super mutant is known to attack surviving ghouls it detects, creating a volatile predator dynamic within the tunnels. A utility junction between track lines near the Farragut West access door contains an Eat'o'tronic 3000 wall dispenser and a vending machine, remnants of pre-War commuter infrastructure. The station's name appeared in Metro advertisements before the War. A rigged toilet trap in the men's bathroom near the Friendship Heights exit contains microfusion cells, suggesting someone booby-trapped the facilities. The station serves as a critical passage for anyone attempting to reach the Galaxy News Radio station through Chevy Chase.
topic_desc_basic: Tenleytown Station is a Red Line Metro tunnel connecting to Friendship Station in the Capital Wasteland. It serves as a passage toward Chevy Chase North and the Galaxy News Radio station. The tunnels are infested with feral ghouls, radroaches, and a super mutant guarding the northern entrance. Pre-War amenities like an Eat'o'tronic 3000 dispenser and vending machine remain in a utility junction between track lines.
tags: capital wasteland metro,chevy chase north exit,feral ghoul infestation,galaxy news radio access,red line metro tunnel,super mutant presence

topic_desc: The Museum of Dave is a small single-room building within the Republic of Dave, serving dual purposes as both a repository of Dave memorabilia and an impromptu schoolhouse for the republic's children. Shawna, a merchant who operates from the building, educates the children about Dave's past and periodically conducts guided tours explaining the history behind various artifacts on display. The museum's collection consists of items Dave considers significant to his personal history and the history of the settlement. The room is arranged with school desks along the left wall and artifacts displayed along the right wall, some on shelves and others fixed directly to the wall. A blackboard hangs opposite the entrance. The museum also functions as a trading location, making it one of the few commercial spaces in the small settlement. The Perception Bobblehead rests on a shelf among the exhibits, alongside pre-War books.
topic_desc_basic: The Museum of Dave is a small building in the Republic of Dave that doubles as a trading post and schoolhouse. Shawna, a merchant, teaches the republic's children about Dave's history and gives tours explaining the various Dave memorabilia stored inside. The single-room interior contains school desks, a blackboard, and artifacts displayed along the walls and on shelves.
tags: dave history tours,dave memorabilia collection,impromptu schoolhouse,republic of dave,shawna merchant teacher,trading location

topic_desc: Jury St. Tunnels are a tunnel system accessible through Jury St. Station in the Capital Wasteland. The tunnels have become notable for the activities of Ryan Brigg, a wastelander who joined a group of raiders to further his culinary research. Brigg eventually became their leader by paying them for mole rat meat and wonderglue they scavenged, using the raiders as both guards and supply runners for his laboratory in the northeast section of the tunnels. Brigg's experiments with mole rat meat led him to construct the Wonder Meat Maker, a device that combines wonderglue and mole rat meat to produce mole rat wonder meat. However, his experiments appear to have increased the aggressiveness of the mole rat colony inhabiting the tunnels, resulting in frequent attacks against raider positions. Brigg keeps a tame mole rat named Pumpkin in a cage in his laboratory, a notable exception among the otherwise hostile colony. The tunnels contain significant quantities of mole rat meat, wonderglue, and blood packs stored near Brigg's work area.
topic_desc_basic: Jury St. Tunnels are a tunnel system reachable through Jury St. Station. They are inhabited by mole rats and raiders led by Ryan Brigg, a wastelander who joined the raiders to pursue his research on improving mole rat meat. Brigg's experiments appear to have made the local mole rat colony more aggressive, causing frequent attacks on raider positions. He keeps a tame mole rat named Pumpkin in his laboratory.
tags: jury street station tunnels,mole rat wonder meat,pumpkin tame mole rat,raider gang hideout,ryan brigg laboratory,wonder meat maker

topic_desc: The Brass Lantern is a restaurant in Megaton operated by the Stahl family, consisting of siblings Leo, Jenny, and Andy Stahl. After the death of their parents, Leo, the eldest, took charge of raising his younger siblings. The establishment remains family-owned, with Andy serving as owner, Leo working inside the restaurant, and Jenny serving settlers in the outdoor eating area. The restaurant is divided into several sections: an outdoor eating area, an indoor eating area, a storage and preparation room, an owner's office, and private living quarters for the Stahl family separated by a shack door. The owner's office contains a floor safe and a terminal. A crumpled note jammed behind a chair in the office can unlock the terminal, which in turn can open the safe. The living quarters are split between Jenny's downstairs bed and the two brothers' separate upstairs beds. A Chinese neon sign outside reads partially as "Ming Fast Food," with the final character missing from the sign. The restaurant is one of the primary dining and social establishments in Megaton.
topic_desc_basic: The Brass Lantern is a restaurant in Megaton run by the Stahl family. Andy Stahl owns the establishment, Leo works inside, and Jenny serves settlers in the outdoor eating area. After their parents died, Leo raised his younger siblings. The restaurant includes indoor and outdoor seating, a storage room, an owner's office with a floor safe, and private living quarters for the family.
tags: andy stahl owner,brass lantern eatery,jenny stahl server,leo stahl worker,megaton restaurant,stahl family business

topic_desc: Guardian Peak rises in the Mojave Wasteland south-southeast of Ranger Station Bravo, marked by a pre-War sign listing an elevation of 2,667 feet. The New California Republic dispatched soldiers under Sergeant Banner to reclaim old hiking trails and establish an observation base, but the survey team failed to note a cave system within the mountain. On the fifth day of operations, strange noises were reported, and blasting uncovered a passage leading deep inside. A team including Private Halford was sent to explore. The summit offers commanding views of Hoover Dam, the Colorado River, Fortification Hill, and Lake Mead. The surface camp is now devoid of living NCR personnel; giant rats and radscorpions roam the peak. The nearby Camp Guardian Caves contain the remains of the troopers who were stationed there. Broc flowers grow along the trail, and scattered daily logs record the garrison's final days.
topic_desc_basic: Guardian Peak is a mountain in the Mojave Wasteland, south-southeast of Ranger Station Bravo. The New California Republic established Camp Guardian on its northern slope as an observation post. Soldiers under Sergeant Banner cleared old hiking trails and blasted rock, inadvertently uncovering a cave system. Strange noises preceded the garrison's demise. The summit offers views of Hoover Dam, the Colorado River, Fortification Hill, and Lake Mead. Giant rats and radscorpions now populate the area.
tags: camp guardian,cave system,mount guardian peak,ncr observation post,private halford,sergeant banner

topic_desc: Zapp's Neon Signs, located in the South Vegas Ruins, was once a major sign manufacturing company whose work illuminated the Las Vegas Strip. After the Great War, the company's durable signage found new purpose as barricade material; both the Fiends of South Vegas and the inhabitants of North Vegas Square repurposed the signs as impassable perimeter walls. The building retains an entrance office, workshop, and foreman's office, surrounded by exterior barricades assembled from assorted pre-War signs, including the feet of a Tall Boy statue. The interior has been heavily trapped with frag mines, trip wires, and a grenade bouquet. A Fiend named Duke occupies the foreman's office, which contains an easy-locked terminal with company records. Notably, the terminal entries identify the business as McMurray's Neon Sign Designs rather than Zapp's Neon Signs, suggesting a discrepancy between the common wasteland name and the original company name.
topic_desc_basic: Zapp's Neon Signs is an unmarked location in the South Vegas Ruins of the Mojave Wasteland. Before the Great War, it was a major sign manufacturer that lit up the Las Vegas Strip. Afterward, its signs became barricade material for the Fiends and North Vegas Square residents. The building is now inhabited by Fiends and heavily trapped with mines and trip wires. A Fiend named Duke guards the foreman's office.
tags: duke the fiend,fiend stronghold,neon sign factory,neon sign graveyard,south vegas ruins,trapped building

topic_desc: The Yangtze Memorial is a pre-War stone monument topped by a large cross, erected to honor soldiers who fell during the Yangtze Campaign following the Chinese invasion of Alaska. Though weathered and scavenged, the structure still stands over two centuries after the Great War, with the names of the fallen still visible on faded stone. Few wastelanders recall the memorial's original purpose; most now use it simply as a navigation landmark. It occupies a raised platform surrounded by descending steps and a central fence. Three graves lie to the south, and a hollowed-out rock marked with a peace sign is nearby. The memorial currently marks the edge of safe territory around Quarry Junction, where deathclaws have established a presence. A warning sign east of the monument alerts travelers to the danger. An abandoned shack lies to the northwest. Coyotes and radscorpions are known to patrol the vicinity.
topic_desc_basic: The Yangtze Memorial is a pre-War landmark in the Mojave Wasteland honoring fallen soldiers of the Yangtze Campaign after China invaded Alaska. Damaged by time and scavenging, it still stands over two centuries after the Great War. Few wastelanders remember its purpose; most use it as a navigation aid. It now marks the edge of safe territory near Quarry Junction, where deathclaws have taken over.
tags: mojave wasteland landmark,navigation landmark,pre-war monument,quarry junction deathclaws,sino-american war,yangtze campaign memorial

topic_desc: Ranger Station Echo is a New California Republic military outpost positioned equidistant from the Cliffside Prospector Camp and Coyote Mines in the Mojave Wasteland. Its strategic purpose is to observe and report on Caesar's Legion movements at Cottonwood Cove. The station comprises a sandbag overlook, a shack, and a tent, with a large radio tower rising from the clifftop. Access is limited to the western approach. Ranger Erasmus commands the post, and Comm Officer Green operates the radio equipment. Notably, many personnel stationed at Echo are ghouls, a characteristic unique among NCR ranger stations. Several radioactive craters lie to the south, the southernmost containing water emitting roughly two rads per second. Private Kyle Edwards may be present at the station under certain circumstances. The station's position makes it vulnerable to Legionary Assassin attacks arriving from the base of the hill.
topic_desc_basic: Ranger Station Echo is a New California Republic outpost in the Mojave Wasteland, located between the Cliffside Prospector Camp and Coyote Mines. Its purpose is to observe Caesar's Legion activity at Cottonwood Cove. The station includes a sandbag overlook, shack, tent, and radio tower. Ranger Erasmus commands the post, with Comm Officer Green operating the radio. Many personnel here are ghouls, unique among NCR ranger stations.
tags: comm officer green,cottonwood cove observation,ghoul personnel,ncr ranger station,radio tower outpost,ranger erasmus

topic_desc: The Ranger Sequoia serves as both a weapon and a badge of honor within the New California Republic Rangers, the elite military arm of the NCR. Only those who have completed two decades of service receive one, making it a rare sight even among Ranger units. Chief Hanlon, the longtime head of the NCR Rangers stationed at Camp Golf, carries one as a personal sidearm. The revolver is closely related to the hunting revolver, a scoped and somewhat less powerful variant; both are heavy-caliber handguns designed for stopping power at moderate range. The engravings reflect the Rangers' self-image as defenders of the Republic against tyranny, a ethos that has shaped the unit since its founding as a frontier law-enforcement and scouting force. Veteran Rangers deployed to the Mojave Wasteland during the NCR's campaign against Caesar's Legion are frequently seen carrying the Sequoia, marking them as the most experienced and hardened personnel in the NCR military apparatus.
topic_desc_basic: The Ranger Sequoia is a large double-action revolver carried by veteran members of the New California Republic Rangers. It is presented as a gift after twenty years of service, and a plate on the grip reads "20 Years." The barrel is engraved "For Honorable Service" and "Against All Tyrants," and the grip bears the Ranger insignia. It is a scopeless variant of the hunting revolver and is among the most respected sidearms in NCR service.
tags: camp golf,commemorative sidearm,double action revolver,hanlon sidearm,mojave war weapon,ncr veteran ranger

topic_desc: The chainsaw is a pre-war tool repurposed as a weapon of war in the post-nuclear era. Its continuous cutting action makes it devastating against armored foes, as the spinning chain tears through protective gear that would deflect conventional melee strikes. In the Mojave Wasteland, the weapon is associated with some of the region's most violent factions. Motor-Runner, the leader of the Fiends occupying Vault 3, wields one as his signature arm. Caesar's Legion employs chainsaws among its centurions and blacksmiths, reflecting the Legion's pragmatic embrace of brutal close-quarters weaponry despite its otherwise classical Roman aesthetic. During the Second Battle of Hoover Dam, Legion centurions carried chainsaws into the assault. The weapon is also occasionally stocked by merchants such as Cliff Briscoe in Novac, Quartermaster Bardon at Hoover Dam, and the Vendortron kiosk outside the Gun Runners' fabrication plant. A modifiable variant is distributed through the Gun Runners' Arsenal catalog. The chainsaw is related in function to the Ripper, another continuous-cutting melee weapon, and both are valued for their ability to shred through hardened targets where ordinary blades would fail.
topic_desc_basic: The chainsaw is a heavy melee weapon that uses a motorized cutting chain to inflict continuous injury on anything in contact with its blade. Unlike ordinary bladed weapons, it is held against a target to keep cutting rather than striking in discrete blows. Its tearing action is effective against even well-armored opponents. Chainsaws are found in the hands of Fiends, Caesar's Legion centurions, and various traders across the Mojave Wasteland.
tags: continuous melee weapon,fiend weapon,legion centurion arm,mojave melee weapon,motor runner weapon,prewar tool weapon

topic_desc: The multiplas rifle is an energy weapon derived from the common plasma rifle platform, modified to discharge three plasma bolts simultaneously rather than one. This triple-shot mechanism dramatically increases raw destructive output but at the cost of tripled ammunition consumption per firing, making it expensive to operate for extended engagements. Each bolt can independently inflict severe thermal injury, meaning a single trigger pull can produce multiple critical hits on a target. The weapon is relatively rare in the Mojave Wasteland. Examples have been recovered from the bodies of dead prospectors at Deathclaw Promontory, found in the possession of super mutant brutes at Ruby Hill Mine, and spotted among the inventory of the Van Graff family's Silver Rush energy-weapon emporium in Freeside. The Followers of the Apocalypse keep one in their safehouse, and traders such as Blake at the Crimson Caravan Company and Miguel in Westside occasionally stock the rifle. A unique and more refined variant of the plasma rifle family, the Q-35 Matter Modulator, represents a separate line of development. The multiplas rifle's aggressive ammunition consumption limits its practicality for wastelanders without reliable access to microfusion or energy cell supplies, but its sheer output makes it prized by those who can sustain the cost.
topic_desc_basic: The multiplas rifle is a plasma weapon that fires three bolts of superheated plasma with each trigger pull, consuming three energy cells per shot. It is a variant of the standard plasma rifle, trading efficiency for raw output. The weapon can be found in the hands of prospectors, super mutants, and merchants across the Mojave Wasteland, and is sometimes stocked at the Silver Rush in Freeside.
tags: high consumption weapon,mojave energy weapon,plasma energy weapon,silver rush weapon,triple shot rifle,van graff stock

topic_desc: Lucky is a distinctive variant of the .357 Magnum revolver, one of the most common handgun designs in the Mojave Wasteland. What sets Lucky apart from the standard model is a combination of a high rate of fire and an unusually high likelihood of striking a target's most vulnerable point, making it devastating in the hands of a skilled shooter. The word "Lucky" is engraved on the frame, suggesting it was either a custom piece or a personally named weapon. Lucky is concealed in a hardened floor safe within the gift shop of the Bison Steve Hotel in Primm, a town that has seen its share of turmoil from raider occupation to NCR law-enforcement efforts. The safe requires considerable skill to open. Among one-handed firearms in the Mojave, Lucky is regarded as having one of the finest combinations of speed and precision, surpassed only by specialized silenced pistols in sheer critical-strike potential. It is classified as an improved holdout weapon, meaning it can be carried discreetly into locations where firearms are normally confiscated. The revolver can be maintained using parts from standard .357 Magnum revolvers and the smaller police pistol.
topic_desc_basic: Lucky is a unique .357 Magnum revolver engraved with the word "Lucky" along its barrel. It fires rapidly for a revolver and is noted for its exceptional precision, making it a favored sidearm among those who value accuracy. Lucky is kept in a locked floor safe inside the Bison Steve Hotel in Primm, hidden in the gift shop behind the cash register.
tags: engraved sidearm,high precision revolver,holdout weapon,mojave unique weapon,primm bison steve,unique magnum revolver

topic_desc: Before the war, Callville Bay functioned as a boating harbor and marina serving Lake Mead, with Captain Dean Boat Rentals supplying motors and supplies to recreational boaters. The facility included a store and a boathouse near the water's edge. In the post-war era, the location has become a no-man's land. Cazadores have established a nest within the boathouse, making the site hazardous to approach. Giant rats occupy the store interior, where a locked safe and first aid supplies remain. The boat launch on the Lake Mead shoreline retains its tow winch. The site's relative isolation and position on the lake make it notable for those familiar with the region's geography. Maritime signal flags on the Callville Bay sign spell out the letters RJTD. The location sits along Lake Mead's north shore in what was once Clark County, Nevada.
topic_desc_basic: Callville Bay is a derelict former boat launch on the shores of Lake Mead in the Mojave Wasteland, northeast of the Scavenger Platform. Once a small port operated by Captain Dean Boat Rentals, it offered Poseidon U-235 Outboard Motors to boaters. Today the site is overrun by cazadores that have nested inside the remains of a corrugated metal warehouse. A ruined boathouse and the abandoned rental store still stand, with a boat launch and tow winch on the shoreline.
tags: captain dean rentals,cazador nest,derelict boat launch,lake mead shoreline,mojave wasteland location

topic_desc: Operated by Chet, the Goodsprings General Store serves as the commercial hub of the small Mojave town of Goodsprings. The store's shelves stock firearms, armor, weapon mods, and everyday provisions. A notable feature is that Chet's merchant inventory is linked directly to the store's interior shelving, so purchasing certain items removes their physical copies from the displays. The store interior contains grocery freezers with consumables, display cases holding scrap electronics and a silenced pistol, and a back room with a bed and refrigerator. Outside, a Mojave Express Dropbox and crafting benches sit on the porch and along the eastern wall. The building's layout, proximity to the Prospector Saloon, and design closely mirror the real-world Goodsprings General Store in Goodsprings, Nevada, including ceiling design, wall construction, and external signage.
topic_desc_basic: The Goodsprings General Store is the primary supply shop in the town of Goodsprings, run by a local merchant named Chet. The store sells guns, armor, weapon modifications, and various basic supplies to travelers and townsfolk. A Mojave Express Dropbox sits on the porch outside. The building sits between the Prospector Saloon and outdoor crafting benches, making it a central stop for anyone passing through the small settlement.
tags: chet merchant store,goodsprings nevada building,goodsprings supply shop,mojave express dropbox,weapon mods vendor

topic_desc: The Goodsprings Schoolhouse is a pre-war educational facility that has fallen into disrepair within the small Mojave settlement of Goodsprings. The building retains its distinctive spire and chain-link fence, closely resembling the real-world Goodsprings Elementary School, which closed in 2026 due to low enrollment and was repurposed by the town. Inside, the ruins are littered with overturned desks, lockers, and assorted debris. Giant mantis nymphs have made the structure their home, with egg sacs that can release additional nymphs if disturbed. A long counter in the rear holds a footlocker, toolbox, and an easy-locked terminal connected to an easy-locked safe on the floor nearby. The safe contains a Stealth Boy and a super stimpak, while various skill magazines are scattered among the benches and desks. Xander root grows near the tree stump outside the east entrance. Local residents are aware of the safe and may suggest it as a source of useful supplies.
topic_desc_basic: The Goodsprings Schoolhouse is a pre-war school building in the town of Goodsprings. Surrounded by a broken fence, it has two entrances and is filled with toppled desks, lockers, and debris. Giant mantis nymphs inhabit the interior, along with their egg sacs. A locked safe and terminal sit on a counter in the back of the building. Xander root plants grow near the east entrance by a tree stump outside.
tags: abandoned schoolhouse building,giant mantis nymphs,goodsprings pre-war school,locked safe terminal,xander root plants

topic_desc: Friendship Station is a Red Line Metro tunnel connecting to Tenleytown Stations in the Capital Wasteland's pre-war transit network. The northern rail platform area features restrooms and small offices near the Friendship Heights exit. The station is infested with feral ghouls and radroaches, and several dead mercenaries and wastelanders can be found throughout, suggesting prior expeditions ended badly. A collapsed corrugated steel shelter on the platform burns steadily. In the train tunnels to the north, a glowing one and feral ghoul have killed a mercenary armed with a laser rifle. The junction to the south holds another dead mercenary alongside a cache of crafting components. Notable items include a Nuka-Cola Quantum on a bench near the northern escalator, a copy of Lying, Congressional Style near a generator, and a Grognak the Barbarian comic in the back room of the northeast office. The men's bathroom contains a trapped toilet rigged with microfusion cells. The station serves as a passage toward the Galaxy News Radio station through the Chevy Chase North exit.
topic_desc_basic: Friendship Station is a Red Line Metro tunnel in the Capital Wasteland connecting to Tenleytown Stations. The northern rail platform area contains restrooms and small offices near the Friendship Heights exit. It is infested with feral ghouls and radroaches. Dead mercenaries and wastelanders are found throughout the tunnels. The station must be traversed to reach the Galaxy News Radio station through the Chevy Chase North exit.
tags: chevy chase north exit,feral ghoul infestation,friendship heights exit,galaxy news radio passage,red line metro tunnel,tenleytown stations connection

topic_desc: Franklin Metro Utility is a partially irradiated and water-filled metro utility tunnel within the Capital Wasteland's metro network, with exits to Falls Church and Hubris Comics. The tunnel loops back onto itself, allowing traversal from the end back to the beginning via a hole in the floor. The area is heavily populated by feral ghouls and glowing ones, with more dangerous feral ghoul reavers appearing in greater numbers at higher experience levels. The heavily irradiated sections can harbor groups of up to five ghouls attacking simultaneously. Notable findings include five stealth boys scattered throughout the tunnel, pre-war books in the upstairs portion of the first room, and a Tumblers Today guide near the Falls Church door beside a turret. A Burnmaster flamethrower and a Nuka-Cola Quantum rest in a trailer at the heavily irradiated end. A mini nuke sits on a crate alongside an advanced radiation suit where the tunnel first becomes submerged. The tunnel also contains the largest single-section cache of turpentine in the wasteland, totaling fifteen flasks.
topic_desc_basic: Franklin Metro Utility is a metro utility tunnel in the Capital Wasteland, slightly irradiated and partially water-filled, with exits to Falls Church and Hubris Comics. The tunnel loops back onto itself. It is heavily infested with feral ghouls and glowing ones. Notable items include stealth boys, pre-war books, a Burnmaster flamethrower, a Nuka-Cola Quantum, and a mini nuke with an advanced radiation suit underwater.
tags: falls church exit,feral ghoul infestation,hubris comics exit,irradiated water-filled tunnel,metro utility tunnel,stealth boy cache

topic_desc: Hallowed Moors Cemetery is a ruined burial ground in the Capital Wasteland, situated north of Big Town, west-northwest of the Meresti Trainyard, and northeast of Vault 106 across the river. A decrepit chapel on the grounds has been occupied by four super mutants who keep gore bags and hold a human captive. At higher experience levels, one of these super mutants may be a super mutant overlord. A respawning deathclaw roams the nearby area, making the cemetery a hazardous waypoint. Three makeshift beddings around a campfire inside the building suggest the chapel has been used as a camp. The Keller Family Transcript, part two of five, rests on a podium beside the door, along with a Big Book of Science and a D.C. Journal of Internal Medicine on nearby shelves. A mini nuke can be found in a crate by a radio. The caravan merchant Lucky Harith is known to pass near this area and frequently engages the super mutants, often with fatal results if the chapel has not been cleared beforehand. A raider outpost of three respawning raiders lies south-southeast near a stone bridge leading toward Big Town.

topic_desc: The Montgomery County Reservoir is an abandoned water treatment plant in the mid-northwest reaches of the Capital Wasteland, situated northwest of the Reclining Groves Resort Homes. The facility serves as a stopping point for travelers, offering relatively clean drinking water with only minimal radiation, obtained by operating wheels on two of the four circular water tanks. The site is home to up to a half dozen raiders who respawn roughly every three days. An abandoned barn to the northwest contains ammunition boxes on its second floor, along with a fake pre-war book and a bottle of vodka. West of the barn, a makeshift shelter holds additional unlocked ammunition boxes. A silo next to the barn contains an assault rifle, a carton of cigarettes, and a first aid box, with a ladder leading to a walkway holding two more ammunition boxes. Entering the silo may attract talon company mercenaries or regulators depending on one's reputation. The silo itself was added to the site as part of post-war developments and contains munitions and medical supplies alongside potentially stolen barrels of Aqua Pura.

topic_desc: The Followers of the Apocalypse maintain a discreet safehouse in the Mojave Wasteland, situated due west of Griffin Wares Sacked Caravan and south of Nevada 157. Access is granted only to those who have earned the deep trust of the organization, typically through Julie Farkas at the Old Mormon Fort in Freeside, who extends membership and a key to individuals regarded as allies of the Followers' humanitarian mission. The safehouse serves as a practical refuge for traveling members and trusted associates. It contains a workbench, safe storage lockers and footlockers, a radiation-free drinking fountain, and beds that provide genuine rest. Notable provisions include an advanced radiation suit, a tri-beam laser rifle, an all-purpose science suit, and a multiplas rifle, along with a copy of the D.C. Journal of Internal Medicine. Doctor Luria visits periodically, offering stimpaks, super stimpaks, or radiation supplies to those present. The safehouse reflects the Followers' ethos: modest, utilitarian, oriented toward healing and knowledge rather than defense, yet stocked with capable equipment for those operating in hostile territory.

topic_desc: The Dino Dee-lite Motel in Novac offers several rooms to travelers and residents, reflecting the town's character as a modest waypoint along the Mojave's southern trade routes. The rooms contain basic furnishings: beds, sofas, tables, chairs, televisions, and assorted containers, with irradiated water in the bathrooms typical of the region's degraded infrastructure. One upper-level room can be rented indefinitely from Jeannie May Crawford, the motel's proprietor, for one hundred caps, or provided at no cost to individuals who have earned an Accepted reputation in Novac. If Crawford is unavailable, Cliff Briscoe at the Dino Bite Gift Shop can arrange access. The room's bed is known to heal crippled limbs and provide restorative sleep, and its containers are reliable for long-term storage. Other rooms in the motel reveal glimpses of transient lives: one vacant first-floor room holds liquor and pre-war books, while a second-floor room shows evidence of chem use and violence, with bloodstains and surgical tubing scattered among personal effects. These details underscore the precarious existence of Novac's inhabitants and passers-through.

topic_desc: The Casa Madrid Apartments are a run-down residential building in Westside, situated across the street from Miguel's Pawn Shop. The building has been owned and managed by Marco for several years and caters to wasteland inhabitants who cannot afford accommodations on the New Vegas Strip. Residents receive a room and, if desired, access to the services of three prostitutes arranged through Pretty Sarah: Sweetie, Jimmy, and Maude. The building's ground floor includes Dermot's apartment, with an openly accessible door, and Saint James's residence, secured by an average-quality lock for which a key can be obtained from Sweetie. Mean Sonofabitch, a robot, stands guard by the entrance. The apartments reflect Westside's character as a working-class community existing on the margins of New Vegas's wealth, where residents scrape by through trade, labor, and informal economies. The building's modest quarters and the presence of transient tenants illustrate the stratification of Mojave society, where proximity to the Strip does not guarantee access to its prosperity.

topic_desc: Ranger Station Delta is a New California Republic outpost in the Mojave Wasteland, located southeast of Boulder City and northeast of Camp Forlorn Hope. The station was constructed atop the ruins of a pre-war farmstead, whose remnants remain visible. Its strategic purpose, as described by Ranger Pason, is to monitor the Colorado River and prevent crossings by Caesar's Legion forces. The station's command center operates from a tent, while a destroyed farmhouse nearby conceals a cellar containing a reloading bench, a locked gun cabinet with lower-grade weapons, and provisions consisting primarily of Sunset Sarsaparilla and foodstuffs. A detailed pre-war map of Hoover Dam and its surroundings hangs on the cellar wall; similar maps are distributed across all NCR ranger outposts as well as Camp Golf and Hoover Dam itself, underscoring the dam's central importance to NCR military planning. Comm Officer Scheffer and Ranger Pason staff the station. A robobrain belonging to Ranger Pason observes Hoover Dam from the site, equipped with a GBRM2KX memory chip. Southeast of the camp, a cliff descends to the river, where lakelurks inhabit a cove near submerged remains and explosive ordnance. The station exemplifies the NCR's forward-deployed reconnaissance doctrine, stretching its forces across difficult terrain to watch a vast frontier.

topic_desc: Ranger Station Bravo occupies a strategic position in the northeast Mojave, deliberately sited to watch for Legion movements that could bypass the main defenses at Hoover Dam by circling around Lake Mead. The base is a modest affair of trailers and shipping containers, with one container housing radio equipment and NCR propaganda posters. Despite its importance as the easternmost NCR installation in the wasteland, the station suffers from chronic supply mismanagement. Comm Officer Tilden has noted that the base receives regular shipments of ammunition when what they actually need is water, a logistical failure that reflects the broader strain on NCR supply lines across the Mojave. The station is typically guarded by two NCR Rangers, though veteran rangers may also be present depending on the operational tempo of the region. The surrounding area is not without danger; super mutants have been known to establish encampments nearby.

topic_desc: Cerulean Robotics is a derelict pre-War facility in northern Freeside, accessible through a narrow gap in concrete piles past a ruined store near the city wall. The building's interior is overrun by giant rats and contains four damaged Protectrons, remnants of the facility's original robotic operations. A Protectron programming interface terminal remains functional, though accessing it requires either considerable technical expertise or a terminal access card stored in a locked tool cabinet. The cabinet key can be found in the grasp of a skeleton near a television set in the break room, a grim indicator of the last days of the facility's occupants. The building has drawn interest from parties in Freeside for its intact robotics equipment, particularly the robot designated Fisto, which can be reprogrammed through the terminal. The facility also contains a reloading bench, workbench, scrap metal, and sensor modules, making it a useful if dangerous site for scavengers and technicians operating in Freeside.

topic_desc: Techatticup Mine, located at the turnaround point on the road past Nelson, was once a productive mining operation and tourist destination before the Great War ended such activities. In the post-War years, the mine found use as a dumping ground for nuclear waste, with barrels of radioactive debris stored in its chambers alongside the remains of those caught in the contamination. By 2281, the long-abandoned mine has been repurposed by Caesar's Legion as a forward holding camp. Decanus Alexus commands a force of approximately a dozen Legion troops distributed across the mine's winding passages. The main chamber, built around a large concentration of irradiated barrels and scattered skeletons, serves as the Legion's base of operations. Captured NCR soldiers are held in locked storage areas along the righthand passage, guarded by additional Legion troops. The mine's irradiated environment makes it a hazardous posting for both captors and captives alike.

topic_desc: Lone Wolf Radio is a derelict trailer parked against a rock wall south of Goodsprings and south-southwest of the Goodsprings Source. The trailer's interior tells a bleak story of isolation: scattered radio equipment, empty whiskey bottles, shot glasses, and a mattress suggest someone lived here alone for an extended period before succumbing to despair. The graffiti scrawled on the interior wall — "Everyone is gone. I am all alone. Let it all end" — and the exterior warning of "Keep out" paint a picture of a survivor who lost contact with the world and eventually lost hope. The trailer still contains useful scavenged components including scrap electronics and sensor modules. A short distance downhill from the trailer, a small basin of clean water sustains a cluster of broc flowers, and geckos have congregated around the water source, making the immediate vicinity hazardous for unwary travelers despite the trailer's relative seclusion.

topic_desc: The .32 Pistol is a compact revolver chambered for .32 Caliber Rounds, widely encountered throughout the Capital Wasteland. Raiders and wastelanders favor it for its availability and ease of use, though it is not regarded as a particularly formidable sidearm. A unique variant known as Wild Bill's Sidearm is both more powerful and more durable than the standard model, recovered from the body of Wild Bill. Another variant, the Concealed .32 Pistol, was smuggled into the Pitt by Wernher to bypass gate guards, converting into a standard pistol once the carrier reached Downtown. The weapon's real-world lineage traces to the Smith & Wesson Model 2 Double Action revolver from 1880. Notable individuals known to carry one include Flash and Timebomb of Big Town, James after departing Tranquility Lane, Jenny Stahl of Megaton, and several merchants and mercenaries across the wasteland. A grim discovery at Hubris Comics places one in a dead man's hand beside whiskey and Nuka-Cola Quantum, suggesting suicide.

topic_desc: The Hunting Shotgun is a pump-action shotgun chambered for 12 Gauge Rounds, engineered for greater range and power than comparable scatterguns. Its tubular magazine is loaded one shell at a time through the bottom, resulting in slower reloads, though this manual process can be interrupted mid-reload to fire if urgency demands it. The weapon can be fitted with a long tube magazine, expanding capacity from five to eight shells, and a choke modification that significantly tightens shot spread. A unique variant called Dinner Bell is awarded by Red Lucy of the Thorn upon completion of a challenging arena trial. The shotgun is found in diverse locations across the Mojave, from Bloodborne Cave and Bootjack Cavern to Vault 34 and the Old Nuclear Test Site. NCR Heavy Troopers and Veteran Rangers occasionally carry it, as do Great Khans, White Legs Storm-Drummers, and Lobotomites at the Big MT. The weapon's pump-action mechanism introduces a slight delay between shots, making it less rapid than the Riot Shotgun, which remains the superior choice for sustained close-quarters engagements.

topic_desc: The YCS/186 is a unique variant of the Gauss Rifle, distinguished by its improved accuracy and greater structural integrity compared to the standard model. It consumes four Microfusion Cells per shot rather than the five required by its conventional counterpart, making it marginally more economical in ammunition. Its sole disadvantage is a slightly increased weight of eight pounds over the standard seven. The weapon is fitted with a 3.5x magnification scope. The YCS/186 is recovered from a mercenary camp east of Brooks Tumbleweed Ranch, where a hostile mercenary wearing reinforced combat armor carries it and attacks on sight. Under certain anomalous conditions associated with the Wild Wasteland phenomenon, the mercenaries are replaced by alien beings who instead possess an Alien Blaster, rendering the YCS/186 unobtainable through that encounter. The weapon is regarded as one of the most devastating non-explosive armaments in the Mojave Wasteland. In hardcore conditions, a single shot consumes 0.4 pounds of ammunition at a combined cost of roughly twelve caps. Despite expending four cells per blast, only one drained Microfusion Cell can be recovered for recharging.

topic_desc: Girdershade is one of the smallest and most isolated settlements in the Capital Wasteland, situated under a highway overpass southwest of Evergreen Mills. It was founded by Sierra Petrovita, a young woman with an intense fascination for Nuka-Cola Quantum, who maintains a collection of the rare beverage. The only other human resident is Ronald Laren, a former wastelander who harbors romantic interest in Sierra and carries a unique shotgun known as the Kneecapper. A single brahmin rounds out the settlement's population. Despite its modest size, Girdershade's location places it near several notable landmarks; conversing with the residents yields knowledge of Evergreen Mills, the Dunwich Building, and the Nuka-Cola Plant. The settlement's isolation makes it vulnerable to wandering wasteland creatures, including yao guai and radscorpions at higher threat levels. Following major developments in the Capital Wasteland, Enclave forces have established a camp north of the settlement, occasionally sending soldiers and even deathclaws into the surrounding area.

topic_desc: La Maison Beauregard stands as a pre-war establishment in the Georgetown district of Washington, D.C., now a shell of its former self within the Capital Wasteland. The building's exterior walls have holes revealing broken cement floors on multiple levels, and the decorative stonework above the entrance has deteriorated significantly, though the sign itself remains in remarkably good condition. Inside, the ground-floor lobby features shattered flooring, damaged wallpaper, a desk with a cash register, and a landslide of debris blocking access to upper doors. A bar area with a flickering Nuka-Cola sign and a pool table with two white balls survive on the upper accessible level. The building is occupied by super mutants, including leveled specimens in the interior and two stationed in the courtyard, generally equipped with heavy ordnance such as miniguns and missile launchers. Notable items within include a mini nuke, a Stealth Boy, a bottle of Nuka-Cola Quantum, and a U.S. Army flamethrower manual. The building's limited accessibility, with most areas blocked by rubble, makes it a confined but dangerous location for any wastelander braving Georgetown's ruins.

topic_desc: Meresti Metro Station is a repurposed underground transit facility in the Capital Wasteland's Washington, D.C. metro network, serving as the headquarters and communal living space for the Family, a group that adopts a vampire-like lifestyle under the leadership of Vance and his wife Holly. The station has been extensively modified from its original configuration: the rail pit has been filled with debris and boarded over, creating a level floor upon which benches, tables, and beds have been arranged. The benches are organized in rows resembling church pews, with the elevated lobby functioning as a chancel from which Vance delivers addresses to his followers. Karl operates a small shop in the southwest corner, notably selling scrap metal in quantities useful for trade. Makeshift bedrooms are situated above Karl's shop, while Vance and Holly's private quarters lie along the western hallway leading to a blocked surface exit. The station has been completely severed from the rest of the metro tunnel network, accessible only through the Meresti Trainyard or an irradiated sewer manhole in Northwest Seneca Station. An electronically locked room within the station has been used to confine individuals, including Ian West.

topic_desc: Smith Casey's Garage is a derelict automotive repair facility in the Capital Wasteland, formerly operated by an individual named Smith Casey. The modest structure sits amid fallen trees and overgrown bramble, with both a standard door and a garage door on the same side. A military checkpoint is situated to the north, where automated defense units such as Mister Gutsy or Sentry robots may patrol. The interior consists of a single average-sized room with a service counter on the right side. Behind the counter lies an open safe and a mattress beside a skeleton, offering a rudimentary resting place. A switch near the counter opens a trap door in the floor, revealing the entrance to Vault 112, one of the few intact vaults in the Capital Wasteland. Mole rats and radroaches infest the interior. The garage's location places it along patrol routes used by Brotherhood Outcast units in the surrounding area. The site does not reset over time, making it suitable as a temporary shelter or storage location for wastelanders. Yao guai have been known to appear near the entrance when departing the premises.

topic_desc: The Prospector Saloon has stood in Goodsprings since before the war and took on its current role under Trudy's management around 2274, seven years before the events of 2281. The structure retains much of its original character, including a neon sign, a bar with a cash register, and a northern room with a jukebox and pool table. A small office behind the bar contains a locked terminal and floor safe where Trudy keeps records and supplies. A separate moonshine distillery, accessible only through a very easy-locked exterior entrance, holds fission batteries and other distilling materials. The saloon functions as the town's de facto meeting hall; it is where disputes are aired and where locals like Sunny Smiles and Easy Pete can regularly be found. Trudy also serves as the town's informal source of news, keeping a radio behind the bar, though it is often broken. Goodsprings settlers frequent the bar throughout the day, and the establishment remains the central landmark of the small Mojave community.

topic_desc: The Securitron Vault lies buried beneath the Fort, accessible only through a hatch that requires the Platinum Chip to open. Caesar's Legion has attempted to pry, drill, and blast the doors open without success, leaving the facility sealed. Inside, the vault is bathed in low-level radiation and defended by Protectrons, turrets, and sentry bots that can be partially deactivated via security terminals. The interior consists of generator rooms and long windowed corridors overlooking rows upon rows of dormant Securitrons. A central operations console can read the Platinum Chip's data to upgrade every Securitron to the Mark II operating system and activate the entire underground army. Mr. House maintains a terminal in the first room but lacks control over the facility's security systems. The vault represents a significant strategic asset in the Mojave, as the Securitron army within could dramatically shift the balance of power among the region's major factions. The facility's generators are critical to its operation; their destruction triggers radiation leaks and structural collapse, rendering the vault unusable.

topic_desc: The four Goodsprings Homes reflect the modest, self-sufficient lifestyle of the settlement's inhabitants. Three sit southeast of Doc Mitchell's house, while the fourth lies to the northwest. Each has a mailbox and a small plot of land where settlers grow Nevada agave, maize, prickly pear cactus, barrel cactus, and banana yucca. The interiors are furnished with pre-war appliances, including refrigerators, ovens, and first aid boxes. Home One, shared by Trudy and Sunny Smiles, contains a Chinese Army: Special Ops Training Manual and a single shotgun. Home Two belongs to Easy Pete and is notable for having an average-locked safe with pre-war money and a key hidden beneath it. Home Three is a simpler structure with a BB gun and Buffout on a desk. Home Four contains a Lad's Life magazine and a Sunset Sarsaparilla star bottle cap. Most items in the homes are considered owned property, reflecting the tight-knit community's respect for private possessions. Easy Pete's house is unusual in that its storage is unowned and serves as practical lodging for travelers passing through Goodsprings.

topic_desc: The Mojave Outpost Headquarters occupies a pre-war highway checkpoint on the Long 15, established to monitor travelers entering the long stretch of Interstate 15. Abandoned for over a century after the Great War, the site was eventually claimed by the New California Republic as its southeasternmost Mojave installation. Ranger Jackson holds command, overseeing protection of the I-15 south of Primm and Highway 95 up through the Camp Searchlight area. The headquarters building serves as the administrative hub where officers log and compile outpost traffic data, process clearance papers, and manage the growing backlog of caravans stalled by threats on the highway below. Major Knight operates the front desk, providing regional intelligence and repair services. The outpost's strategic position at the base of the valley, enclosed by rock walls and fortified with sandbags, makes it a critical chokepoint for NCR logistics and trade flowing into the Mojave from California. The Unification Monument at the northern end of the valley commemorates the NCR's expansion into the region. Satellite dishes on the headquarters and adjacent barracks provide communication links to other NCR installations.
topic_desc_basic: The Mojave Outpost Headquarters is an NCR administrative building at the Mojave Outpost, the southeasternmost NCR installation in the Mojave Wasteland. Ranger Jackson commands the outpost, and Major Knight runs the front desk. The building handles traffic logging, regional command, and coordination for NCR forces along the I-15 and Highway 95.
