topic_desc: Before the Great War, the United States was a global superpower whose culture revolved around mass consumption, corporate branding, and technological optimism. Companies like RobCo Industries, Vault-Tec Corporation, General Atomics, and Hornwright Industrial produced consumer robots, underground vaults, and automated mining equipment marketed to ordinary households. The national government promoted patriotism through legislation such as the "Patriotic Patriots of America True Patriotism Act" and maintained wartime censorship that enabled confiscation of seditious materials. As the Resource Wars intensified from 2052 onward, the economy strained under petroleum and uranium shortages. The government closed borders, dissolved the United Nations, suspended workman's compensation, and placed defense contractors under military command. Executive Order 99066 authorized the internment of Chinese-American citizens in concentration camps like the Turtledove Detention Camp in Maryland, with many disappearing into research facilities. Organized labor pushed back against corporations replacing workers with robotics, culminating in Automation Riots. Despite mounting shortages and food rationing, pre-War consumer culture maintained a facade of normalcy through media, advertising, and national pride, even as the nation moved toward nuclear annihilation on October 23, 2077.
topic_desc_basic: Pre-War America was a consumer-driven society shaped by national brands, mass media, and government propaganda. Corporations like RobCo, Vault-Tec, and General Atomics dominated daily life. Citizens purchased processed foods, household robots, and automobiles on credit. Wartime censorship allowed the government to confiscate seditious material, while defense contractors fell under military command. The culture prized patriotism, technological progress, and convenience even as global resources dwindled.
tags: automation riots,patriotic patriotism act,prewar consumer goods,resource wars economy,robco industries,vault-tec corporation,wartime censorship

topic_desc: By 2077, the Sino-American War had ground into a stalemate following the United States liberation of Anchorage with winterized T-51 Power Armor under General Constantine Chase. Media outlets reported billions wasted with no clear victor. Preparing for nuclear or biological attack, the president retreated to an oil rig off the West Coast in March 2077. On Saturday, October 23, the war both began and ended. At 00:03 EST, COMPACFLT identified submarines off the West Coast. At 09:13 EST, IONDS detected the first four missile launches and the United States moved to DEFCON 2. Four minutes later, NORAD confirmed strikes. Los Angeles was struck in the city center. Washington citizens received warnings only after the West Coast was destroyed. At 09:26 EST, the president ordered retaliatory strikes under scenario MX-CN91. Pennsylvania and New York were hit at 09:42 EST. By 09:47, facilities went offline. The Chinese stealth submarine Yangtze launched missiles at the East Coast. Las Vegas was spared a direct strike because Mr. House disabled or destroyed 68 of 77 incoming warheads. Electromagnetic pulses disabled communications, crippling emergency response. National Guard and first responders mobilized on the evening of October 22, but lack of centralized command and radiation sickness caused many to desert. The exchange lasted two hours and resulted in 7.54 billion deaths.
topic_desc_basic: The Great War was a global nuclear exchange on October 23, 2077, that ended the Sino-American War and killed an estimated 7.54 billion people. The two-hour exchange began when submarines were detected off the West Coast and missiles launched. Air raid sirens sounded across America. Most major cities were destroyed. Only those who reached Vault-Tec vaults survived in significant numbers. Society collapsed entirely.
tags: defcon two,great war 2077,mr house missile defense,nuclear exchange,october 23 2077,sino-american war,yangtze submarine

topic_desc: The food riots were incidents of civil unrest that erupted across the United States as decreasing food supplies led to government-imposed rationing. The White House belittled those protesting, claiming the president was suffering too, having to substitute cube steak for prime rib while relying on what was called the detestable Chateau Montrose 2043 wine. The crisis turned deadly in Roxbury, Boston, where a hungry crowd stormed a food bank. Soldiers guarding the location opened fire on the unarmed crowd, killing four and injuring eight. The incident was particularly notorious because soldiers were allegedly selecting targets in the crowd in advance and laughing as they did so. The food crisis presented an opportunity for the Vault-Tec Corporation to propose solutions. The company built facilities such as the Vault-Tec Agricultural Research Center to test automation of agriculture, and converted Vault 22 into a research center for experimental fertilizer and genetically modified plant organisms. These efforts represented the intersection of corporate ambition and government desperation in the final years before the Great War, as the nation's resource crisis deepened and public trust in institutions eroded.
topic_desc_basic: As food supplies dwindled before the Great War, the United States government imposed rationing, triggering civil unrest known as the food riots. The White House dismissed protesters, claiming the president himself suffered by substituting cube steak for prime rib. In Roxbury, Boston, soldiers guarding a food bank opened fire on an unarmed crowd, killing four and injuring eight. Vault-Tec attempted agricultural solutions at facilities like Vault 22.

topic_desc: The Sierra Madre Casino was the brainchild of Frederick Sinclair, who invested the last of his savings into its construction as a grand resort in the mountains. The casino was designed as a trap for Dean Domino, a pre-war entertainer whose greed Sinclair was aware of; Domino orchestrated many of the financial losses Sinclair faced during construction. The casino's gala opening never occurred, as the Great War intervened, leaving the resort sealed and frozen in time for two centuries. The interior is divided into several sections: the Cantina Madrid restaurant and kitchen, the casino floor with blackjack, roulette, and slots, the Tampico theatre where legendary entertainers including Vera Keyes and Dean Domino performed, the Executive Suites for guest lodging, and a basement vault containing gold bars and pre-war money. Security holograms patrol the casino floor and suites, powered by emitters that can be disabled. The casino's vending machines accept Sierra Madre chips, and a holographic cashier exchanges pre-war money for chips. The Cloud, a toxic rust-colored gas, has seeped into portions of the building, particularly the Executive Suites.
topic_desc_basic: The Sierra Madre Casino is the centerpiece of the Sierra Madre resort, a grand pre-war casino and hotel frozen in time since its gala opening never took place. It features a casino floor with gaming tables and machines, the Cantina Madrid restaurant, the Tampico theatre, executive suites accessed by elevator, and a basement vault guarded by automated turrets. The casino remains sealed and patrolled by holographic security.

topic_desc: The Executive Suites of the Sierra Madre Casino were intended to provide luxurious accommodations for the resort's guests but now stand in advanced decay after two centuries of abandonment. The floor is a linear maze of interconnected rooms, some accessible only through holes blasted through adjoining walls, suggesting violent entry or structural collapse over time. The Cloud, the Sierra Madre's toxic atmospheric hazard, has infiltrated portions of the hallways. Three holograms modeled after Vera Keyes patrol the corridors, their emitters concealed behind doors in suites at the northeast, northwest, and southwest corners of the floor. A service room contains laundry machines, a workbench, and terminals connected to the hotel's maintenance network. A security room holds a hunting shotgun, an automatic rifle, suits of Sierra Madre armor, and ammunition stores. Vera Keyes' personal suite contains her remains, still dressed in her signature outfit, surrounded by syringes of Med-X, suggesting she died there during or shortly after the war. The suite also contains a chemistry set and access to an elevator leading toward the vault.
topic_desc_basic: The Executive Suites are the guest lodging area of the Sierra Madre Casino, accessed via elevator from the main lobby. The suites are in significant disrepair, with the Cloud seeping through hallways and holes blown through adjoining walls. The area is patrolled by holograms of Vera Keyes. Notable rooms include a service room with laundry machines and a workbench, a security room stocked with weapons and Sierra Madre armor, a kitchen, and Vera Keyes' personal suite.

topic_desc: The Sierra Madre Lobby functions as the primary nexus of the Sierra Madre resort, connecting the casino floor, Cantina Madrid restaurant, the Tampico theatre, and the Executive Suites via an elevator near the top of curved stairs. The lobby's receptionist terminal on the welcome desk can activate a greeter hologram once the appropriate security codes are retrieved from terminals in the Tampico, the Cantina Madrid kitchen, and the Executive Suites service room. With all three codes, the greeter can be upgraded to a security hologram capable of engaging hostile intruders. The lobby contains active speakers, some of which are shielded and cannot be deactivated until the casino floor has been dealt with. Recordings of Vera Keyes' songs, including 'Begin Again,' 'Go to the Faraway,' and 'Let the Bright Tomorrow in,' are accessible through the receptionist terminal. Ghost People, the hostile mutated inhabitants of the Sierra Madre villa, are known to breach the lobby despite its sealed entryway, with banging audible from the main doors. The lobby's chandelier is a notable architectural feature of the space.
topic_desc_basic: The Sierra Madre Lobby is the central nexus of the Sierra Madre resort, directing guests to the casino, restaurant, theatre, and Executive Suites. It features a welcome desk with a receptionist's terminal, curved stairs leading to the elevator, and a grand chandelier. Active speakers are present throughout. The lobby serves as a hub connecting all major sections of the resort.

topic_desc: The Northern Passage is a cave system situated north of North Vegas Square in the Mojave Wasteland, occupying the same geographical location as the real-world June Bug Mine at the foot of Gass Peak, bordering North Las Vegas, Nevada. June Bug Mine historically served as a municipal fallout shelter. The passage serves as the primary overland route connecting the Mojave Wasteland to Zion Canyon, and is used by the Happy Trails Caravan Company as the staging point for their trade expeditions northward. The actual route between the Mojave and Zion follows northbound Interstate 15, as referenced in Happy Trails expedition broadcasts. Inside the cave, wooden supports and hanging lanterns line the passage, with a Happy Trails shipping crate for storing goods during transit. The caravan expedition, led by boss Jed Masterson, includes hired hands such as Stella and Ricky, along with caravan guards. The passage was initially inaccessible due to a barrier of fallen rocks, which were cleared to allow caravan travel. A grave and a hollowed-out rock containing minor supplies can be found near the entrance, the latter bearing the cryptic inscription 'the sun is killing me.'
topic_desc_basic: The Northern Passage is a cave location north of North Vegas Square in the Mojave Wasteland. It serves as the route to Zion Canyon, used by the Happy Trails Caravan Company for their expeditions. The cave entrance is marked by a hollowed-out rock inscribed with the words 'the sun is killing me.' Banana yucca plants grow nearby. Before caravan expeditions began, the passage was blocked by fallen rocks.

topic_desc: The sniper rifle is one of the most effective long-distance weapons available in the Capital Wasteland, firing .308 rounds from a detachable box magazine. Its integrated scope enables precise engagement from elevated positions, though the weapon's mechanical complexity and relative scarcity make maintenance a constant concern; a rifle in full condition can fire roughly eighty-three rounds before requiring significant repair. Several variants exist. The Victory Rifle is functionally identical in damage but is more durable and knocks targets down on critical hits, at the cost of a reduced critical chance. The Reservist's Rifle, carried by members of a pre-war military reserve unit, holds only three rounds but fires faster with less recoil. Sniper rifles appear throughout the wasteland in the hands of raiders at Bethesda Ruins, Talon Company mercenaries at their recon camp near Arlington Library, Chinese Remnant soldiers at Mama Dolice's, and the defender of Minefield known as Arkansas. The Brotherhood of Steel's Knight Captain Dusk employs one, as does Allistair Tenpenny from his tower. The weapon's scarcity means that wasteland scavengers and merchants who stock one can command a premium price.
topic_desc_basic: The sniper rifle is a precision long-range firearm chambered for .308 ammunition, favored by raiders, mercenaries, and trained marksmen across the Capital Wasteland. Its scoped design allows engagement of targets at considerable distances, though a crippled arm severely disrupts aim. The rifle is relatively scarce, and heavy use demands regular merchant repairs. Notable users include Allistair Tenpenny and Knight Captain Dusk of the Brotherhood of Steel.

topic_desc: The AEP7 laser pistol represents a significant advancement in pre-war directed-energy weapons development. Researchers at the Citadel believed its improved design, featuring a new photonic focusing chamber and a redesigned focusing crystal pattern, put the weapon on track to replace the N99 10mm pistol as the standard military sidearm. Brotherhood Outcast researcher J. T. Benning noted that laser weaponry was produced in small runs of prototypes by the United States Armed Forces, and that the pistol's low recoil made long-range engagements easier for soldiers. The weapon draws power from Energy Cells and is notably durable, capable of firing approximately 729 shots from full condition before breaking. Several unique variants exist in the Capital Wasteland. Colonel Autumn carries a distinctive laser pistol. Protectron's Gaze is a variant associated with the Mechanist. Smuggler's End is carried by Elder Lyons of the Brotherhood of Steel. The pistol sees widespread use among Brotherhood of Steel soldiers, Enclave personnel, and various wasteland inhabitants including Armitage, the Mechanist, Tinker Joe, and William Brandice. Its beam can ignite gas leaks, adding a secondary hazard to its already lethal output.
topic_desc_basic: The AEP7 laser pistol is a pre-war energy weapon developed by the United States Armed Forces to replace the overheating-prone AEP5 model. It features a redesigned photonic focusing chamber and crystal pattern with reduced weight and bulk. Both the Brotherhood of Steel and the Enclave use it as a standard sidearm. Fatal critical hits reduce targets to ash without damaging their equipment.

topic_desc: The Gatling laser is a formidable heavy energy weapon that uses multiple barrels firing in rotating sequence to project a continuous stream of laser beams, avoiding the rapid overheating that plagues simpler laser designs. Despite its name, the barrels do not rotate in the manner of a traditional Gatling gun; instead, they fire in a rotating order, eliminating the wind-up delay associated with conventional miniguns. This makes the weapon quicker to deploy in combat. The Gatling laser is capable of engaging vertibirds, making it one of the few portable weapons that can threaten aerial targets. In the Capital Wasteland, the weapon is most commonly associated with the Brotherhood of Steel, the Brotherhood Outcasts, and Enclave soldiers, who carry it in areas around the Washington Monument, Fort Independence, Arlington Library, and the Citadel. Super Mutant Overlords have also been observed wielding Gatling lasers, particularly on approaches to the National Guard Depot. The weapon is rare without significant Enclave activity in the region. The unique variant Vengeance offers greater damage output at the cost of durability, while the Precision Gatling Laser features an exceptionally high critical multiplier. The weapon can fire approximately 3,125 beams before breaking.
topic_desc_basic: The Gatling laser is a heavy directed-energy weapon using multiple rotating barrels to fire a sustained stream of laser beams without rapid overheating. It is among the most advanced heavy weapons in the Capital Wasteland. The Brotherhood of Steel, Brotherhood Outcasts, and Enclave forces all employ it. Super Mutant Overlords have also been observed carrying them. A unique variant known as Vengeance is more powerful but less durable.

topic_desc: The frag grenade is the most common explosive ordnance encountered in the Capital Wasteland, serving as a versatile anti-personnel tool for raiders, Super Mutants, smugglers, and other combatants. Its blast deals significant damage with a high probability of crippling limbs, making it effective at disabling fleeing or charging targets. The grenade's interaction with physics allows skilled throwers to bounce it around corners or through doorways to reach enemies behind cover. Frag grenades are found in caches throughout the wasteland, including Shalebridge, Meresti Metro Station, L.O.B. Enterprises, Hamilton's Hideaway, and the Chryslus Building basement. The weapon's cultural footprint is notable: Super Mutants call grenades "hot potatoes," and Swampfolk in Point Lookout refer to them as "pineapples," reflecting the grenade's rough resemblance to the fruit. A virtually limitless supply can be obtained through trade with Protector Casdin at Fort Independence, who accepts energy weapons, scrap metal, sensor modules, and power armor in exchange. Damaged frag grenades can sometimes be found and repaired with other damaged grenades, though they produce reduced blast yield. The safety lever design prevents accidental detonation while the grenade is held after the pin is pulled.
topic_desc_basic: The frag grenade is a standard thrown explosive producing a powerful blast with a high likelihood of crippling limbs. Raiders and Super Mutants commonly carry them as a ranged option when melee engagement is impractical. Thrown grenades are affected by physics and may bounce or roll unpredictably. Super Mutants refer to them as "hot potatoes," while Swampfolk call them "pineapples."

topic_desc: The Z-9 Crotalus DNA Preservation Lab stands as a testament to the reckless genetic experimentation conducted at Big MT before the war. Named after Crotalus, a genus of venomous pit vipers commonly known as rattlesnakes, the facility was central to Dr. Borous's nightstalker project—a hybrid creature created by splicing rattlesnake DNA into another species. The lab's layout reflects its dual purpose: containment and research. Holding cells line one corridor, each containing cages with egg clutches, suggesting active breeding programs. The main laboratory area features computing equipment, chemistry sets, and operating tables strewn with surgical instruments such as bone saws and tweezers, indicating live dissection and experimentation. A caged observation area allowed researchers to study specimens directly. The presence of a unique nightstalker specimen designated Shadis in the main lab suggests the facility continued producing or housing notable variants. The lab also contains an Auto-Doc upgrade component, specifically Implant Y-3, left on an operating table—evidence that the facility's medical technology was repurposed or under development alongside the biological research. Lobotomite corpses and scattered supplies indicate later occupation or incursion by the Think Tank's experimental subjects.
topic_desc_basic: The Z-9 Crotalus DNA Preservation Lab is a Big MT facility situated northwest of the X-8 Research Center. It houses numerous nightstalkers and contains holding cells with egg clutches, a laboratory area with medical equipment, and a caged observation section. Dr. Borous conducted research here that led to the creation of nightstalkers by splicing rattlesnake DNA. An Auto-Doc upgrade component can be found on one of the operating tables.

topic_desc: The X-7a "Left Field" Artillery Launch represents Big MT's pre-war military testing infrastructure, designed to evaluate artillery systems against the X-7b "Boom Town" Target Zone. The facility's fixed artillery guns are miniaturized versions of those used at the Anchorage artillery overlook, reflecting the Think Tank's involvement in military applications. A command console allows test firing of the guns, which can be activated repeatedly, each detonation carving a crater in the target zone. The site bears signs of post-war activity: a military truck has crashed through the command center wall, killing at least one occupant, and the blue Old World flag painted on the command room door is attributed to Ulysses, suggesting the courier passed through this location. The area is defended by an RY-589 Ultimo Bot, a sophisticated security automaton carrying a LAER weapon, alongside Y-17 Trauma Override Harness teams—remnants of Big MT's medical experimentation programs that continue to function autonomously. The presence of proton throwing axes and explosives documentation suggests later visitors attempted to repurpose the facility. The command center plays music identical to that found in the Sierra Madre vault, an unexplained connection between Big MT and the Sierra Madre.
topic_desc_basic: The X-7a "Left Field" Artillery Launch is a Big MT facility located in the southwest of the crater. It features fixed artillery guns controlled from a command center, which can fire upon the X-7b "Boom Town" Target Zone. The area is guarded by an RY-589 Ultimo Bot and patrolled by Y-17 Trauma Override Harness units. A military truck has crashed through the command center's wall. The door to the command room bears an Old World flag painted in blue by Ulysses.

topic_desc: The Long 15 occupies a section of pre-war Interstate 15, serving as a critical NCR logistical corridor and military checkpoint controlling access to the Mojave Wasteland. The Ranger Unification Treaty monument is visible from the area, underscoring its proximity to significant NCR historical sites. The location's destruction came through nuclear warheads launched from the Divide, transforming the military installation into an irradiated crater emitting approximately twenty rads per second at its edge. The blast ghoulified the NCR garrison, producing Irradiated Heavy Troopers and Glowing Trooper Ghouls from soldiers who had been wearing salvaged power armor. Colonel Royez, the commanding officer, survived in a ghoulified state and retained his plasma caster and Scorched Sierra Power Armor. The presence of crashed vertibirds bearing Enclave markings from Navarro rather than standard NCR insignia raises questions about the aircraft's provenance, possibly connecting to Enclave remnants or salvaged hardware. The destroyed camp includes a firing range, medical aid station, and numerous supply caches containing ammunition and equipment in quantities unusual for the Mojave. Burnt silhouettes of vaporized personnel mark the firing range wall, grim evidence of the blast's intensity. The area also contains the remains of children among ruined buildings, hidden beyond the accessible zone.
topic_desc_basic: The Long 15 is a stretch of pre-war Interstate 15 used by the New California Republic as a minor military base and checkpoint for travelers entering and leaving the Mojave Wasteland. Following a nuclear strike launched from the Divide, the area became a irradiated wasteland populated by ghoulified NCR troopers and their commanding officer, Colonel Royez. Crashed vertibirds bearing Enclave markings from Navarro litter the destroyed camp.

topic_desc: The Hopeville Missile Silo Bunker is a sprawling pre-war military installation within the Divide, reflecting the strategic importance of the Hopeville area as a missile deployment site. The facility spans multiple levels, with a central silo housing an intact missile and supporting infrastructure including reactor rooms, utility areas, and storage spaces. Security was managed through automated sentry bots and turrets, with access controlled by General Martin Retslaf, whose body remains at his desk on the top level alongside his terminal and silo network security codes. Retslaf's US Army General Outfit and security holotapes indicate he was the ranking officer at the time of the facility's abandonment or catastrophe. The bunker contains a broken duraframe eyebot near the silo door, and a bot pod capable of interfacing with an ED-E unit, suggesting the facility had connections to advanced robotics programs. Arc welders found near Marked Men corpses on the mainframe control level indicate that these mutated survivors of the Divide have occupied or passed through the facility. The presence of Nuka-Cola Quartz, Dean's Electronics, and an H&H Tools Nail Gun among the supplies suggests the bunker was partially stocked for extended occupation. After the Divide's events, Marked Men are known to shelter within the bunker's multiple levels.
topic_desc_basic: The Hopeville Missile Silo Bunker is a large military facility in the Divide, extending across the northern map. It contains a missile silo, maintenance areas, and a central computer system capable of restoring power to the building. The body of US Army General Martin Retslaf can be found on the top level behind his desk. The facility also contains a broken duraframe eyebot and sentry bot security systems.

topic_desc: In the aftermath of the Great War, the collapse of organized governments and standing armies created a vacuum filled in part by mercenaries—individuals who offer their martial skills for payment. These hired guns operate across the Capital Wasteland and the Mojave, taking contracts from settlements, merchants, and factions needing protection or enforcement. Some mercenaries work independently, while others organize into companies or bands that can field multiple fighters for larger operations. The profession attracts former soldiers, drifters, and those with combat training who have no other livelihood in the devastated economy. Mercenaries are generally viewed with suspicion by common wastelanders, as their loyalty extends only as far as their pay, but their services remain in constant demand given the pervasive dangers of raiders, wildlife, and factional conflict.
topic_desc_basic: Mercenaries are individuals who act as soldiers for hire throughout the wasteland. They sell their combat skills to the highest bidder, taking on dangerous jobs that settlements, factions, or individuals need done. Mercenary work is a common profession in the lawless post-war world, where organized military forces are scarce and threats are numerous.

topic_desc: Gambling persisted after the Great War as both entertainment and economic activity. Pre-war casino games like blackjack, roulette, craps, and slot machines continue to operate in post-war establishments, particularly in centers like New Reno and the New Vegas Strip. New forms emerged as well, most notably Caravan, a two-player card game played throughout the Mojave Wasteland using decks built from traditional playing card sets. Caravan players build three caravans of numbered cards, aiming for values between 21 and 26. Beyond casino games, wastelanders bet on arena combat—The Thorn outside New Vegas hosts fights between wasteland creatures, while boxing rings operate in places like New Reno and Junktown. The prevalence of gambling reflects both the scarcity economy of the wasteland, where fortunes can change on a single wager, and the enduring human desire for entertainment amid hardship. Casinos and gambling halls serve as social hubs where caps, goods, and information change hands alongside bets.
topic_desc_basic: Gambling is a popular form of entertainment in the wasteland, surviving from before the Great War and evolving into new forms. Wastelanders wager money or valuables on games of chance and skill, from casino staples like blackjack, roulette, and slot machines to post-war inventions like Caravan, a card game popular throughout the Mojave Wasteland. Settlements such as New Reno and New Vegas are known centers of gambling activity.

topic_desc: Before the Great War, water was part of municipal services affected by polluted industrial runoff. After the war, drinkable water sources became contaminated by radiation, making purification essential for survival. The bottle cap emerged as post-war currency backed by water, underscoring its fundamental importance. In the Capital Wasteland, the Potomac River remained irradiated until efforts by Rivet City scientists to activate Project Purity, a facility designed to cleanse the river on a massive scale. Megaton's robot butler Wadsworth produced purified water through condensation, while Tenpenny Tower and certain Vault-Tec facilities dispensed rad-free water from their infrastructure. In the Mojave, water's scarcity made it a catalyst for war. Hoover Dam provided nearly limitless clean water from Lake Mead and the Colorado River, making it the prize in the First Battle of Hoover Dam in 2277 between Caesar's Legion and the New California Republic, and again in the Second Battle four years later. Smaller communities devised their own solutions: the Boomers maintained a filtration system at Nellis, the King controlled Freeside's water pump, and Westside implemented small-scale irrigation with help from engineer Tom Anderson and the Followers of the Apocalypse. The NCR's sharecropper farms near New Vegas suffered from the Office of Science and Industry underproviding their water allocation by twenty percent, threatening crop yields. Vaults were equipped with Water Chips for reclamation, though these degraded over time and required replacement.
topic_desc_basic: Water is among the most contested resources in the post-war wasteland. Most natural sources are contaminated by radiation, making clean water scarce and valuable. Wastelanders purify water through methods ranging from simple boiling to large-scale industrial systems. The bottle cap, the dominant post-war currency, is backed by water. Drinking untreated water increases radiation levels and can prove fatal over time.

topic_desc: Super Mutants originate from Forced Evolutionary Virus research begun at West Tek and transferred to Mariposa Military Base in January 2077. The original mutants were created by the Master, who sought to unify the wasteland under a single mutant race. In the Capital Wasteland, Vault 87's Evolutionary Experimentation Program produced a distinct strain beginning in 2078. These mutants grow larger and stronger with age, are sterile, and became a permanent presence, raiding to kidnap humans for conversion with FEV, or green stuff. By 2277, Vault 87 mutants were running low on the virus and searching desperately for new sources. In the Mojave, Marcus, a former Unity super mutant, founded a settlement at Black Mountain, using the site's radiation as a deterrent to humans. A rift developed between Marcus and Tabitha, a Nightkin officer whose mental state deteriorated after her robot companion Rhonda broke down. Clashes between Nightkin and first-generation mutants became commonplace, and Marcus left to establish Jacobstown, a haven for first-generation Super Mutants and Nightkin. Doctor Henry conducted research there into curing Nightkin mental illnesses caused by Stealth Boy use. Black Mountain became the center of the State of Utobitha under Tabitha's command, where hostile Nightkin and second-generation mutants harassed travelers along I-15. Some politicians in the NCR campaigned on anti-mutant platforms, and mutants elsewhere faced attack, capture, and torture.
topic_desc_basic: Super Mutants are humanoid mutants created by exposing humans to variants of the Forced Evolutionary Virus. They possess exceptional strength, endurance, and resistance or immunity to disease and radiation, though their intelligence is often modified. Different strains exist across the wasteland, created at separate facilities including Mariposa Military Base and Vault 87. Super Mutants have formed communities of varying organization and hostility.

topic_desc: Cottonwood Crater is one of the few atomic impact sites in the Mojave Wasteland. During the Great War, seventy-seven nuclear warheads were launched at Las Vegas and the surrounding area. Fifty-nine were disarmed mid-flight by defense systems installed by the pre-war businessman Mr. House, nine were destroyed by a laser defense system atop the Lucky 38 Hotel and Casino, and the remaining nine struck the surrounding desert. Cottonwood Crater marks one of these impact points. The site overlooks Cottonwood Cove from elevated terrain to the south and is connected to Fire Root Cavern to the north. The crater contains highly radioactive pools of water, with radiation levels reaching approximately twenty rads per second of exposure. Golden geckos are drawn to the irradiated environment. The remains of a dead prospector have been reported on a rock along the western edge of the crater, though accounts of what the prospector carried vary. The location is notoriously difficult to reach on foot, typically accessed either by traversing precarious cliff terrain or by emerging from Fire Root Cavern and following a narrow peninsula.
topic_desc_basic: Cottonwood Crater is an atomic bomb impact site in the Mojave Wasteland, situated in the southern mountains overlooking Cottonwood Cove. It lies east of Searchlight Airport and connects northward to Fire Root Cavern. The area is highly irradiated, with radioactive pools reaching up to 20 rads per second. Golden geckos are known to inhabit the crater.

topic_desc: The Basincreek Building was a pre-war office complex in the Mojave Wasteland that experienced a string of mundane yet memorable misfortunes before the Great War. A car lost control and crashed into the building. The sanitary facilities suffered repeated flooding incidents, and at one point the wall of the men's bathroom was broken into. The building also endured a deadly ant infestation and a pervasive bad odor caused by a rat that died within the walls of one of the offices. During the pre-war period, an individual working in the building locked themselves inside an office and could not find the key, slipping a desperate note under the door pleading for someone to call the police. In the post-war era, the building is occupied by giant soldier ants, giant worker ants, and radroaches. The first floor contains two bathrooms, one of which is inaccessible due to a jammed door behind which a broken pipe gushes water. A note titled Help Me! can be found on the ground in front of an easy-locked door at the rear of the building. The structure's second floor is partially accessible through a gap behind the receptionist's desk.
topic_desc_basic: The Basincreek Building is a pre-war office structure in the Mojave Wasteland, located south of the West Pump Station and west of the Allied Technologies Offices. It is now inhabited by giant ants and radroaches.

topic_desc: Ivanpah Dry Lake is a desolate expanse in the Mojave Wasteland located south of Primm and east of the Nevada Highway Patrol Station. The terrain is largely flat and featureless, characteristic of a dry lake bed. The main point of interest is a small hill at the center of the area, where a burned-out vehicle rests with a suitcase in the back seat and a stash toolbox nearby. A harvestable honey mesquite pod grows on the hill. The surrounding ground supports sparse desert vegetation, including barrel cactus and jalapeño pepper plants. Wildlife in the vicinity includes bark scorpions and giant ants that patrol the area. Despite its sparse appearance, the location's map marker icon suggests an active settlement rather than a natural landmark, which has led to some confusion among travelers. The dry lake bed is named after the real-world Ivanpah Lake, a dry lake bed in Clark County, Nevada.

topic_desc: The Mesmetron was developed before the Great War by Implied Hypnotics, Inc. as an experimental non-lethal subjugation device intended for United States military use. The weapon operates by transmitting a series of waves that the brain attempts to decode, but the resulting neural static overwhelms the synapses, causing confusion and the shutdown of higher-level mental functions and voluntary motor control. This leaves the target extremely susceptible to suggestion. The device was still in its testing phase during the war and exhibited two serious undesirable side effects: extremely increased aggression in the target, and a resonant brain wave feedback loop that resulted in spontaneous cranial eruption. Despite its prototypical nature, several Mesmetron units were attached to Robobrains to assist in interrogation processes, with official documentation acknowledging a ten to fifteen percent casualty rate due to cranial eruption. In the Capital Wasteland, a Mesmetron was scavenged from an old military base and is associated with the slaver operations at Paradise Falls. The device is considered invaluable to slavers, as it renders targets senseless and easy to collar. However, the Mesmetron's waves interfere with slave collar radio signals, causing collars to detonate if the device is used on someone already wearing one. A variant known as the Microwave Emitter, designed for lethal rather than subjugation purposes, was developed and can be found at the St. Aubin Medical Facility in Point Lookout.
topic_desc_basic: The Mesmetron is an experimental pre-war non-lethal subjugation device developed by Implied Hypnotics, Inc. for the United States military. The device was still in testing when the war began and was known to cause spontaneous cranial eruption in some subjects.

topic_desc: Before the convict breakout, Primm had developed into a promising trade town as the NCR expanded into the Mojave. Its strategic location along Interstate 15 made it a natural stopping point for travelers and merchants moving between California and Las Vegas. However, when prisoners from the NCR Correctional Facility broke out, trade ceased and residents were forced to shelter in the Vikki and Vance Casino. The NCR's 5th Battalion established a camp southwest of town, but their presence served primarily to prevent convicts from pushing further south toward the Mojave Outpost rather than to protect Primm itself. Lieutenant Hayes led a squad of NCR troopers holding a barricade on the western overpass. The town's governance and law enforcement remained in flux, with the sheriff's office standing empty and the community's future uncertain. Merchants like Samuel and Michelle abandoned Primm for the 188 Trading Post, further diminishing the town's economic prospects. The NCR's inability to secure Primm highlighted the broader strain on its military resources across the Mojave.
topic_desc_basic: Primm is an independent settlement in the Mojave Wasteland along Interstate 15. The question of who would serve as Primm's law enforcement remained a pressing concern for the community's future stability.

topic_desc: The Followers of the Apocalypse originated from San Diego, near the Glow, founded by former vault dwellers who moved north to escape spreading sickness. Nicole, who lost her parents during the journey, established the organization with the goal of making the wasteland "the way it used to be, before the war." The group is not religious but guided by principles of sharing knowledge and resources to build a world free from war and poverty. In the Boneyard, they established operations in the Boneyard Library, offering free classes and engaging in research on pre-War history and tribal culture. In the Mojave, Julie Farkas administers a regional hub at the Old Mormon Fort in Freeside, emphasizing "the free exchange of ideas." The Followers undertake research on alternative medicines from desert flora, assist communities like Westside with desert agriculture, and help install water pumps. Dr. Usanagi leads a medical clinic providing low-cost services and implants, using profits to purchase additional supplies. The group relies on trading, routine medical charges, and charitable donations, offering discounts in exchange for medicine donations. Their anti-authoritarian tendencies leave them with weak hierarchy, with members ranging from anarcho-syndicalists to social democrats in composition. The average NCR citizen views them as unpatriotic for tending to outsiders rather than helping back home.
topic_desc_basic: The Followers of the Apocalypse are a humanitarian organization founded by former vault dwellers near the Glow. By 2280, they maintained outposts in every major city within the New California Republic, focusing on teaching agriculture, crop rotation, and pre-War survival techniques.

topic_desc: The Sorrows' religion originated when the first Sorrows, a group of literate English-speaking children who had escaped "The School," began receiving notes and gifts signed "the Father" in Zion's Narrows. Early gifts were story books, later replaced by medical texts and weapon manuals. The Father's notes offered both practical advice and spiritual guidance, telling the children that Zion was his gift—an apology for the sorrows of their lives and the Great War. The Father eventually sent a final note with personal messages for each member, announcing he would step back but maintain a silent vigil. The Sorrows venerate not only the Father but also his wife and son. Murals throughout Zion depict the Father, including scenes of him driving Vault 22 dwellers from the canyon. The caves where the Father dwelt are sacred and taboo to enter, marked with white hand prints; those who seek them out are believed to be taken from this world. The Sorrows believe that individuals who die before their naming day become restless ghosts wandering the earth. Daniel, a New Canaanite missionary, has attempted to convert the Sorrows to Mormonism, but they have syncretized the Father with God, Sylvie with Mary, and Michael with Jesus Christ, blending both faiths rather than fully adopting either. The Sorrows' funerary rites involve interring their dead on raised wooden structures at Burial Mounds, surrounded by grave goods and burial murals.
topic_desc_basic: The Sorrows are a tribe living in Zion Canyon whose culture centers on worship of a spirit called "the Father in the Cave." The Sorrows believe that when they die, the river carries their water to the next life to be with the Father. Their faith is overseen by the Shaman White Bird.

topic_desc: Holotapes, also called holodisks or holo-discs, were manufactured-crystal storage devices developed by Wattz Electronics using tape holography technology beginning in 2063. They quickly became the dominant pre-War information storage medium, available in multiple compatible variants. Data was organized into "blocks" with a capacity of 256 blocks per tape, and actual storage depended on data compression. Early models averaged between 64 and 128 kilobytes, with some holding only 256 kilobytes, but by 2077 the latest models could store up to 4 terabytes. G.E.C.K. units were advertised as including a holotape with an abridged Library of Congress. Beyond data storage, specialized holotape models carried entertainment—music, movies, and games—with dedicated players for displaying high-resolution volumetric images. Holo Generators created THT entertainment tape players, though many ceased functioning after the war. Holotapes could be played on RobCo terminals equipped with holotape players. In the post-War era, holotapes remain a critical medium for preserving and transmitting knowledge, with their durability allowing information to survive for extended periods in harsh wasteland conditions.
topic_desc_basic: Holotapes are laser-readable storage devices produced by Wattz Electronics, based on Tape Holography Technology. Early models stored as little as 64 kilobytes, while the latest 2077 models could hold up to 4 terabytes. Holotapes could store transmissions, software backups, entertainment, and reference materials, and can be played on terminals.

topic_desc: Jack Rabbit Springs consists of five irradiated hot springs arranged around a small hill topped by two poles. The location sits south of the Prospector's Den and northeast of Ivanpah Dry Lake in the Mojave Wasteland. The springs are heavily contaminated, emitting radiation that necessitates protective measures such as radiation suits and Rad-X for anyone attempting to explore the area. A radiation suit can be found cached nearby in the Hidden Supply Cave to the east. The springs and surrounding terrain are inhabited by centaurs, evolved centaurs, and at least one super mutant master encamped against the mountains, sometimes accompanied by additional super mutants. The pools themselves exhibit unusual properties, notably failing to ripple when struck by projectiles. The geography resembles the real-world Jack Rabbit Spring within Ash Meadows National Wildlife Refuge in Nye County, Nevada. Scattered supplies including ammunition boxes and a Stealth Boy have been reported on the central hill.
topic_desc_basic: Jack Rabbit Springs is a cluster of irradiated hot springs in the Mojave Wasteland, situated south of the Prospector's Den and northeast of Ivanpah Dry Lake. Centaurs and super mutants have been known to inhabit the vicinity, making it hazardous for travelers.

topic_desc: The Camp McCarran Concourse occupies the space between the Terminal Building and the Supply Shack at Camp McCarran, the NCR's primary military installation in the Mojave Wasteland. Before the Great War, these open-air buildings provided passengers with access to airplanes. The NCR has since repurposed the concourse into troop quarters and support facilities. Private Morales can typically be found seated among inoperable slot machines near the entrance. The concourse contains several partitioned sections with additional rows of defunct slot machines, a medical area in the far southern corner equipped with gurneys, partitions, and displayed x-rays, and a sleeping area with bunks, lockers, and a pool table. A dining area serves food and drinks, managed by Corporal William Farber. Long hallways extend outward to connect the concourse with the terminal building and supply shack. The concourse is subdivided into Concourse Gates A, B, and C, a mess hall, kitchens, and a lower concourse level. Dr. Kemp, a scientist stationed at the camp, works within the concourse.
topic_desc_basic: The Camp McCarran Concourse is a section of Camp McCarran in the Mojave Wasteland, consisting of open-air buildings that once served pre-War airline passengers. Now repurposed by the New California Republic, it functions as living quarters for NCR troopers. The concourse includes a medical area, dining facilities, sleeping quarters with bunks and lockers, and connects to the terminal building and supply shack.

topic_desc: Gypsum Train Yard sits in the Mojave Wasteland northwest of the Cap Counterfeiting Shack and west of Bitter Springs. The outdoor area is heavily patrolled by blind deathclaws and young deathclaws, making approach extremely dangerous. The office building is infested with three giant ants, and ten ant egg clutches can be found within, most containing ant meat. An irradiated pool of water near the cliffs provides a contaminated drinking source. The yard's office contains a Sunset Sarsaparilla star bottle cap on a desk. Notably, an unmarked train tunnel lies to the north of the yard, secured with very hard locks on both ends, providing a route to Nellis Air Force Base. This tunnel offers an alternative approach to the Boomers' territory that bypasses their anti-aircraft gun bombardment. The yard's geography corresponds to the real-world Nevada Industrial Switch Railway Station that served the PABCO Gypsum Mine in northeast Las Vegas, Nevada.
topic_desc_basic: Gypsum Train Yard is a location in the Mojave Wasteland, located northwest of the Cap Counterfeiting Shack and west of Bitter Springs. The yard is patrolled by blind deathclaws and young deathclaws, while the office building is occupied by giant ants. An irradiated pool of water sits near the cliffs. An unmarked train tunnel to the north connects to Nellis Air Force Base.

topic_desc: Within the Capital Wasteland, the practice of field repair relies on cannibalizing similar items for compatible components. Every weapon or piece of apparel can always be repaired using an identical item. Beyond direct matches, certain families of weapons share enough mechanical similarity that parts from one variant can service another. The 10mm pistol family illustrates this principle: standard 10mm pistols, silenced variants, and even distinctive models such as Colonel Autumn's 10mm pistol share enough commonality that components from any one can be used to repair any other in the same family. This cross-compatibility extends to all weapons sharing a common repair classification. Unique or specially-manufactured weapons, including alloy-steel variants and simulation-grade firearms, also fall within these same repair families, meaning their parts are interchangeable with common variants. This approach to maintenance means that wasteland scavengers and technicians can keep equipment functional by pooling parts from multiple damaged but similar items, rather than requiring a single pristine replacement. The practice of using unique weapons as repair fodder for common ones has been noted as wasteful by some, as it sacrifices a rare item to restore a common one.
topic_desc_basic: In the Capital Wasteland, weapons and apparel can be repaired using similar items of the same type. A weapon can always be cannibalized for parts by an identical weapon. Certain related firearms share compatible components, allowing cross-repair between variants. For example, a 10mm pistol can be repaired using parts from a silenced 10mm pistol or other 10mm variants, as their internal mechanisms are sufficiently similar.
tags: 10mm pistol family,cannibalized weapon parts,capital wasteland maintenance,cross-variant component compatibility,weapon field repair
editorial_note: The source extract describes a gameplay form-list system; this has been reframed entirely as in-world knowledge about weapon repair practices and component compatibility among similar weapon variants.

topic_desc: Two Skies Cave is one of several sites in Zion Canyon connected to the survivalist Randall Clark, who lived in the region following the Great War. The cave's interior is extensively fortified with traps, suggesting Clark or another occupant took deliberate measures to deter intruders. The most notable feature is an electrified door that can be deactivated either by destroying a nearby generator or by accessing a terminal on the far side. An alternate submerged route through a flooded cavern section also leads to the survivalist's chamber, though air pockets are limited along the way. The chamber itself is divided into three sections: a campfire area near the southeast entrance, a raised platform with beds and a hidden cache, and a rear area containing a reloading bench, explosives crates, a footlocker, and a terminal with journal entries from 2083, 2084, and 2095. These entries provide insight into the survivalist's life in Zion during the early post-war years. The cave is one of six locations where a Survivalist Hidden Cache can be found.
topic_desc_basic: Two Skies Cave is a cave system in Zion Canyon, located directly west of the Old Rockville Bridge. Its interior forks into multiple passages, one of which leads to a chamber formerly inhabited by a survivalist who left behind journal entries dated 2083, 2084, and 2095. The cave is heavily trapped, including a unique electrified door and concealed shotgun traps. A survivalist cache with a substantial amount of survival gear is hidden within.

topic_desc: The Southern Passage functions as the primary transit route between the Mojave Wasteland's Northern Passage and Zion Canyon. The passage begins at an ambush site where travelers have left duffel bags against the rocks, which can serve as temporary storage. The tunnel system itself is relatively straightforward, serving as a corridor rather than a habitation site. After the conclusion of events in Zion, a footlocker appears at the cave entrance containing items associated with key figures in the Zion conflict: Joshua Graham's armor, Daniel's hat and outfit, Chalk's headdress, Salt-Upon-Wounds' helmet and power fist, a weapon called A Light Shining in Darkness, Scripture, and Waking Cloud's outfit. These items represent the material culture of the various groups present in Zion, including the Sorrows, the Dead Horses, the New Canaanites, and the White Legs. The passage's role as a chokepoint between two wasteland regions makes it strategically significant for anyone attempting to enter or leave Zion Canyon.
topic_desc_basic: The Southern Passage is a network of tunnels and passages in Zion Canyon that connects back to the Northern Passage in the Mojave Wasteland. It serves as the entry point for travel into Zion. Several duffel bags rest against the rocks near an ambush site at the passage. After the events in Zion conclude, a footlocker appears near the cave entrance containing various garments and equipment belonging to notable figures of the region.

topic_desc: The Red Gate holds deep cultural significance for the Sorrows tribe of Zion Canyon, as it is the site where Randall Clark—known to the Sorrows as the "Father"—spent his final days. Clark was a survivalist who lived in Zion following the Great War, and his journal entries found throughout the canyon document decades of solitary existence from 2083 onward. By 2124, the year of his final recorded holotape, Clark had become a figure of reverence or myth among the indigenous groups of Zion, particularly the Sorrows, who regarded him as a spiritual progenitor. His remains rest against a rock formation at the top of the Red Gate, his gaze directed toward Bighorn Bluff. Beside his skeleton lies a survivalist cache containing the Survivalist's Rifle and the Year: 2124 holotape, his last known message. The location is difficult to reach, requiring navigation around the rock formation or a steep climb up a barely scalable slope to the northwest. The site's remoteness and elevation suggest Clark chose it deliberately as a final vantage point over the canyon he had inhabited for over four decades.
topic_desc_basic: The Red Gate is a rock formation in Zion Canyon, located north-northwest of the Red Rapids Docks and overlooking the river. It is the final resting place of Randall Clark, the survivalist known as the "Father" to the Sorrows tribe. His remains lie against a rock formation facing west-northwest, obscured behind evergreen trees. A survivalist cache beside his skeleton contains his rifle and a holotape dated 2124.

topic_desc: The Forbidden Zone Dome Entrance was originally designated the X-42 Robo-Warfare Facility, a military research installation within the Big MT research complex. Following the exile of Doctor Mobius by the Think Tank, the facility was renamed and became Mobius's base of operations. The workshop area is a single vast room dominated by a central cargo elevator upon which the X-42 Giant Robo-Scorpion—a formidable automated weapon—resides. Raised walkways and observation rooms line the perimeter, containing terminals with technical data on the Robo-Scorpion's systems. The dome section is in significant disrepair compared to the Think Tank's facility: lighting is a sickly green, equipment is rusted or broken, and Mobius has covered surfaces with intricate scrawls of notes and mathematical formulas, suggesting deteriorating mental function—consistent with his known Mentats dependency. A substantial stash of 44 Mentats is stored in one of the six smaller rooms off the upper tier. At the top of the main staircase sits a brain tank containing a removed brain. The facility also contains a LAER (Laser Assisted Electrical Rifle), Dr. Mobius's glove and scrubs, and an audio sample of the Robo-Scorpion's sounds. The facility's isolation and heavy automation reflect Mobius's strategy of defending himself through robotic proxies rather than direct confrontation.
topic_desc_basic: The Forbidden Zone Dome Entrance, formerly the X-42 Robo-Warfare Facility, is a location in the northeast section of Big MT. It was renamed after the exile of Doctor Mobius. The facility consists of a large workshop dome housing the X-42 Giant Robo-Scorpion on a central cargo elevator, and a secondary dome in poor condition covered with Mobius's scrawled notes and formulas. The dome contains Mobius's private stash of Mentats and various equipment.

topic_desc: The Sierra Madre Vault was built by Frederick Sinclair as the ultimate secure repository beneath his casino, intended to protect both his fortune and those he trusted. It is not a Vault-Tec vault but a reinforced chamber accessible only through a basement labyrinth filled with the Cloud, shielded speakers, and patrolling security holograms. Forcefields block direct access, and the vault's security protocols can only be disabled from a terminal in the corridor approaching the vault room. Inside, the single-room vault holds thirty-seven gold bars, bundles of pre-War money, Sierra Madre armor, ammunition, chems, and medical supplies. A terminal on an overseer-style desk contains personal messages from Sinclair to Vera Keyes, revealing his changing feelings about her fate. Sinclair's skeleton rests on pipes near the walkway, alongside a duffle bag containing a copy of Nikola Tesla and You. A holotape on the walkway contains a letter from Sinclair condemning Vera for deceiving him. The vault became the site of a final confrontation when Father Elijah sought to claim its treasures.
topic_desc_basic: The Sierra Madre Vault is a reinforced secure storage area beneath the Sierra Madre Casino, not a Vault-Tec installation. It contains vast pre-War wealth, including gold bars, pre-War money, Sierra Madre chips, armor, and ammunition. The vault is protected by forcefields, weapon turrets, security holograms, and the toxic Cloud. Frederick Sinclair's remains lie near the vault entrance.

topic_desc: The Tampico served as the Sierra Madre Casino's primary entertainment venue, hosting the finest pre-War acts and performers, most notably singer Vera Keyes and entertainer Dean Domino. The theater was designed in the style of an Old World dinner theater, with numerous tables and chairs arranged before a large central stage. On October 23, 2077, the venue became the scene of mass death when the casino's security holograms activated in response to system alerts triggered by the falling nuclear bombs, slaughtering guests and staff alike. The theater's layout includes a front lobby with a receptionist desk, a main auditorium with a stage, and a backstage area containing Dean Domino's dressing room and Vera Keyes's dressing room. Vera's music stand sits before the stage, holding her partitures and a hidden backstage key. Dean's dressing room contains a safe holding blackmail evidence he collected, while Vera's dressing room holds a holotape of Dean's song Saw Her Yesterday and her master key. The backstage area also contains a hologram emitter that can be used to control security systems. The name Tampico references the Mexican town where the 1948 film The Treasure of the Sierra Madre was filmed.
topic_desc_basic: The Tampico is the theater within the Sierra Madre Casino, designed as the premier entertainment venue for casino guests. It featured pre-War performers including Vera Keyes and Dean Domino. On October 23, 2077, the theater became a slaughter site when security holograms activated as nuclear bombs fell. The theater includes a lobby, main stage, and backstage dressing rooms.

topic_desc: Before the Great War, Campanas del Sol served as a residential and religious area for Sierra Madre Casino staff, containing a church, morgue, and dormitory housing. Situated at the northern edge of Salida del Sol, the area is accessible through a large courtyard surrounded by balconies, with multiple passages leading through chapel rooms, a wine cellar, and empty dormitories. Ghost People inhabit the buildings and balconies throughout the area. The bell tower at the summit contains a control panel used to trigger the Gala Event, a celebration intended to open the Sierra Madre's doors, along with two vending machine codes—one for super stimpaks and another for holorifle focus optics. When the gala event is activated, additional Ghost People appear throughout the area and previously inactive speakers turn on. Embalming fluid can be found in rooms near the staircases leading to lower levels, a remnant of the area's morgue function. The area's architecture reflects its Spanish-influenced naming, consistent with the Sierra Madre's thematic design.
topic_desc_basic: Campanas del Sol is the northernmost area of Salida del Sol in the Sierra Madre, consisting of a former church, morgue, and staff housing before the Great War. It features a large courtyard, chapel, wine cellar, and a bell tower containing a control panel for the Gala Event and vending machine codes.

topic_desc: Cueva Guarache, meaning Sandal Cave in Spanish, is a cave system in Zion Canyon southeast of Ranger Substation Osprey. The cave descends steeply before branching into multiple passages, one of which is blocked by a dense wall of brush concealing bear traps, a tripwire connected to rigged shotguns, and a hard-locked door leading directly to the chambers of Randall Clark, the Survivalist. The deeper passages open into large chambers infested with spore carriers, spore carrier runts, spore carrier brutes, and giant spore plants. A natural balcony runs across the eastern end of the main chamber, accessible via a tunnel from the north end. Beyond a chain-link fence and gate on the balcony lies a plasma mine and supply sacks. Clark's chamber contains a campfire, workbench, explosives crates, a bed, and a computer holding his personal logs from the years 2097, 2100, and 2101, documenting his life in Zion after the Great War. A locked gun case and a Survivalist Hidden Cache are also present, one of six such caches hidden throughout Zion Canyon. The cave's upper level layout bears similarity to Silver Peak Mine.
topic_desc_basic: Cueva Guarache is a cave in Zion Canyon, located southeast of Ranger Substation Osprey near the river. It contains the hidden chamber of Randall Clark, the Survivalist, with his living quarters, workbench, campfire, and computer logs from 2097, 2100, and 2101. The cave is heavily trapped and infested with spore carriers and spore plants.

topic_desc: The Nipton Road Reststop sits at the crossroads of two major Mojave routes: Interstate 15 and Nevada Highway 164, making it a natural waypoint for travelers moving between Primm and Nipton. The Poseidon Energy gas station and adjoining general store are the complex's main structures. The store is distinct from the Nipton Trading Post within Nipton proper. Radscorpions nest throughout the area, discouraging casual visitors. The store harbors Mayor Steyn's hidden cache—sacks and a locked gun cabinet—documented on his Town Hall terminal, suggesting the mayor maintained supplies well outside Nipton's limits. A dead Bright Follower lies against the gas station sign, hinting at recent violent passage through the area. Graffiti above the awning bears the name "Lester," also seen inside Vault 3, and a nearby garage bears the painted question "Where's New Canaan, anyway?"—a reference to the Mormon settlement whose fate has circulated among wasteland travelers.
topic_desc_basic: The Nipton Road Reststop is a Poseidon gas station at the junction of I-15 and Nevada 164, near Nipton Junction south of Primm. The area includes a general store, a destroyed house, and an inaccessible house. Radscorpions of various sizes infest the grounds. A wrecked vehicle out front holds ammunition. The general store contains Mayor Steyn's secret stash, referenced in his Nipton Town Hall terminal.

topic_desc: The Monte Carlo Suites occupies a position on the western fringe of New Vegas, sandwiched between the Sunset Sarsaparilla Headquarters and the Westside district. Despite its deteriorated exterior—wrecked trucks flanking the entrance and a crumbling interior—the building retains a degree of organization unusual for a wasteland gang hideout. The Scorpions, led by Roller and Yvette, have arranged sleeping quarters, dining rooms, children's rooms, and a workspace, suggesting a more settled and hierarchical operation than typical raider bands. A constant guard watches the front door. The ground floor contains a workbench and reloading bench, indicating the gang maintains its own equipment. A Sierra Madre poster adorns one room, a relic of the ill-fated casino's pre-war promotional campaign. Klamath Bob, who runs a liquor store in Westside, can provide information about the location and its inhabitants. Yvette carries a well-maintained .44 Magnum revolver, and the suites stock numerous large whiskey bottles.
topic_desc_basic: The Monte Carlo Suites is a large building on the western side of New Vegas, north of Sunset Sarsaparilla Headquarters and south of Westside. It serves as the base of the Scorpions gang. The building is decayed with demolished stairs blocking the second floor. Gang leaders Roller and Yvette command the members inside, who are armed with small guns and switchblades.

topic_desc: The Camp McCarran Supply Shack functions as a logistical node within the NCR's primary Mojave military installation. Located in the airfield's southeastern corner, the two-story metal shack is accessible through three separate entry points: a ground-level southern door, an elevated eastern door reached via ramps, and a northern passage connecting through the concourse. Sergeant Daniel Contreras operates as the NCR supply merchant from within, managing arms and ammunition distribution. The first floor features a reloading bench and workbench in a western niche, suggesting on-site equipment maintenance. The second floor serves as Contreras's personal quarters, containing an owned bed, a radio, an average-locked terminal, and a hard-locked filing cabinet. Contreras has been linked to irregular arms requests, with documentation referencing a McCarran Arms Request that can be obtained either directly from him or downloaded from the NCR supply database terminal. The elevated eastern door has a known structural fault, requiring an angled approach to interact with properly.
topic_desc_basic: The Camp McCarran Supply Shack is a two-story metal structure in the southeastern corner of the Camp McCarran airfield. It houses the NCR supply merchant, Sergeant Daniel Contreras. The first floor contains empty shelves, lockers, a reloading bench, and a workbench. The second floor has a bed, radio, terminal, and a locked filing cabinet. Three access points connect the shack to the airfield and concourse.

topic_desc: Brooks Tumbleweed Ranch sits at one of the northernmost reaches of the Mojave Wasteland, beyond the remains of Highway 95 and northwest of the Horowitz Farmstead. The ranch house comprises a kitchen, living room, storage area, and bedroom, with a second-floor dresser holding a cattle prod. Tumbleweeds have invaded the interior—one resting on a sofa, another on a bed—while more drift through the cattle pen behind the structure. A dead wastelander lies near the pen entrance. The ranch's most notable inhabitant is a cloaked Nightkin who uncloaks when approached, offering to sell "wind-brahmin"—the Nightkin's term for tumbleweeds, which the super mutant genuinely perceives as living creatures. This delusion reflects the psychological deterioration common among Nightkin from prolonged Stealth Boy use. The ranch's internal layout is architecturally identical to the capitol building in the Republic of Dave, a settlement in the Capital Wasteland. A copy of Lying, Congressional Style can be found on the top floor, and a Sunset Sarsaparilla Star Bottle Cap rests on the kitchen floor.
topic_desc_basic: Brooks Tumbleweed Ranch is a remote location north of Highway 95 in the northern Mojave Wasteland, slightly northwest of the Horowitz Farmstead. The ranch house contains a kitchen, living room, storage area, and bedroom. A cattle pen behind the house holds drifting tumbleweeds. A Nightkin near the pen offers to sell "wind-brahmin" to passersby.

topic_desc: The Ruined Store sits in the western portion of Freeside, a short distance from the Silver Rush and the Freeside Train Station. The building is a destroyed structure whose only entrance remains locked, accessible by key, pickpocketing, or learning a password from locals such as the missionary or Rotface. Inside, Major Elizabeth Kieran of the NCR runs a soup kitchen distributing free supplies to Freeside squatters, reflecting the NCR's efforts to maintain goodwill among the impoverished population of the Mojave. Two NCR troopers typically guard the entrance. The location's proximity to Cerulean Robotics and the surrounding rubble makes it difficult to find without familiarity with Freeside's layout. The NCR's presence here illustrates the republic's logistical and humanitarian outreach in territories it does not fully control, operating relief efforts amid Freeside's lawlessness and poverty.
topic_desc_basic: The Ruined Store is a destroyed building in western Freeside, near Cerulean Robotics. topic_desc: The Great Khan Encampment is a strategic overlook position used by the Great Khans to monitor Quarry Junction from the ridges above. Situated southeast of the Makeshift Great Khan Camp and west of the quarry itself, the encampment is sparsely furnished with two makeshift beds. Its primary inhabitant is Melissa, accompanied by two other Great Khans. Workers in Sloan have reported seeing people on the ridge, though the quarry's closure due to deathclaw infestations has made the area dangerous. The encampment reflects the Great Khans' continued interest in the quarry region, likely tied to their broader operations and trade networks. The location's proximity to Quarry Junction places it in contested territory where wildlife threats and faction interests intersect, illustrating the precarious nature of Great Khan operations in the northern Mojave.
topic_desc_basic: The Great Khan Encampment is a small camp in the Mojave Wasteland, located southeast of the Makeshift Great Khan Camp and west of Quarry Junction. The Great Khans use it to overlook the quarry. It contains two makeshift beds and is inhabited by Melissa and two Great Khan members.

topic_desc: Spring Mt. Ranch State Park occupies a position between the Tribal Village and Red Rock Canyon in the Mojave Wasteland, placing it within territory associated with the Great Khans. The park's landscape centers on a lake that has become habitat for giant mantises and cazadores, while bighorners graze the surrounding area. A burned-down house near the lake contains minor salvage. More significantly, a destroyed house to the northeast conceals a cellar door leading to the Great Khan Armory, a basement equipped with a workbench and reloading bench. The Great Khan Armorer operates from this basement, trading with those on friendly terms with the Great Khans. The park's proximity to Red Rock Canyon reinforces its connection to Great Khan territory, and the armory's presence suggests the Khans maintain supply and manufacturing capabilities in the area. The pre-war park was a public recreation area within the Red Rock Canyon National Conservation Area.
topic_desc_basic: Spring Mt. Ranch State Park is a location in the Mojave Wasteland, situated between the Tribal Village and Red Rock Canyon. The area features a lake surrounded by giant mantises and cazadores, with bighorners grazing nearby. A burned-down house stands near the lake, and a destroyed house to the northeast contains a cellar leading to the Great Khan Armory.

topic_desc: The Arizona Spillway is a structural component of Hoover Dam on its eastern side, overlooking the Colorado River. Its strategic significance was underscored during the Battle of Arizona Spillway, which occurred sometime after the First Battle of Hoover Dam. In this engagement, Caesar's Legion successfully pushed NCR forces off the east banks, consolidating Legion control over the eastern approaches to the dam. This battle represents part of the ongoing conflict between the NCR and the Legion for control of the Colorado River and Hoover Dam, the Mojave's most critical strategic and resource asset. The spillway itself is a real-world engineering feature of Hoover Dam designed to handle excess water flow. An Arizona Spillway Tunnel exists in records but remains unused and inaccessible in the current Mojave landscape. The spillway's role in post-First Battle engagements highlights how the dam's infrastructure became contested ground in the broader NCR-Legion war.
topic_desc_basic: The Arizona Spillway is part of the Hoover Dam, situated on the eastern side overlooking the Colorado River. After the First Battle of Hoover Dam, the Battle of Arizona Spillway took place here, with Caesar's Legion pushing NCR forces off the east banks of the river.

topic_desc: The barracks serves as a rest and recreation point for NCR personnel stationed at the Mojave Outpost, the southernmost major NCR installation along the I-15 corridor. Inside, Lacey operates a bar counter stocked with alcohol, Nuka-Cola, and assorted provisions, though the goods on her shelves are technically marked as NCR property, leading troopers to occasionally help themselves. The bunk area accommodates numerous soldiers, though some troopers here lack dog tags, hinting at irregularities in unit records or recent transfers. Cass, a caravan merchant with ties to the Crimson Caravan company, can be found at this location, as can a traveling caravaneer. The rooftop position occupied by Ranger Ghost provides a vantage over the surrounding approach roads, and the paired satellite dishes suggest continued communications infrastructure. A copy of Duck and Cover rests on a shelf behind the bar, and several bottles of Nuka-Cola Quartz and ice-cold Nuka-Cola line the shelves. The building's proximity to the Unification Monument underscores the outpost's symbolic role in NCR-Mojave relations.
topic_desc_basic: The Mojave Outpost Barracks is one of two enterable buildings at the Mojave Outpost, situated on the southern side of I-15 between the headquarters and the Unification Monument. It houses a bar run by Lacey, who sells alcohol and other goods, a small kitchen, and a bunk area filled with beds used by NCR troopers. Ranger Ghost, an NCR sniper, keeps watch from a rooftop overlook. Two satellite dishes stand atop the roof.

topic_desc: Crescent Canyon West and its eastern counterpart trace a crescent-moon-shaped gully beneath a collapsed bridge, carving a natural corridor through the rugged terrain of the McCullough Range. The canyon's irradiation stems from scattered waste barrels dumped along its length, making passage hazardous without protective gear. Golden geckos, drawn to the radioactive environment, pose an additional threat to anyone traversing the gully. A hollowed-out rock near the western entrance, adjacent to a rusting vehicle, offers a modest stash for travelers. Roughly halfway through the canyon, an overturned truck marks the location of a case containing an advanced radiation suit, a critical find for those needing to press deeper into the irradiated passage. The canyon's geography corresponds to the real-world Crescent Canyon below Crescent Peak, and its natural barrier function channels north-south movement along the southern Mojave. The combination of radiation, geckos, and confined terrain makes the canyon a dangerous shortcut rather than a safe route.
topic_desc_basic: Crescent Canyon West is the western entrance to a large crescent-shaped canyon south of Morning Star Cavern in the Mojave Wasteland. The canyon connects with Crescent Canyon East to form a natural barrier along the southern edge of the map. It is populated by golden geckos and littered with radioactive waste barrels, producing radiation levels of up to four rads per second. An advanced radiation suit can be found near an overturned truck midway through.

topic_desc: The Wrecked Highwayman marks the final resting place of a pre-war Highwayman, a model of automobile once common on American roads. The vehicle has largely sunk into the ground, leaving only its trunk exposed to the elements. Within the open trunk, a footlocker holds a modest cache of energy weapon ammunition, including microfusion cells and energy cells, along with scrap metal and a Sunset Sarsaparilla star bottle cap. The presence of energy ammunition suggests the vehicle's owner may have been a traveler equipped with energy weapons, or that the trunk was used as a stash point after the war. The location sits near Highway 95, a major pre-war route connecting settlements in the region. The wreck is isolated, with no nearby structures or camps, making it a waypoint for prospectors combing the highway corridor between Clark Field and Snyder Prospector Camp. The vehicle itself is not connected to any known historical figure from the Mojave's post-war record.
topic_desc_basic: The Wrecked Highwayman is a location in the Mojave Wasteland, situated northwest of Snyder Prospector Camp and southwest of Clark Field just off Highway 95. It consists of the sunken remains of a Highwayman automobile, with only the trunk visible above ground. A footlocker in the open trunk contains microfusion cells, energy cells, scrap metal, random supplies, and a Sunset Sarsaparilla star bottle cap.
