topic_desc: The Nipton Road Pit Stop sits along Nevada 164, a stretch of highway connecting the Mojave's southern settlements to the town of Nipton. Before the war, it likely served as a roadside rest area; in the post-war era, it has become a haunt for the Jackals, one of the Mojave's raider tribes. A group of Jackals, sometimes led by two separate leaders, occupies the ruined structures and uses the site to ambush passersby. Additional Jackal members travel between the pit stop and Bradley's Shack to the southeast, following a route near the Mojave Drive-in, though radscorpions in the surrounding desert sometimes thin their numbers. The campfire and healing powder suggest the gang maintains rudimentary survival practices. The graffiti proclaiming "The Burned Man Walks!" on the western brick wall reflects the spread of rumors about the legendary burned figure associated with Caesar's Legion's past. A briefcase hidden beneath a blue car offers additional salvage. The pit stop's proximity to Nipton makes it a dangerous approach for anyone heading east toward the town.
topic_desc_basic: The Nipton Road Pit Stop is a ruined wayside along Nevada 164, west of Nipton and south of the Ivanpah Race Track. It consists of destroyed buildings, a campfire, and makeshift beds. The site is occupied by Jackal gang members who ambush travelers on the road. Frag mines and frag grenades can be found in the ruined northern building. The words "The Burned Man Walks!" are scrawled on the western wall of the brick building.
tags: burned man graffiti,frag mines cache,jackal gang ambush,mojave drive-in route,nevada 164,nipton road

topic_desc: Ruby Hill Mine's flooded lower cavern holds a grim and curious tableau. Beneath the water's surface sits a round table with four chairs, four human skeletons in or near the seats, and the floating corpse of a super mutant brute. A deck of cards rests on the table, with two cards dealt before each seat—one face up, one face down—suggesting the dead had been playing blackjack when they met their end. The super mutant brute carries a multiplas rifle. Elsewhere in the cavern, a dead Jackal gang member can be found carrying a worn key that opens explosive crates on the island in the lake; two additional explosive crates sit in the northernmost dead-end of the cave. The Jackal also carries Pushy, a unique displacer glove. An apparent exit behind the dead-end cannot be traversed, and only one entrance is functional despite two map markers appearing inside.
topic_desc_basic: Ruby Hill Mine is a small mining location nestled in a west-facing rock formation in the Mojave Wasteland, northwest of Nevada 157. The entrance opens into a main room frequented by lakelurks. Stairs lead down to a large flooded cavern inhabited by more lakelurks. A grave sits southwest of the entrance near the cliff face, where bighorner bulls are commonly seen. A hollowed-out rock near the entrance sometimes contains useful supplies.
tags: flooded mine,jackal gang member,lakelurk cavern,mojave wasteland location,ruby hill mine,super mutant brute
editorial_note: The blackjack tableau and the presence of a dead super mutant among human skeletons is an unexplained scene; its origin is not documented in the source.

topic_desc: Before the Great War, the Goodsprings Gas Station was a Poseidon Energy property, part of the corporation's sprawling energy and fuel infrastructure across the American Southwest. In the postwar era, the station has served as a sheltered hideout. Ringo, a caravan guard on the run from Joe Cobb and the Powder Gangers, has taken refuge inside, reportedly because the building's layout offers a defensive advantage against anyone approaching. However, the exterior windows are boarded up and the interior has no windows, making Ringo's claimed tactical advantage questionable. The station's shelves, though in disarray, still hold useful supplies: a copy of Boxing Times, a doctor's bag, turpentine, crates of Sunset Sarsaparilla, cartons of cigarettes, and 9mm rounds beneath the cash register. An easy-locked safe sits beneath a duffel bag in the corner. The station's proximity to Goodsprings' town center makes it a contested site during local conflicts involving the Powder Gangers.
topic_desc_basic: The Goodsprings Gas Station is a building in the town of Goodsprings in the Mojave Wasteland. Before the Great War it was owned by Poseidon Energy. The exterior features a drive-in garage, a Poseidon Gas Station sign, and a Sunset Sarsaparilla vending machine. Inside, the shelves are disorganized but contain useful consumables, crafting ingredients, and a duffel bag beside a bed resting on an easy-locked safe. The counter holds ammunition and cigarettes.
tags: goodsprings gas station,mojave wasteland location,poseidon energy property,powder ganger conflict,ringo hideout,sunset sarsaparilla crates
editorial_note: Ringo's claim about shooting through windows contradicts the boarded-up exterior described in the source; this discrepancy is preserved as reported.

topic_desc: The Devil's Throat is one of the most hazardous irradiated sites in the northeastern Mojave. The crater's pools of contaminated water and scattered toxic waste barrels produce radiation levels of approximately eleven rads per drink in the water and two to eight rads per second around the barrels. The wrecked truck at the crater's center is unusual compared to other derelict trucks in the wastes, lacking both a motor and doors. At the rear of the truck lies a dead super mutant, and inside the trailer a dead prospector can be found wearing reinforced combat armor and a unique party hat, with the unique minigun CZ57 Avenger beside them. The centaur population, led by a giant evolved centaur, respawns within days of being killed. Northwest of the crater lies a super mutant camp hosting up to four super mutant masters, where NCR rangers have been known to engage them in combat. The broader region is sparsely populated and heavily irradiated, making it one of the more remote and dangerous corners of the Mojave Wasteland.
topic_desc_basic: The Devil's Throat is a large radioactive crater in the northeastern Mojave Desert, east of Bloodborne Cave. Contaminated water pools at the bottom, and a wrecked truck sits at the center surrounded by toxic waste barrels. The area is inhabited by centaurs, including a giant evolved centaur. A dead super mutant lies at the rear of the truck. Radiation levels near the barrels range from two to eight rads per second.
tags: centaur habitat,cz57 avenger,devil's throat crater,mojave wasteland location,radioactive crater,super mutant camp
editorial_note: The source references a 'Wild Wasteland encounter' involving an undetonated atomic bomb called The One; this is preserved as an in-world anomaly without referencing gameplay mechanics.

topic_desc: The Legion Raid Camp serves as one of Caesar's Legion's forward assault positions in the Mojave, projecting Legion power into territory contested with the NCR. The camp's two-level layout uses natural landmasses for defense. The upper level contains a storage tent and two red tents, each with four bedrolls and two footlockers. The lower level has an additional tent where legionaries sometimes sleep. Each level features a campfire. A perimeter patrol of two to four legionaries guards the approach, and NCR patrols traveling nearby have been known to engage the Legion in firefights. The camp also holds two captured Powder Gangers, bound as prisoners. The camp is one of the few locations where Legion forces respawn after being killed, indicating its strategic importance as a maintained forward position. Nightstalkers have been known to attack the camp, occasionally killing all occupants. The surrounding area sits along a corridor of ongoing Legion-NCR friction, making it a flashpoint for small-scale skirmishes in the southeastern Mojave.
topic_desc_basic: The Legion Raid Camp is a forward assault camp for Caesar's Legion in the Mojave Wasteland, located northeast of Wolfhorn Ranch between Walking Box Cavern and Broc Flower Cave. The camp is built on two natural levels with storage and sleeping tents, campfires, and up to five legionaries in residence. A patrol of two to four legionaries walks the perimeter. Two Powder Gangers are held hostage at the camp.
tags: caesar's legion forward camp,legion ncr skirmish,legion raid camp,mojave wasteland location,nightstalker attack,powder ganger hostages
editorial_note: The source mentions specific quests ('Booted' and 'I Forgot to Remember to Forget') but these are omitted per instructions; only the in-world situation of the hostages and camp is described.

topic_desc: The Prospector's Den sits directly southeast of Primm and southwest of the Emergency Service Railyard, serving as a modest cave shelter with a three-room structure built inside: a living room and kitchen with beds, jukebox, radio, and refrigerator; a main quarters with eight mattresses and footlockers; and a small maintenance shack with a reloading bench, first aid supplies, and a generator. Evidence suggests it long functioned as a safehouse and rest stop for Mojave scavengers. Recently, a gang of Jackals raided the den, slaughtering the prospectors sheltering within and claiming it as their hideout. The dead prospectors' belongings, including weapons and caps, remain scattered across the floor. The surrounding area is hazardous, with centaurs and bark scorpions known to appear near the entrance.
topic_desc_basic: The Prospector's Den is a cave shelter southeast of Primm in the Mojave Wasteland. Prospectors once used it as a safehouse and rest stop. A gang of Jackals recently raided the den, killing the prospectors inside and claiming it as their hideout. The cave contains a built structure with living quarters, a kitchen, beds, a reloading bench, and scattered supplies belonging to the dead.

topic_desc: Matthews Animal Husbandry Farm lies equidistant between the Raided Farmstead to the north and the Crashed Vertibird to the south. It consists of two dilapidated barns, several animal pens, and the burnt ruins of a farmhouse. Scattered diary pages reveal the fate of its last inhabitant, a lone child. The child's parents traveled to Camp Searchlight for supplies and never returned; when the child went searching, they found their parents had become feral ghouls and were forced to shoot them in self-defense. Traumatized and alone, the child grew increasingly paranoid, believing the farm animals conspired to overtake the property. In a final desperate act, the child burned the farmhouse to the ground while still inside. The child-sized skeleton remains among the ruins. The barns still hold malnourished bighorners and brahmin, and two graves lie to the southeast.
topic_desc_basic: Matthews Animal Husbandry Farm is a ruined farmstead in the Mojave Wasteland, located between the Raided Farmstead and the Crashed Vertibird. It has two barns with malnourished bighorners and brahmin, animal pens, and a burnt farmhouse. Diary pages reveal a lone child lived here after the parents became feral ghouls at Camp Searchlight. The traumatized child eventually burned the farmhouse down, perishing inside.

topic_desc: Coyote Mines sits northeast of Searchlight North Gold Mine and southwest of Ranger Station Echo in the Mojave Wasteland. The site comprises two sections: a two-story house and the mine itself. The house contains a bed, storage, a working jukebox, kitchen food supplies, and three first aid boxes. The mine features a branching path: to the left lies a camping area with a bedroll, toolbench junk, healing powders, and hydra, occasionally sheltering prospectors; to the right, alcoves hold dynamite, frag grenades, and minor supplies. Feral ghouls from Camp Searchlight occasionally roam near the house. The location corresponds geographically to the real-world Coyote Gold Mines north of Searchlight, Nevada. Neither the house nor the mine contains hostile creatures or traps under normal conditions.
topic_desc_basic: Coyote Mines is a location in the Mojave Wasteland, northeast of Searchlight North Gold Mine and southwest of Ranger Station Echo. It consists of a two-story house and a mine. The house offers a bed, storage, a jukebox, food, and first aid supplies. The mine contains a camping area with a bedroll and healing items, plus alcoves with dynamite and grenades. Feral ghouls from Camp Searchlight sometimes roam nearby.

topic_desc: Ranger Station Alpha is an NCR outpost perched above Lake Mead with a commanding view of the Fort, located north of Boulder City. The station consists of three tents, a campfire, and a radio tower, with beds in the middle tent. Three rangers are stationed there, including Ranger Lineholm, along with Comm Officer Castillo. The station participates in NCR communications networks across the Mojave. Lakelurks inhabiting the Lake Mead shore pose a recurring threat to the rangers. The Mojave ranger stations follow the NATO phonetic alphabet naming convention; Alpha is notable for diverging from the standard spelling 'Alfa' to the more common 'Alpha.' The station's elevated position gives it strategic value for monitoring activity on and around the lake and the Fort opposite.
topic_desc_basic: Ranger Station Alpha is an NCR outpost north of Boulder City, perched above Lake Mead with a view of the Fort. It consists of three tents, a campfire, and a radio tower. Three rangers are stationed there, including Ranger Lineholm and Comm Officer Castillo. Lakelurks along the nearby shore can threaten the rangers. The station is part of the NCR's network of ranger stations across the Mojave.

topic_desc: Bloodborne Cave is notorious among Mojave travelers for its dense population of nightstalkers. The creatures have claimed the entire interior as their territory, with a legendary night stalker—the largest and most dangerous of the pack—dwelling in the deepest chamber near a campfire. The cave's layout is a single interior section, and the entrance is surrounded by aggressive wildlife, making approach hazardous. Beyond the main chamber, a locked gate secures a significant hoard: thousands of bottle caps, NCR dollars in multiple denominations, Legion denarii and aurei, and a 12.7mm submachine gun in poor condition, all stored in an average-locked trunk. The corridor immediately past the gate contains a tripwire connected to grenade bouquets, making forced entry lethal in the tight space. Skeletons scattered past the campfire suggest previous explorers met grim ends. Nightstalker eggs can also be found within the cave. The nightstalkers are known to repopulate after their numbers are thinned, and cazadores have been observed moving into the area once the nightstalkers are eliminated, indicating the cave's ecology is volatile and contested.
topic_desc_basic: Bloodborne Cave is a cavern east of the Brotherhood of Steel safehouse and northwest of Bitter Springs in the Mojave Wasteland. It is infested with nightstalkers, including a notably large and dangerous specimen. A campfire sits deep inside near the cave's end. A locked gate on the north side conceals a cache of caps, NCR currency, Legion coins, weapons, and ammunition, though the corridor beyond is trapped with rigged explosives.

topic_desc: The Nash Residence is a cornerstone of Primm's commercial life, functioning as both the Nash family home and the only Mojave Express branch operating across the Mojave Wasteland. Johnson Nash, a pragmatic and long-winded elderly merchant, runs the storefront, buying and selling a variety of goods including a bladed gauntlet. His wife Ruby is known for her cooking, particularly a casserole prepared using radscorpion poison glands—a dish that has gained some local notoriety. The building sits on Primm's main street, directly across from the Bison Steve Hotel and the Vikki and Vance Casino, with a large Mojave Express sign atop the roof making it a visible landmark. A Mojave Express dropbox sits on the countertop in the first room. At some point, a damaged Enclave Eyebot designated ED-E was delivered to the residence and left in a state of disrepair inside the building. The Nashes were forced to abandon the residence when Primm was overrun by escaped convicts who seized the Bison Steve, leaving the town in turmoil. The Mojave Express operations from Primm were disrupted as a result, and the residence stood empty until order was restored to the town.
topic_desc_basic: The Nash Residence in Primm is the home of Johnson and Ruby Nash, serving as both a storefront and a dwelling. It is the sole Mojave Express office in the Mojave Wasteland. Located across from the Bison Steve Hotel and the Vikki and Vance Casino, the building bears a prominent rooftop sign. Johnson Nash trades equipment, while Ruby Nash is known for her casserole made from radscorpion poison glands. A broken Eyebot designated ED-E was found inside.

topic_desc: Bonnie Springs was once a mining settlement along Nevada 159, northeast of the Tribal Village and southeast of Spring Mt. Ranch State Park. By 2281, the town is little more than a cluster of destroyed and derelict buildings flanking a single main street that terminates at a boarded-up saloon. Despite its ruined state, it remains a navigational landmark for travelers moving through the area. The town has been claimed by a gang of Vipers—four regular members and two leaders. One Viper leader wears green combat armor and carries a unique set of spiked knuckles known as "Love and Hate," while the other wears reinforced metal armor and wields a trail carbine, supplemented by plasma grenades. A grave on the western hill hints at the town's earlier history. The area's ecology is volatile: once the Vipers are eliminated, cazadores move into the abandoned houses and build nests within four days, killing any remaining gang members. If the cazadores are in turn wiped out, a blind deathclaw has been known to appear. The clouds above Bonnie Springs sometimes take on an unnatural green tint, reminiscent of the contamination over Camp Searchlight, though the cause is unclear. Two Sunset Sarsaparilla star bottle caps can be found in open crates on a porch in the southeast part of town.
topic_desc_basic: Bonnie Springs is a former mining town along Nevada 159 in the Mojave Wasteland, located north of Goodsprings Cemetery. It serves as a landmark for travelers. The town consists of a single main street leading to a boarded-up saloon, flanked by derelict buildings. A grave sits on a hill west of town. It is occupied by a well-armed gang of Vipers, including leaders equipped with plasma grenades and a trail carbine.

topic_desc: Silver Peak Mine sits on a rocky embankment west of Nevada 157, just off the road leading to Jacobstown. The mine complex includes a surface shack and a large underground cavern system. The cavern was colonized by cazadores that entered through a hole high on the chamber wall, and the interior now hosts a significant population, including a legendary cazador of exceptional size and aggression. The upper level of the cavern, accessible via a tunnel at the back of the main chamber, contains a gated area where a Remnants power helmet has been stored—an artifact suggesting pre-war or Enclave-affiliated activity in the mine. Crates near the gate and in a side room hold a substantial cache of explosives, including C-4 plastic explosive, plasma grenades, frag mines, frag grenades, dynamite, pulse grenades, and pulse mines. The surface area is patrolled by bighorner bulls that attack intruders on sight. The mine's ecosystem is volatile: the legendary cazador and its attendants are known to repopulate after being eliminated. A copy of Tumblers Today can be found in the shack near a locker, and a Sunset Sarsaparilla star bottle cap rests on a table near the entrance. The combination of aggressive wildlife and the mine's remote location makes it a dangerous site for any wastelander.
topic_desc_basic: Silver Peak Mine is a location in the Mojave Wasteland, west of Nevada 157 along the path to Jacobstown. It is connected to the Silver Peak Mine shack. The mine is infested with cazadores, including a legendary specimen that entered through a hole high on the cavern wall. Bighorner bulls guard the exterior. Inside, a tunnel leads to an upper level with crates, a gated area, and a Remnants power helmet stored behind a fence door.

topic_desc: The El Dorado Substation sits in the shadow of HELIOS One, the pre-war solar power installation now occupied by the NCR. The facility consists of a tall concrete structure with a garage door entrance and a barricaded side door, fronted by an array of transformers within a fenced compound. NCR military police maintain a permanent garrison here, reflecting the strategic importance of regional power infrastructure. The substation's geographical placement corresponds to the real-world El Dorado Solar Power Plant substation near Boulder City, Nevada. Tensions surround the site: NCR troopers will not permit access to restricted areas under any circumstances, and covert entry is treated as a hostile act regardless of reputation. The substation plays a role in regional power distribution decisions connected to HELIOS One's output, making it a point of interest for parties concerned with the Mojave's energy future.
topic_desc_basic: The El Dorado Substation is a concrete building and transformer array near HELIOS One in the Mojave Wasteland, located southwest of Vault 11 and northwest of El Dorado Dry Lake. NCR Troopers, including a sergeant, guard the site and prohibit entry to the building and fenced area regardless of one's standing with the Republic.

topic_desc: The Mesquite Mountains Crater is one of the more dangerously irradiated sites in the Mojave Wasteland. The crater's pools of water emit significant radiation, and the area attracts feral ghouls, roamers, and reavers, making it hazardous for unprepared travelers. On the southwest rim sits Hell's Motel, a small shack containing a copy of D.C. Journal of Internal Medicine and a weapon repair kit. East of the crater, an improvised shelter offers a bed and first aid supplies, while a makeshift shack below the eastern cliff contains a motorcycle with reading material nearby. The presence of a concealed mine under a traffic cone suggests previous visitors took pains to discourage followers. The crater's remote location and intense radiation make it a site few wastelanders visit willingly, though scavengers occasionally brave its dangers for salvageable goods.
topic_desc_basic: The Mesquite Mountains Crater is a heavily irradiated location in the Mojave Wasteland, southwest of Primm and north of the Mesquite Mountains Camp Site. Pools of irradiated water fill the crater, and feral ghouls roam the area. A shack called Hell's Motel sits on the crater's southwest side.

topic_desc: The Nellis Hangars form a core part of the Boomers' settlement at Nellis Air Force Base. The northern hangar functions as a mess hall and munitions storage facility, while the southern hangar serves as an aircraft maintenance bay. The Boomers, a tribe descended from Vault 34 dwellers who developed an obsession with explosives and heavy weaponry, use these hangars to store combat armor and munitions. Loyal, one of the Boomers' senior members and a gifted mechanic, and Jack, a younger technician, frequently work in the hangar area. The hangars gained particular significance when the Boomers undertook the ambitious project of raising a crashed B-29 bomber from the depths of Lake Mead. The salvaged bomber, christened "Pearl," was brought to the southern hangar for restoration, with Boomers working from elevated platforms to repair the vintage aircraft. This project exemplifies the Boomers' combination of technical ingenuity and martial ambition.
topic_desc_basic: The Nellis Hangars are two large hangars in the northern section of Nellis Air Force Base, home to the Boomers. The northern hangar serves as a mess hall and munitions storage area, while the southern hangar houses aircraft. Boomers such as Jack and Loyal can be found working in this area.

topic_desc: Fremont Street is the main thoroughfare of Freeside, the impoverished district that has grown organically around the intersection of Fremont and Las Vegas Boulevard outside the walls of the New Vegas Strip. The street hosts several of Freeside's most prominent establishments: the Silver Rush, headquarters of the Van Graff family's energy weapons trade; the King's School of Impersonation, base of the Kings, a gang modeled on pre-war Elvis Presley culture; and the Atomic Wrangler, one of Freeside's few functioning casinos. The area has experienced escalating conflict between destitute travelers heading to or from the Strip and local residents who resent the influx. Robert House values the Fremont Street area but considers it subordinate to the Strip itself in his vision for New Vegas. The street's fortunes are tied to regional power distribution, as electricity from HELIOS One can potentially be routed to the surrounding area, influencing its economic prospects.
topic_desc_basic: Fremont Street is a roadway in Freeside, the slum district surrounding the New Vegas Strip. Freeside grew around the intersection of Fremont and Las Vegas Boulevard. Notable establishments on Fremont Street include the Silver Rush, the King's School of Impersonation, and the Atomic Wrangler.

topic_desc: Before the Great War, the Old Nuclear Test Site functioned as a nuclear weapon test range and waste disposal area, activities that permanently contaminated the surrounding landscape. The lingering radiation has made the site a natural habitat for heavily irradiated feral ghouls, including Reavers and Glowing Ones, which pose a significant threat to any wastelander approaching the compound. The site is largely fenced off and inaccessible, with the exception of the Nuclear Test Shack, which itself remains irradiated inside. Notably, the apex of radiation is not centered in the crater but concentrated closer to the shack entrance. On a nearby hill to the northwest, an observation area with five chairs and five pairs of Authority Glasses overlooks the site, suggesting pre-War personnel monitored detonations from that vantage. The location sits equidistant from Caesar's Legion Safehouse to the northwest and the Crashed Vertibird to the southeast, placing it in a remote and dangerous stretch of the southern Mojave.
topic_desc_basic: The Old Nuclear Test Site is a location in the Mojave Wasteland, situated between Caesar's Legion Safehouse and the Crashed Vertibird. It served as a pre-War nuclear weapon test range and waste disposal area, leaving the entire vicinity saturated with persistent radiation. The site is mostly fenced off but contains an enterable Nuclear Test Shack. Feral Ghoul Reavers and Glowing Ones inhabit the compound, while feral ghouls roam the surrounding hills. Radiation levels near the shack can reach nine rads per second.

topic_desc: The El Rey Motel stands as a grim counterpart to Novac's Dino Dee-lite, sharing a similar architectural layout but suffering from far greater decay. Its remaining inhabitants are predominantly destitute chem addicts, reflecting the poverty and desperation common in the Freeside outskirts. The motel's structural deterioration has rendered most of its rooms inaccessible, blocked by accumulated debris. The few rooms that remain reachable tell fragmentary stories of the wasteland's harsh economy: one ground-floor room belonged to an individual who borrowed money from a loan shark and failed to repay it, a fate underscored by a threatening note left on the table. That same room is now occupied by Bark Scorpions and a dead wastelander. The top floor holds two rooms behind very easy locks, one housing a hostile crazed chem addict and the other containing another dead wastelander. The motel gained a measure of notoriety when it appeared during the opening sequence of wasteland records depicting an NCR Veteran Ranger firing from the Fabulous New Vegas sign at a Fiend positioned near the motel.
topic_desc_basic: The El Rey Motel is a dilapidated motel in the Mojave Wasteland, located south of Freeside and directly west of Camp McCarran. Similar in appearance to the Dino Dee-lite Motel in Novac, the El Rey is far more run-down and populated largely by destitute chem addicts. Most room doors are blocked by debris and inaccessible. A few rooms can be entered, including one on the bottom floor infested with Bark Scorpions and two on the top floor behind locked doors.
tags: bark scorpions,camp mccarran vicinity,chem addicts,dilapidated motel,freeside outskirts,loan shark victim

topic_desc: The Searchlight Airport represents a remnant of pre-War aviation infrastructure in the southeastern Mojave Wasteland, situated directly south of Camp Searchlight. The facility's layout includes one runway aligned along the north-south axis and two additional east-to-west runways, alongside a control tower with an empty, inaccessible interior and a main terminal building. A reinforced tunnel runs beneath the runways, parallel to Highway 95, though the only entrance is a collapsed tunnel on the northern side. The grounds are crawling with Radscorpions of varying sizes, making the site hazardous to explore. Four rusted jet planes remain scattered across the area, two of which have their landing gear trapped in junk piles but are otherwise intact. Fuel and non-descript holding tanks sit east of the main building. Two trunks on the west side of the terminal have been known to contain significant quantities of bottle caps, and ammunition boxes beneath the westernmost jet plane sometimes hold energy weapons, ammunition, and missiles, suggesting the airport may have been used for military supply transport before the War.
topic_desc_basic: The Searchlight Airport is a pre-War airport in the southeastern Mojave Wasteland, directly south of Camp Searchlight. Its only entrance is a collapsed tunnel on its northern side. The facility features one north-south runway, two east-west runways, a control tower, and a main terminal building. The airport is overrun with Radscorpions of various sizes. Four rusted jet planes remain on the grounds, two with landing gear stuck in junk piles. No buildings are accessible.
tags: camp searchlight south,collapsed tunnel entrance,pre-war airport,radscorpion infestation,rusted jet planes,southeastern mojave

topic_desc: Crescent Canyon East forms the eastern approach to a large crescent-moon-shaped canyon that, together with Crescent Canyon West, creates a natural barrier along the southern edge of the Mojave Wasteland. The canyon lies below a collapsed bridge south of Mojave Drive-in. A train hangs precariously over the canyon from the roadway above, with some of its cars having come to rest at the canyon floor. The area is irradiated at approximately four rads per second, a contamination likely stemming from the radioactive waste barrels scattered throughout the gully. Golden Geckos populate the canyon, drawn to or sustained by the irradiated environment. An overturned truck roughly halfway through the canyon marks the location of an Advanced Radiation Suit stored in a marked case, providing some relief for those traversing the area. An armor case nearby may contain combat armor or a combat helmet. At the east end of the canyon, a Hollowed-Out Rock sits at the bottom of the hill to the right. The railroad tracks do not continue beyond the train car on the north side, where the road transitions into a normal street.
topic_desc_basic: Crescent Canyon East is the eastern entrance to a crescent-moon-shaped gully below a collapsed bridge south of Mojave Drive-in in the Mojave Wasteland. It connects with Crescent Canyon West to form a natural barrier along the southern end of the map. The canyon is populated by Golden Geckos and strewn with radioactive waste barrels. Radiation levels reach four rads per second throughout the canyon.
